papers.title: Unimodal Singularities of Parametrized Space Curves
papers.abstract: The aim of the article is to classify unimodal parametrized space curve singularities defined over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$. We provide explicit normal forms of parametrizations up to $\mathcal A$-equivalence. The parametrizations are given by convergent power series over a real valued field, which includes parametrizations given by formal power series and by, for example, convergent power series over the complex numbers or the field of Puisieux series. The list of normal forms is surprisingly simple.

papers.title: Positive Codegree Density of Suspensions of Graphs
papers.abstract: We determine the exact positive codegree density of suspensions of graphs $S^r(G)$ when $χ(G)=t$ and $t-2$ is prime power. The value is $γ^+(S^{r}(G)) = \frac{(t-3)(t-2)^{r-1}}{(t-2)^r-1}$. The case of suspensions of $K_4$ gives the positive codegree density of daisies, answering a question of Balogh, Halfpap, Lidický and Palmer. The lower bound construction is from Ellis, Ivan and Leader, while we establish the corresponding upper bound based on a weighted graph inequality.

papers.title: $5I(K_X+Δ)$ is very ample on stable log surfaces
papers.abstract: We prove that Bombieri's bound for canonical models of surfaces of general type extends to stable log surfaces, that is, $mI(K_X+Δ)$ is very ample for every $m\geq 5$ and every stable log surface $(X,Δ)$ over $\mathbb{C}$ with reduced boundary and global Cartier index $I$. On the way to this result we determine the cases where $|3I(K_X+Δ)|$ has base points.

papers.title: Cluster-theoretic Newton--Okounkov polytopes of flag varieties of types $A_4$ and $B_2$
papers.abstract: Newton--Okounkov bodies have been used for studying toric degenerations of flag varieties. We classify the Newton--Okounkov polytopes associated with cluster valuations and the anticanonical line bundle on full flag varieties of types $A_4$ and $B_2$. In type $A_4$, the $672$ seeds of cluster type $D_6$ yield $162$ affine unimodular equivalence classes, which coincide with the combinatorial equivalence classes. We determine the subgroup of exchange-graph automorphisms preserving every polytope class. It is a Klein four group of index six in the automorphism group of the exchange graph of cluster type $D_6$. In type $B_2$, we give defining inequalities for all six seeds. At the anticanonical weight, the two combinatorial equivalence classes split into three affine unimodular equivalence classes. Their respective class-preserving automorphism groups have orders four and two.

papers.title: The unavoidable minor in graphs of uncountable edge-connectivity
papers.abstract: For any given uncountable cardinal $κ$, we show that every $κ$-edge-connected graph admits a minor embedding of the graph $T_κ\star1$ (the $κ$-regular tree with a new apex vertex adjacent to all its nodes), which is itself $κ$-edge-connected. This extends a previous result of Kurkofka regarding unavoidable minors of $\aleph_0$-edge-connected graphs to all uncountable cardinalities $κ$.

papers.title: Edge-coloring spectra of odd-fold graph covers and counterexamples to a conjecture
papers.abstract: For a loopless multigraph $G$ and an odd integer $\ell\ge3$, let $Δ(G)$ be the maximum degree of $G$, let $s_\ell(G)$ be the minimum chromatic index of a cyclic $\ell$-fold cover of $G$, and let \begin{align*} L_\ell(G):=\max\left\{ Δ(G),\ \max_{\substack{S\subseteq V(G)\\ |S|\ge3\text{ odd}}} \left\lceil\frac{2\ell|E(G[S])|}{\ell|S|-1}\right\rceil \right\}. \end{align*} In this paper, we prove the sharp upper bound \begin{align*} s_\ell(G)\le\max\{Δ(G)+1,L_\ell(G)\}. \end{align*} For every nonempty bridgeless cubic graph $H$, we construct two $3\ell$-regular graphs, one a multigraph and the other a simple graph. In each case, the minimum chromatic indices over cyclic and over all $\ell$-fold covers both equal the chromatic index of the multigraph obtained by replacing each edge of $H$ with $\ell$ parallel edges. Taking $H$ to be the Petersen graph gives both multigraph and simple graph counterexamples to a conjecture of Chen, van der Holst, Luo, and Ma, which asserts that $s_\ell(G)=L_\ell(G)$ always holds. When $G$ is connected and $L_\ell(G)>Δ(G)$, we determine the common spectrum of its connected cyclic and arbitrary $\ell$-fold covers. We give polynomial-time algorithms to compute $L_\ell(G)$ and the spectrum endpoints. For fixed $\ell$, we also construct in polynomial time a connected cyclic cover with any prescribed chromatic index in the spectrum.

papers.title: The Optimal Constant for One-Shot Channel Simulation and Strong Functional Representation Lemma
papers.abstract: We prove a tight bound for one-shot channel simulation via a stronger version of the strong functional representation lemma: for any random variables $X,Y$, there exists a random variable $Z$ with $I(Z;X)=H(Y|X,Z)=0$ and $H(Y|Z)\le I+\log I+(1-γ)\log e-\log\log e+O(I^{-1}\log I)$, where $I=I(X;Y)$ and $γ$ is the Euler-Mascheroni constant. A more convenient bound is $H(Y|Z)<I+\log(I+2)+1$. The first bound is notable in the sense that the constant term $(1-γ)\log e-\log\log e$ is optimal, and cannot be improved for any bound stated only in terms of $I$. Hence, this is the tightest form of the strong functional representation lemma up to the third order. We also prove that the Poisson functional representation is almost optimal up to a constant gap, and provide a simple finite-blocklength achievability bound that implies the $(1/2)\log n$ redundancy of the simulation of memoryless non-singular channel. These are proved via a generalization of the functional information, in particular, the exponential functional information, which closely approximates the cost of one-shot channel simulation.

papers.title: Pre-Model Structures on the Category of $C_p$-Sets
papers.abstract: It is a folk theorem of Goodwillie that there are exactly 9 model structures on the category of sets, coming from 18 pre-model structures. We investigate model structures and pre-model structures on the category of $G$-sets for a finite group $G$. We outline a strategy for finding all model structures in this category, and partially execute this strategy for the case of $C_p$-sets, where $C_p$ denotes a cyclic group of prime order $p$. In particular, there are exactly 1777 pre-model structures on the category of $C_p$-sets.
papers.comments: Comments welcome! Accompanying code can be found at https://github.com/diracdeltafunk/model-structures-GSet

papers.title: Product Asymptotics for Rows of the Walsh Table on Regular Compact Sets
papers.abstract: Let $E$ be a regular compact set with connected complement, and let $f$ be holomorphic in a neighborhood of $E$. We establish Hadamard-type asymptotic formulas for products of errors of best uniform rational approximation of $f$ on $E$, formed from the first $m+1$ rows of the Walsh table. When the corresponding meromorphy radii are finite, we also show that the extremal exponential rates of the approximation errors along these rows are attained along a common subsequence. We also prove a sharp asymptotic comparison theorem for ratios of best rational approximation errors along fixed rows of the Walsh table on $E$ and its closed Green sublevel sets, and derive corresponding sharp asymptotic estimates for ratios of their products. These results extend earlier product theorems from continua with connected complement and Jordan boundary to the more general setting of regular compact sets with connected complement.

papers.title: Hamilton cycles in vertex-transitive graphs of prime-power order
papers.abstract: A graph is vertex-transitive if, for any two vertices, there is an automorphism mapping one to the other. We prove that every connected vertex-transitive graph of order $p^n$, where $p$ is a prime and $p^n\geq 3$, has a hamiltonian cycle. Our main tool extends Witte's theorem [JCTB (1986)] on Cayley digraphs of $p$-groups.

papers.title: Local Periodic Orbit Penetration in Dynamical Systems
papers.abstract: We introduce two complementary frameworks for studying local periodicity and recurrence in dynamical systems. In the topological setting, we consider continuous maps with nonempty periodic-point sets, restricted to the closures of their periodic points. We define the periodic penetration time of an open set as the least period of a periodic point it contains. Using dynamically refined finite generating covers, we construct asymptotic mean and variance invariants that describe local periodic penetration relative to the logarithms of minimum subcover cardinalities. We establish their invariance under topological conjugacy and investigate their behavior for finite periodic systems, full shifts, shifts of finite type, and zero-entropy systems with dense periodic points. We also extend the construction to invertible systems using symmetric dynamical refinements. In the measure theoretic setting, we define local return times through positive measure intersections of measurable sets with their iterated preimages. Using dynamically refined finite generating partitions, we construct corresponding asymptotic mean and variance invariants and establish their invariance under measure-theoretic isomorphism. We derive explicit formulas for finite probability-preserving systems and study finite periodic approximations of uniform Bernoulli shifts on $q\geq 2$ symbols, proving that their system-level mean and variance invariants converge to $1/\log q$ and $0$, respectively. Our results demonstrate that local periodic penetration and return-time statistics provide information about dynamical systems beyond that captured by classical entropy.

papers.title: The Isomorphism Problem for Cayley Graphs on Monogenic Semigroups
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the structural properties of Cayley graphs of monogenic semigroups and present a complete characterization of their weakly connected components. Several essential properties of these components are rigorously proven. Building upon these structural results, we introduce the notion of labelled colour-permuting isomorphisms between Cayley graphs. Using this new isomorphism framework, we address the Cayley graph isomorphism problem for monogenic semigroups, commonly known as the CI problem. In particular, we establish the necessary and sufficient conditions under which two Cayley graphs over monogenic semigroups are labelled colour-permuting isomorphic.

papers.title: Neumann Series of Bessel Functions for a Quadratic Sturm--Liouville Pencil
papers.abstract: We construct Neumann series of Bessel functions representations for solutions and their first derivatives of the equation $-y^{\prime\prime}(x)+(q(x)+2ρp(x))y(x)=ρ^2y(x)$. The series arise from Legendre expansions of two transmutation operator kernels. The obtained series converge uniformly on horizontal strips in the complex plane of the parameter $ρ$. We develop a recursive integration procedure for computing the coefficients of these representations. The knowledge of the first coefficients allows one to recover the potentials $p$ and $q$ which is useful for solving inverse problems. For separated boundary conditions, we estimate the characteristic functions whose zeros determine the eigenvalues. Two numerical examples illustrate the practical applicability of the obtained series representations to the solution of spectral problems.

papers.title: Minimal dynamics with polynomial and intermediate complexity
papers.abstract: We study how complicated the orbits of a minimal system can be when the topological entropy vanishes, by looking at the exact order of growth of the number of distinguishable orbit segments, and not only at its exponent. For a broad class of growth rates, including all polynomial ones, we construct minimal homeomorphisms of one-dimensional continua realizing them; in particular, two such systems may have the same polynomial entropy and yet incomparable growth. We also show that passing from a minimal subshift to the maps obtained by running its suspension flow for a fixed time only rescales time in the growth law, and we characterize exactly when this rescaling has no effect. Combined with a construction of Cassaigne, this yields minimal homeomorphisms of continua whose growth lies strictly between all polynomial and all exponential rates.

papers.title: Boundary-controlled irreversible port--Hamiltonian modeling and structure-preserving discretization of tubular reactors
papers.abstract: This paper presents a boundary-controlled irreversible port-Hamiltonian model and a structure-preserving spatial discretization for a non-isothermal tubular reactor with axial convection, variable-density momentum dynamics, chemical reaction, mass diffusion, heat conduction, and jacket heat transfer. Reaction, diffusion, and heat conduction are described by irreversible port-Hamiltonian channels, whereas convection and momentum are represented by a weighted Eulerian interconnection. The boundary ports recover the axial energy flux and the corresponding entropy flux. A partitioned finite-element method is then formulated in conservative coordinates using a power-preserving change of variables. The semi-discrete model satisfies the Hamiltonian balance and a discrete entropy balance with non-negative entropy production due to reaction, diffusion, heat conduction, and jacket heat transfer. Numerical results for an open tubular reactor are validated against independently computed continuous steady boundary-value solutions and show the transient temperature, composition, and velocity profiles in the very-low-Mach regime. The same discretization is also tested with reciprocal Soret--Dufour coupling, for which the discrete entropy production remains non-negative.

papers.title: Gromov-Witten Nonvanishing and Symplectic Deformations of Toric Varieties
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be nonzero in the cohomology ring of a smooth projective toric variety $X$. In this note, we observe the existence of a nonzero Gromov-Witten invariant of the form $\langle A, A, \ldots\rangle_{0, n,β}^X$ as a consequence of Iritani's work on the big quantum cohomology ring of $X$. This implies Kollár's conjecture on the symplectic deformation invariance of rational connectedness in the case where $X$ is toric. If $X$ is moreover Fano and $B$ is also nonzero in the cohomology ring, we prove the existence of a nonzero Gromov-Witten invariant of the form $\langle A,B,*\rangle_{0,3,β}^X$ using Batyrev's presentation of the small quantum cohomology ring of $X$. We conclude with a few consequences of this nonvanishing result.

papers.title: Ostrik's Theorem for Operator Algebras in a Unitary Tensor Category
papers.abstract: We define Hilbert modules for $\mathrm{C^*}$ and $\mathrm{W^*}$ algebra objects in the ind-completion of a unitary tensor category. We then prove an operator algebraic Ostrik's theorem in an ind-category: the 2-category of $\mathrm{C^*}$ or $\mathrm{W^*}$ algebras objects, their modules, and adjointable intertwiners is $\dagger$-equivalent to the 2-categories of $\mathrm{C^*}$ or $\mathrm{W^*}$ module categories.
papers.comments: 24 pages, many figures. No LLM's were used at any stage during this project. Comments welcome!

papers.title: Bi-parameter local linearization and parameter estimation for the damped stochastic Klein--Gordon equation with spatially colored noise
papers.abstract: Consider the one-dimensional nonlinear damped stochastic Klein--Gordon equation driven by Gaussian noise that is white in time and fractional in space, with Hurst parameter $H\in(1/2,1)$. For a globally Lipschitz diffusion coefficient, we approximate characteristic mixed increments by those of the additive equation, multiplied by the coefficient frozen at the base point. A critical-kernel reduction and localized Riesz covariance estimates control the additional kernel terms and spatial correlations. We also establish $L^p$ error bounds for normalized quadratic variations and, under a nondegeneracy condition, construct jointly strongly consistent estimators of the Hurst parameter and a positive diffusion parameter.

papers.title: Minimum Synthesis Time for Single-Deletion Correcting Codes of Prescribed Size
papers.abstract: DNA is a promising medium for data storage, but the high cost of DNA synthesis remains a major obstacle to its widespread deployment. In the reference-based synthesis model, synthesis time is measured by the length of the reference sequence. Previous studies have analyzed code sizes under synthesis-time constraints and constructed cost-constrained codes, including codes that correct deletions. In this paper, we study the minimum synthesis time for codes of prescribed size, considering both unrestricted codes and single-deletion correcting codes. We establish finite-length lower bounds valid for arbitrary reference sequences and upper bounds using existing $q$-ary differential VT codes. For fixed $q\geq3$, $A>0$, and $R\in(0,1)$, we determine the minimum synthesis time up to an $O(1)$ term when the code size is $M_n=\lfloor Aq^{Rn}\rfloor$. The corresponding redundancy is $(1-R)n\log_2q-\log_2A+o(1)$ bits. In particular, for these code sizes, the minimum synthesis time for single-deletion correcting codes exceeds that for unrestricted codes by a term proportional to $\ln n$, and we determine its coefficient. We also derive upper and lower bounds for code sizes $\lfloor q^n/(nq^{s_n})\rfloor$, where $s_n\to\infty$ and $s_n=o(n)$. These sizes correspond to redundancy $\log_2 n+s_n\log_2q+o(1)$ bits. For code sizes $\lfloor q^n/(nq^c)\rfloor$ with fixed constant $c$, the redundancy is $\log_2 n+c\log_2q+o(1)$ bits. We give conditions under which single-deletion correcting codes exist or do not exist for all sufficiently large $n$, together with bounds on the minimum synthesis time. These results show how code size and the single-deletion correcting constraint affect synthesis time and provide theoretical guidance for the construction of cost-constrained codes.

papers.title: A uniqueness theorem for Allen--Cahn global minimizers asymptotic to the Simons cone
papers.abstract: For every integer $m\ge4$, we prove that the saddle-shaped solution of the Allen--Cahn equation in $\R^{2m}$ constructed by Cabré and Terra \cite{CabreTerra2009} is a global minimizer. Moreover, up to sign, it is the unique global minimizer whose nodal set at infinity is a normal graph over the Simons cone with a height that decays faster than that of the Hardt--Simon leaves.

papers.title: Claw-free minimal bricks
papers.abstract: A graph $G$ is called a \emph{brick} if it is $3$-connected and $G-\{u,v\}$ has a perfect matching for every pair of distinct vertices $u,v\in V(G)$. A brick is \emph{minimal} if deleting any edge results in a graph that is no longer a brick. A graph is \emph{claw-free} if it contains no induced $K_{1,3}$. Plummer proved that every $3$-connected claw-free graph of even order is a brick. In this paper, we completely characterize all claw-free minimal bricks. Apart from $K_4$ and the six-vertex wheel $W_5$, they are precisely the line graphs of graphs obtained from loopless $3$-edge-connected cubic multigraphs by subdividing every edge outside a matching of even size exactly once. Consequently, every claw-free minimal brick of order $n$ contains at least $4n/5$ cubic vertices and at least $4n/5$ edges joining cubic vertices. Both bounds are sharp. This establishes the conjectures of Norine and Thomas and of Lovász for claw-free minimal bricks in sharp quantitative forms. We also show that, for a claw-free minimal brick of order at least $8$, deleting an edge leaves a matching covered graph if and only if the edge lies in a triangle.

papers.title: Genus zero simple knots
papers.abstract: We classify the simple knots in lens spaces with planar rational Seifert surfaces. As a consequence, we classify the homology classes of all knots in lens spaces that admit planar rational Seifert surfaces.

papers.title: Regularity Estimates for a Nonhomogeneous Free Boundary Interface Problem
papers.abstract: In this work, we establish regularity properties for minimizers of a novel nonhomogeneous interface problem with a free boundary, formulated in Orlicz-Sobolev spaces. The nonlinear terms fulfill Lieberman-type structural assumptions with subcritical growth. The principal difficulties stem from the nonhomogeneous framework and the lack of suitable representation formulas. Our findings extend recent contributions in the field and provide new insights even in the particular case of the Laplacian. Keywords: Free Boundary Problems; Orlicz-Spaces; Nonhomogeneous Operator; Transmission Problem; Regularity.

papers.title: G-radical-square-zero algebras
papers.abstract: In this paper, we first provide necessary and sufficient conditions for a Krull-Schmidt triangulated category with Auslander-Reiten triangles to have square-zero radical. One of these conditions is that the middle term of every Auslander-Reiten triangle is either zero or indecomposable. We then call an artin algebra {\it G-radical-square-zero} if the stable category of Gorenstein-projective modules has square-zero radical. We characterize when a G-radical-square-zero algebra is CM-finite and, in this case, give an additive generator of the stable category. For certain Iwanaga-Gorenstein G-radical-square-zero algebras, we further show that the stable category admits an additive generator consisting of higher syzygies of simple modules.

papers.title: Differential Monodromy, $q$-Opers, and Universal $(G,q)$-Wronskians
papers.abstract: We give a geometric formulation of the $q$DE/ODE/IM correspondence for families of differential operators associated with simple Lie algebras of ADE type. Under analytic hypotheses, the $q$-connection associated with shifted monodromy defines a twisted $(G,q)$-oper and has Steinberg form in the frame of solutions normalized by prescribed asymptotics in a sector at infinity. We identify the central connection between the normalized solution frames at zero and infinity with a universal meromorphic $(G,q)$-Wronskian. Its generalized minors give $Q$-functions satisfying the ADE $QQ$-relations. When $q$ is not a root of unity, we parametrize shifted monodromy by quantum-affine $q$-characters evaluated on shifted $Q$-ratios, using the same character formulas that describe normalized transfer-matrix eigenvalues. We verify the analytic hypotheses for generic untwisted Feigin--Frenkel--Hernandez affine opers, thereby relating these affine opers to twisted $(G,q)$-opers.

papers.title: Complete Decentralization of Wave Equation Control on a Compact Domain
papers.abstract: A feedback control policy is completely decentralized if the actuation signal at each location in space can be computed based only on state information from that location. For systems equipped with large numbers of spatially distributed sensors and actuators, completely decentralized controllers are desirable since they can be implemented in a communication and computation efficient manner, but generally perform worse than centralized counterparts. However, through a case study of Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) design for wave dynamics on a compact spatial domain, we show that careful design of system parameters to satisfy certain conditions causes a decentralized control policy to perform as well as any centralized policy. We then propose a spatially filtered $H_2$ norm to show that satisfying these conditions does not inherently degrade achievable closed-loop system performance, enabling simultaneous realization of both desirable performance and communication/computation efficiency via system-control co-design. Additional robustness analysis characterizes a range of system parameters such that the system interconnected with a decentralized controller maintains stability and near-optimal performance. Although our framework is derived for spatially continuous dynamics, we demonstrate that this theory can be leveraged to derive results for decentralization in finite-dimensional settings through a damped mass-spring example.
papers.comments: 25 pages, 6 figures, submitted to SIAM Journal on Control and Optimization

papers.title: Divisibility graphs of semigroups as weighted poset blow-ups
papers.abstract: We develop a structural theory of divisibility graphs of arbitrary semigroups. For a semigroup $S$, let $S/{\mathcal J}$ be the poset of Green's ${\mathcal J}$-classes ordered by inclusion of principal ideals,and equip each $\mathcal {J}$-class $J$ with the weight $|J|$. We prove that the divisibility graph ${\operatorname{Div}}(S)$ is obtained from the comparability directed graph $Comp(S/{\mathcal J})$ by replacing each $\mathcal J$-class with a complete symmetric graph of order $|J|$ and by replacing each directed edge $J_u$ to $J_v$ in $Comp(S/{\mathcal J})$ with all directed edges from every element of $J_u$ to every element of $J_v$. Consequently, ${\operatorname{Div}}(S)$ is determined, up to isomorphism, by the weighted poset $(S/\mathcal {J},\{ J \}_{J\in S/{\mathcal J}})$. This yields structural descriptions of its strongly connected components, maximal unilaterally connected subgraphs. The main contribution is the reduction of divisibility graph problems to weighted quotient-poset problems. As applications, we obtain reconstruction and isomorphism criteria and prove an inheritance theorem for divisibility $D$-saturated subsemigroups.

papers.title: Surface subgroups with prescribed finite quotients
papers.abstract: We prove that every finite quotient of a finite covolume Kleinian group $G$ can be realized by a surface subgroup. More precisely, given an epimorphism from $G$ onto a finite group $F$, there exists a surface subgroup that maps surjectively onto $F$. As a consequence, the union of the surface subgroups is dense in $G$ with respect to the profinite topology. We also apply this result to obtain more examples of atoroidal surface bundles with signature zero in the construction of Kent--Leininger.

papers.title: Bounding the security of the Bromberg-Shpilrain-Vdovina hash function
papers.abstract: The Bromberg-Shpilrain-Vdovina hash functions are a family of Cayley hash functions indexed by an integer parameter $k\ge 2$. Hashes are matrices in $SL_2(p)$ where $p$ is a large prime. We present an attack which finds collisions of length $O(\log p)$ whose average-case time complexity is $O(p^{0.28})$ when $k=2$ and $O(p^{0.36})$ when $k=3$ under an assumption in the spirit of Zaremba's Conjecture on continued fractions. This is an improvement on the more general attacks of Mullan-Tsaban and Slaughter which have average-case time complexity $O(\sqrt{p})$. For any $k$, the average-case time complexity of our attack is $O(p^{1-δ_k+o(1)})$ where $δ_k$ is the Hausdorff dimension of a certain Cantor set. This tends to $O(\sqrt{p})$ as $k\to\infty$, so our attack has time complexity comparable to Mullan-Tsaban and Slaughter's attacks as $k$ grows. We give examples of collisions for large primes found by our attack when $k=2, 3$.

papers.title: A proof of the constant-width numerical range conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the conjecture of Chien, Nakazato, and Meng that the numerical range of a finite complex matrix has constant width $d$ if and only if it is a closed disk of radius $d/2$, with a singleton allowed when $d=0$. For $d>0$, the characteristic polynomial of the associated Hermitian pencil and its translate by $d$ have a nonconstant common divisor over $\mathbb{C}(ζ)$. At points on the unit circle where the factorization can be evaluated, every root of the common divisor equals the smallest eigenvalue. A coefficient of the divisor thus gives a rational formula for that eigenvalue. The characteristic equation forces this rational function to be a Laurent polynomial with exponents in $\{-1,0,1\}$. Antipodal symmetry then makes the midpoint of the extreme eigenvalues a first harmonic, giving the support function of a disk. We also obtain the corresponding quadratic factor of the Kippenhahn polynomial.

papers.title: Weak convergence orders for a fully discrete approximation of semilinear stochastic PDEs driven by multiplicative Gaussian and Poisson noise
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the weak convergence of a fully discrete approximation for a class of semilinear stochastic partial differential equations (SPDEs) driven by multiplicative Gaussian and Poisson noise. The scheme combines a spectral Galerkin discretization in space with an exponential Euler discretization in time. Compared with single-noise settings, the simultaneous presence of continuous and jump perturbations introduces additional challenges arising from discontinuous trajectories, nonlocal jump operators, and their interaction with state-dependent multiplicative coefficients. To overcome these difficulties, we establish the exponential integrability of the numerical solution processes and refined moment estimates in negative Sobolev norms for the associated first- and second-order variational processes. Combining these estimates with a discrete-time approximation argument and Wiener--Poisson Malliavin calculus, we derive regularity estimates for the solutions of the Kolmogorov equations associated with the spatial Galerkin approximations. Based on these estimates, we obtain the temporal and spatial weak convergence orders arbitrarily close to one with respect to discretization parameters $τ$ and $λ_N^{-1}$, respectively. To the best of our knowledge, this provides the first weak convergence result for a fully discrete approximation of semilinear SPDEs with simultaneous multiplicative Gaussian and Poisson noise.

papers.title: A cyclotomic Artin-Tate formula and sphere packing for K3 surfaces
papers.abstract: We give new necessary conditions on the Weil polynomial of a K3 surface over a finite field using techniques from the theory of sphere packing. By comparing the Artin-Tate formula over a finite extension, we derive a special values formula at roots of unity that involves the discriminant of the Frobenius coinvariant lattice. Known bounds on the minimum discriminants of even rootless lattices then imply nontrivial lower bounds on these special values. Applying these new conditions to Kedlaya and Sutherland's list of candidate Weil polynomials of K3 surfaces over the field with 2 elements rules out over 50% of the candidates.

papers.title: Fragment-Free Constraint Programming for the Preemptive Flexible Job Shop Scheduling Problem
papers.abstract: This article addresses the preemptive flexible job shop scheduling problem with makespan minimization (FJm | pmtn | C_max). We propose an exact constraint programming approach that completely avoids representing the processing fragments of an operation. Operations are placed in flexible time windows, where Horn's workload condition guarantees feasible preemptive scheduling, and Jackson's preemptive earliest-deadline-first rule reconstructs exact processing segments post-optimization in O(n log n) time per machine. To manage undecided machine assignments, we extend the PreemptiveNoOverlap global constraint to optional intervals within IBM ILOG CP Optimizer, performing overload checking and preemptive edge-finding in O(n log n) time while eliminating infeasible machine alternatives. The CP model is warm-started using a multi-round MILP assignment relaxation with Carlier's head-tail bounds and a window-based greedy heuristic. Extensive computational experiments on 276 pFJSSP benchmark instances and 78 pJSSP instances demonstrate that the proposed method significantly advances the state of the art. Within a 600~s time limit, it improves the upper bounds of the previously published logic-based Benders decomposition by 3.6% on average, increases the number of proven optimal pFJSSP instances from 102 to 180, and closes 74 instances for the first time (including the entire Barnes family). On the pJSSP under identical hardware conditions, it proves 67 of 78 instances optimal (compared to 51 by the baseline solver Mistral) and closes 9 of the 11 long-standing open problems.

papers.title: Half-inverse problems for perturbed Bessel operators with a known left-hand potential
papers.abstract: For the regular Sturm-Liouville operator $-\frac{{\rm d}^2}{{\rm d}x^2}+q$ acting in $L^2(0,1)$, the Hochstadt-Lieberman theorem states that one full spectrum together with the potential on either the left half-interval $q|_{(0,1/2)}$ or the right half-interval $q|_{(1/2,1)}$ uniquely determines the full potential $q$. The inverse-square singular term $\tfrac{l(l+1)}{x^2}$ in the perturbed Bessel operator $-\frac{{\rm d}^2}{{\rm d}x^2}+\frac{l(l+1)}{x^2}+q$, acting in $L^2(0,1)$, breaks the left-right symmetry. It is known that, when the right half of the potential $q|_{(1/2,1)}$ is given, the uniqueness of the potential can be established even if a finite number of eigenvalues (depending on $l$) are omitted. In this paper we study the opposite setting--where the left half potential $q|_{(0,1/2)}$ is known--and show that one full spectrum together with finitely many norming constants uniquely determine the full potential $q$. Moreover, we specify the minimum number of norming constants required for the uniqueness. Finally, for positive integer $l$, $L^2$ potentials, and the Dirichlet boundary condition at $x = 1$, we establish the local bi-Lipschitz stability and the local solvability from the full spectrum and finitely many norming constants, assuming the potential on the left half-interval is fixed.

papers.title: Log-Concavity in Narayana Transforms and Stack-Sorting Fibers
papers.abstract: Given a permutation $π$ of size $n$, let $D_π(x)$ denote the descent polynomial of the fiber of $π$ under West's stack-sorting map. We prove that $D_π(x)$ is ultra-log-concave of order $n-1$ and, therefore, log-concave. More generally, we prove that a multivariate refinement of $D_π(x)$ recording ascent tops and descent tops is the basis generating polynomial of a laminar matroid. We deduce a result about simplex integration from Brändén and Huh's theory and apply it to weighted matchings, obtaining a refinement of the log-concavity of $D_π(x)$ that incorporates the peak statistic on the stack-sorting fiber of $π$. These results imply the log-concavity of certain sums of products of Narayana polynomials over the lattice points of integral binary nestohedra. A complementary argument shows that replacing the monomials of a homogeneous real-stable polynomial with nonnegative coefficients by products of shifted Narayana polynomials produces a real-rooted polynomial; we discuss several applications. The results in this paper were formalized in Lean by AxiomProver.

papers.title: Euclidean Hulls of Double Cyclic Codes of Arbitrary Block Lengths
papers.abstract: Gao et al. \cite{GWF23} recently explored the Euclidean hulls of double cyclic codes over $\mathbb{Z}_2$. While they found answers for non-separable codes with coprime lengths ($\gcd(r, s) = 1$), the non-coprime case ($\gcd(r, s) > 1$) remained an open question. This paper completely solves that problem for all possible block lengths. We calculate the exact generator polynomials for the hull and show the precise conditions needed for a non-separable code to turn into a separable one. Using this, we show how to construct non-separable LCD codes. We also include several numerical examples to confirm our findings.

papers.title: On the two-component $b$-family system modeling shallow-water waves of medium amplitude
papers.abstract: We formally derive a two-component $b$-family system from the full governing equations for two-dimensional water waves in the medium-amplitude regime. The system contains higher-order nonlinearities and includes a two-component Camassa-Holm type system for equatorial shallow-water waves with the Coriolis effect as a special case. We establish the local well-posedness of the Cauchy problem in $B^{s-1}_{p,r}\times B^s_{p,r}$ with $s>\max\{1+\frac1p,\frac32\}$. Using Littlewood-Paley theory and Osgood's lemma, we also prove local well-posedness in the critical Besov space $B^{\frac12}_{2,1}\times B^{\frac32}_{2,1}$. Furthermore, we derive a blow-up criterion for strong solutions. For a special choice of the parameters, we prove finite-time blow-up for a class of initial data and provide an upper bound for the maximal existence time.

papers.title: The Largest Ground Set for Sunflower-Free Systems
papers.abstract: We construct the largest $r$-flower-free system of $k$-uniform sets for $k=3, r=4$ where every element of the ground set $G$ is used at least once. The goal is to maximize $|G|$, also called the span. We define $\mathrm{sp}(k, r)$ to be the maximum $|G|$ for such a system. We show that $\mathrm{sp}(3, 4) = 39$, which yields an improved upper bound $f(3, 4) \leq 130$, improving upon the Erdős--Rado bound of $f(3, 4) \leq 162$.

papers.title: Failure of endpoint estimates for lacunary bilinear spherical maximal functions on Heisenberg groups
papers.abstract: We prove that the lacunary bilinear Nevo--Thangavelu spherical maximal operator on the Heisenberg group $\mathbb H^n$ does not map $H^1(\mathbb H^n)\times H^1(\mathbb H^n)$ into $L^{1/2,\infty}(\mathbb H^n)$ for any $n\geq1$. We obtain this result by lifting the Euclidean counterexample in our recent result (arXiv:2610.40100) to the Heisenberg group.

papers.title: Banach isomorphism between separable \(L_p\)-spaces, \(1\le p\ne2<\infty\), associated with hyperfinite type III von Neumann algebras
papers.abstract: For each fixed \(p\in[1,\infty)\setminus\{2\}\), the number of Banach isomorphism classes of separable \(L_p\)-spaces associated with hyperfinite type III von Neumann algebras is \(2^{\aleph_0}\).

papers.title: Multiscale LegONet: Learning Coefficient-Dependent Local Spaces for Composable Multiscale Finite Elements with Localized Error Bounds
papers.abstract: We introduce multiscale LegONet (Ms-LegONet), a plug-and-play learned block for heterogeneous elliptic problems. One network per spatial dimension is trained once on local coefficient patches and reused, without retraining, across coefficient layouts, sources, boundary data and domain sizes within the trained coefficient class. On a fixed primitive patch the network maps the local coefficient to a zero-boundary space, the only learned object. The multiscale basis functions are the harmonic extensions of a fixed set of boundary traces, each a Galerkin solve in that space. Shared interface traces enforce continuity, larger blocks are assembled by recursive static condensation without any parent-scale network, and a localized Céa bound attributes the error of the learned spaces primitive by primitive. The training labels are harmonic responses of single patches, so no global solve enters the training. Against MsFEM, GMsFEM, the neural-operator element method and an end-to-end Fourier neural operator, Ms-LegONet is the most accurate at equal unknowns: its $L^2$ error is $4$ to $150$ times below the baselines on two-dimensional mosaics of $256$ high-contrast primitives, and its median error stays within $0.1$ percentage points of that of exact local spaces in three-dimensional layered media. For each new coefficient it is $1.6$ to $2.3$ times faster than a fine-grid direct solve in two dimensions. In three dimensions it computes the many-query port response of a chain $30$ to $900$ times faster than finite element solves on the same or a finer mesh, at a relative error of $10^{-4}$ against their $6\%$ and $1.6\%$.

papers.title: A Fast Proximal-Gradient Algorithm for Decentralised Optimisation
papers.abstract: We consider a connected multi-agent network where agents coordinate to minimise a finite sum of convex functions. Each function in the sum can be further expressed as the sum of a smooth and nonsmooth component and is known only to a single agent in the network. We propose a decentralised proximal-gradient-type algorithm for solving this problem, which we term Fast PG-EXTRA. In each iteration, agents evaluate the gradient of the smooth component of their local objective functions and the proximal operator of the nonsmooth component, followed by communicating the results with neighbouring agents in the network. Fast PG-EXTRA can be viewed as an accelerated variant of PG-EXTRA, in the sense that it enjoys non-ergodic $o(1/k^2)$ convergence rates in terms of the first-order optimality residual, successive iterates, and consensus error, compared to PG-EXTRA's ergodic $O(1/k)$ convergence rates. Our analysis of Fast PG-EXTRA is based on an accelerated variant of the Condat--Vũ algorithm for non-distributed convex minimisation, which has similarly improved convergence rates compared to the Condat--Vũ algorithm. We validate our convergence results for Fast PG-EXTRA and demonstrate its potential advantages compared to PG-EXTRA with numerical experiments for power state system estimation and $l_1$-regularised logistic regression.

papers.title: Gradient regularity without gap conditions for parabolic double phase systems with coefficients depending only on time
papers.abstract: We study degenerate parabolic double phase systems with growth exponents $p<q$ whose modulating coefficient depends only on time. In this case, the operator on each time slice has Orlicz growth with structural constants independent of the coefficient, and the system is invariant under spatial translations. Using these features, we prove second order estimates and local bounds for the gradient when the coefficient is merely bounded and measurable, and $C^{1,α}$ regularity when it is Hölder continuous in time. For weak solutions with gradients in $L^q$, these results hold without any gap condition between $p$ and $q$.

papers.title: Entropy maximization for cube projections
papers.abstract: We prove that, in every dimension $n\ge150$, the one-dimensional projections of the uniform distribution on a cube have the largest differential entropy in directions with equal coordinate magnitudes. This establishes the conjecture of Eskenazis, Nayar, and Tkocz in these dimensions.

papers.title: Covering the Triangular Lattice with Non-Overlapping Unit Disks
papers.abstract: For $d>0$, let $\mathcal{T}_d$ be the triangular lattice with minimum distance $d$. We study for which $d$ the set $\mathcal{T}_d$ can be covered by closed unit disks with pairwise disjoint interiors, a question left open by Phetmak, Nuntasombat and Fakcharoenphol for $2-\sqrt3\le d<2/\sqrt{37}$ and on several gaps between their constructions. Writing $\mathcal{N}(d)$ for the largest number of points of $\mathcal{T}_d$ in a closed unit disk, we show that $\mathcal{T}_d$ cannot be covered whenever $\mathcal{N}(d)<4/d^2$, and we determine this set of spacings exactly as a union of fifteen intervals; combined with their constructions, this shows that coverability is not monotone in $d$. At the right endpoints $d=2/\sqrt k$ of these intervals the density bound is attained, and we show that such a spacing is coverable if and only if $k$ is the norm of an Eisenstein integer. We also give two new coverings, at $d=1/\sqrt{13}$ and $d=2/\sqrt{21}$, in which the disks form a hexagonal packing. Consequently, together with an earlier result of Okayama, Kiyomi and Uehara, the smallest coverable spacing $d_{\min}$ exists and satisfies $2/\sqrt{55}<d_{\min}\le1/\sqrt{13}$, which answers a question of Phetmak, Nuntasombat and Fakcharoenphol.
papers.comments: 29 pages, 7 figures, 5 tables. The ancillary file verify_triangular.py (Python 3 with SymPy, exact arithmetic) carries out all computations used in the proofs

papers.title: Statistical Analysis of the Structure from Noise Phenomenon in Generalized Procrustes Problems
papers.abstract: In cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM), observations are highly noisy, and scientists often use reference templates to guide matching, alignment, and averaging to reconstruct the molecular structure. However, these procedures can produce an output resembling the template even when the observations contain only noise, a phenomenon known as Einstein from noise (EfN). This phenomenon has attracted attention in statistics, where simplified observation models involving group actions have been studied to understand the resulting model bias. Characterizing the bias in the full cryo-EM pipeline remains challenging. We study template matching and averaging in the generalized orthogonal Procrustes problem, which provides an analytically tractable setting involving continuous orthogonal group action and lower-dimensional projections of ordered point clouds. We show that, for pure Gaussian noise, the mean of the aligned-and-averaged estimator admits the same left and right singular-vector bases as the template but its singular values may be distorted. This identifies the subspace structure imposed by the template even in the absence of signal. We characterize the singular values and bound their distortion, establish finite-sample operator-norm bounds, and give sufficient sample sizes for the population mean to dominate random fluctuations. In fact, this bias still exists under weak signals: when the template rank is at least the observation dimension, the change from the pure-noise mean is $O(η^2)$ in signal amplitude $η$. Our results provide an explicit characterization of model bias in a registration problem motivated by cryo-EM and show why averaging more observations can stabilize structure imposed by the template without removing the bias.

papers.title: A Variable-metric Inexact Progressive Hedging Algorithm with a Lagged Stopping Criterion for Multistage Stochastic Variational Inequalities
papers.abstract: The progressive hedging algorithm (PHA) solves multistage stochastic variational inequalities (SVIs) by independently solving regularized scenario subproblems and enforcing nonanticipativity through primal-dual updates. Since these subproblems are often solved iteratively, practical implementations need stopping criteria that control errors while preserving convergence. We propose iVMPHA-Lag, a variable-metric inexact PHA with a lagged stopping criterion for monotone SVIs. The method allows scenario block metrics to vary across outer iterations while remaining compatible with nonanticipativity. For each scenario, an error budget combines a positive fraction of the previous budget with a progress measure from the preceding outer iteration. This gives a stopping tolerance fixed before the inner iterations begin, so each scenario can check its criterion independently without a prescribed summable tolerance sequence. With positive initial budgets and a positive inexactness parameter, we prove finite inner termination provided the inner solver produces valid approximations whose residual and enlargement errors tend to zero. Under suitable conditions, we establish global convergence of the primal-dual iterates and local $R$-linear convergence under metric subregularity at the limit point. Numerical experiments on synthetic strongly monotone box-constrained SVIs show that iVMPHA-Lag with adaptive metrics uses fewer scenario evaluations and less time on average than exact PHA and the competing inexact methods among the tested configurations in all four baseline regimes. Its average time advantage over the competing inexact methods persists across the tested problem sizes. Further comparisons show that metric adaptation improves efficiency over the fixed scalar configuration, while lagged stopping and positive budget retention reduce inner computational work.

papers.title: Adaptive Multi-Fidelity Benders Decomposition for Security-constrained Transmission Expansion Planning
papers.abstract: Energy grids worldwide rely on efficient, effective and resilient transmission networks to deliver power from generators to geographically distant destinations. The optimisation problem of designing these networks is made very difficult by the non-linearity and non-convexity of the equations which govern AC power flow. In this paper we propose the Adaptive Multi-Fidelity Benders Decomposition (AMFBD) algorithm, which is capable of solving to global optimality the Security-Constrained Transmission Expansion Planning problems with N-1 redundancy, using the non-convex AC power flow equations. We demonstrate the practical capability of this algorithm by solving security-constrained expansion problems based on the Garver 6-bus problem and the 14-bus IEEE test case. Given the large costs generally associated with energy grids, globally optimal investment decisions that can be found using AMFBD have the potential to provide significant practical benefits over suboptimal solutions produced by approximations or heuristics.
papers.comments: 33 pages, 4 figures, submitted to INFORMS Journal on Computing

papers.title: Third-Order Asymptotics for Fixed-Length Lossy Compression of Discrete Memoryless Sources
papers.abstract: This paper determines the third-order asymptotics of the logarithm of the minimum codebook size for fixed-length lossy compression of discrete memoryless sources. For an excess-distortion probability constraint $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ and every interior distortion level, we establish a third-order correction of $\frac12\log n+O(1)$, where $n$ is the blocklength. This sharpens the general bounds of Kostina and Verdú [IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory, 2012]. The main technical innovation lies in the converse for positive dispersion. Under a reverse change of measure, we retain the exponential weights associated with tilted information and distortion slack and control them jointly using the multivariate weighted-strip estimate of Scarlett, Martinez, and Guillén i Fàbregas [Proc. IEEE ISIT, 2015]. A pairing argument verifies the required covariance nondegeneracy uniformly over all reconstruction words whose distortion balls meet a typical set, yielding the matching converse.

papers.title: The minimum number of cycles of length $0$ modulo $k$ in graphs with no proper $k$-coloring
papers.abstract: Consider an integer $k\geq 3$. Toft and Tuza observed that every graph with no proper $k$-coloring has a cycle of length $0$ modulo $k$. Brewster, McGuinness, Moore, and Noel conjectured the following quantitative strengthening: every graph with no proper $k$-coloring has at least $\frac{(k+1)!}{2k}$ cycles whose lengths are divisible by $k$. The conjecture is sharp, as demonstrated by the complete graph on $k+1$ vertices. Kim and Picollelli confirmed the conjecture for $k=3$. We establish the conjecture for every $k\geq 3$. In other words, we determine the minimum number of cycles of length $0$ modulo $k$ in a graph with no proper $k$-coloring.

papers.title: On Distinct Powers in Finite Groups
papers.abstract: Sun conjectured that if a group $G$ has no elements of orders $2,3,...,n+1$, then every $n$-element subset $A$ can be ordered as $a_1,...,a_n$ so that $a_1,a_2^2,...,a_n^n$ are pairwise distinct. We prove the conjecture for finite groups when $n=4,5,6$. The proofs combine collision-counting arguments with reductions to finite-field assignment problems; the remaining finite cases for $n=6$ are verified exhaustively. We also prove the conjecture for every $n$ when no four elements of $A$ generate the same cyclic subgroup.

papers.title: Exact (Non-)Accelerations of Heavy-Ball Discretizations
papers.abstract: Momentum methods with the same slow dynamics can have different worst-case rates on smooth strongly convex functions. We identify a half-step phase barrier in the gradient query that governs this difference. For momentum with extrapolation $τ_κ\toτ$, $β=1-θ/\sqrtκ+o(κ^{-1/2})$ and $hL\to y$, where $κ=L/μ$ and $θ,y>0$, the exact uniform distance factor is $1-c/\sqrtκ+o(κ^{-1/2})$, with $c=\min\{θ/3,c_Q(θ,y)\}$, when $τ>1/2$ and $y(1+2τ)<4$; $c_Q$ is the slowest quadratic decay exponent. Quadratically accelerated families with $\limsupτ_κ<1/2$ have divergent trajectories on the full function class. Upper bounds use finite-lag certificates: nonnegative combinations of inequalities for values and gradients at finitely separated query points, together with comparisons to the minimizer. For any prescribed accuracy, spiral mixtures or quadratic trajectories of one finite-dimensional objective give matching lower bounds at all iteration horizons. We resolve the parameter layer near $τ=1/2$ and classify all tunings of this family attaining the optimal leading constant 1. The flow also bounds the leading constant of every second-order stationary linear family with the same slow parameters $(θ,y)$ and fixed finite memory.
papers.comments: 63 pages, 7 figures, link to Lean formalization

papers.title: Maximal Triply Even Binary Codes from Elliptic Orthogonal Graphs
papers.abstract: For a finite set $X$, a binary linear code $C\subseteq\mathbb{F}_2^X$ is called a triply even binary code if $\operatorname{wt}(c)\equiv 0\pmod{8}$ for every $c\in C$. Let $q$ be an odd prime power and $n$ be an integer with $n\ge 2$. Let $E^-_{2n+2}(q)$ denote the binary code spanned by all pairwise sums of rows of the adjacency matrix of the elliptic orthogonal graph arising from a $(2n+2)$-dimensional elliptic quadratic space over $\mathbb{F}_q$. We prove that $E^-_{2n+2}(q)$ is a triply even binary code if and only if $n=2$ and $q\equiv 3\pmod{4}$. In this case, we also prove that $E^-_6(q)$ is a maximal triply even binary code.

papers.title: Two nodally bound-preserving and mass-conservative discontinuous Galerkin methods for reaction-diffusion problems
papers.abstract: We propose and analyze two high-order discontinuous Galerkin methods that preserve prescribed nodal bounds and total mass for reaction-diffusion problems with anisotropic and heterogeneous diffusion. Both methods combine a weighted interior-penalty prediction step with a convex correction in either the dG energy or the $L^2$ metric. We construct a pointwise bound-preserving and cellwise mass-preserving comparison function with optimal local approximation properties. This construction yields optimal dG-energy error estimates for the energy correction and, under a dual regularity assumption, optimal $L^2$ and dG-energy error estimates for the $L^2$ correction on quasi-uniform meshes. We further establish a general a posteriori estimate that combines a predictor estimator with the computable correction norm. The resulting estimators are globally reliable and efficient up to data oscillation, with parameter-dependent efficiency constants. Numerical experiments compare the two corrections and illustrate their use in adaptive computations.

papers.title: Fractional-Order Hybrid SIR Forecasting of COVID-19 in Bangladesh and the United States: Memory Effects and Out-of-Sample Evaluation
papers.abstract: Fractional-order epidemic models are often justified by memory, yet whether memory improves forecasts is rarely tested out of sample. We extend a hybrid SIR framework, in which a daily transmission rate is reconstructed from reported cases and then forecast, to Caputo fractional order $α\in(0,1]$. We prove well-posedness, conservation, positivity and a linearized threshold at disease-free states, and derive a Grünwald-Letnikov reconstruction that reduces exactly to the integer-order one at $α=1$. Our main theoretical result shows that for $α<1$ the influence of the unknown initial infectious count vanishes, but no faster than $t^{-α}$; after 332 daily steps it is about $4.4\times10^{8}$ times larger at $α=0.9$ than at $α=1$. In out-of-sample forecasting over 27 weekly origins, the effect of memory depends on the setting. In Bangladesh the integer order gives the lowest error for linear and constant-rate forecasts in 47 of 48 settings. In the United States, where reported cases reached about 18% of the population, a fractional order lowers the linear forecaster's error in all 12 comparisons in 2021 but raises the constant-rate forecaster's, with no difference significant after Holm adjustment. Against standard baselines, the SIR-based linear forecaster was more accurate than the classical SIR model and a neural network without SIR structure, and competitive with ARIMA: in the United States the fractional linear forecaster had the lowest error of all methods (seven-day MAPE 7.54% against 9.14% for ARIMA), whereas in Bangladesh ARIMA had the lowest MAPE, with no significant difference from ARIMA in either country. The choice of a fractional order should rest on out-of-sample evidence rather than in-sample fit.
papers.comments: 23 pages, 5 figures, 9 tables. Code and data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24057230

papers.title: Nonnegative weak tilings and the Coven-Meyerowitz condition (T2)
papers.abstract: We develop a general method, in finite cyclic groups, for constructing nonnegative rational functions $f$, normalized by $f(0)=1$, that satisfy the Coven-Meyerowitz condition $(T1)$ but fail $(T2)$, such that $f$ is a weak complement for a set tile $A$. Motivated by the unsupported-divisor questions in arXiv:2507.11672, we show that if a set tile $A$ admits an unsupported divisor, then a suitable dilation of $A$ admits such a rational weak complement $f$. Using this method, we construct an explicit example in the group $\mathbb{Z}_{180}$. The weak complements in our explicit perturbative constructions are not positive definite because of restrictions on the Fourier support of the perturbations. Thus these constructions do not resolve the proposed extension of the Coven-Meyerowitz conditions to positive-definite weak tilings (arXiv:2411.03854, Problem 1.2).

papers.title: Weak $L^{2/3}$ bounds for the bilinear Hilbert transform
papers.abstract: For Schwartz functions $f_1,f_2$ on $\mathbb{R}$, define the bilinear Hilbert transform by $$ \mathbf{BHT}(f_1,f_2)(x) =\operatorname{p.v.}\int_{\mathbb{R}} f_1(x-t)f_2(x+t)\,\frac{dt}{t}. $$ We prove the weak-type estimate $$ \left\|\mathbf{BHT}(f_1,f_2)\right\|_{L^{2/3,\infty}} \lesssim_{p_1,p_2} \|f_1\|_{p_1}\|f_2\|_{p_2} $$ for $1<p_1,p_2<2$ with $1/p_1+1/p_2=3/2$. The key ingredient is a new local supremum estimate for packet sums, which we use to establish the forest estimate.

papers.title: Regular loci of affine Springer fibers at very special parahoric level
papers.abstract: For split groups, we prove that centralizers act transitively on regular loci of affine Springer fibers at very special parahoric level. As an application, we prove Chi's conjecture on the number of top-dimensional irreducible components of affine Lusztig varieties.

papers.title: Relative Derived Torsion in Categories of Reduced Modules: Comparison and Non-Noetherian Examples
papers.abstract: Let $I$ be an ideal of a commutative ring $R$. We use relative derived torsion in exact full abelian subcategories of $I$-reduced modules to study ambient derived ideal-power torsion. Exact inclusion forces $IM=I^2M$ whenever $I^2$ is finitely generated. Over a Noetherian ring, every finite object consequently decomposes into its torsion part and $IM$, and its positive-degree ambient cohomology vanishes. For $R=S[t]$ and $I=JS[t]+(t)$ with $J^2=J$, we compute every stage of the canonical Ext system and its transition maps, obtaining a comparison with $\Ext_S^q(S/J,-)$. Valuation-domain and product-of-fields examples yield nonzero cyclic first cohomology. A further construction has cyclic coefficients and cyclic ambient cohomology in every positive even degree, while its positive-degree relative cohomology vanishes. Applications determine kernels of canonical Ext maps for these coefficient modules and identify the obstruction to ring-valued specialization in the questions of Eisenbud, Mustaţă, and Stillman.

papers.title: A counterexample to the Erdős--Mahler conjecture
papers.abstract: We disprove a 1939 conjecture of Erdős and Mahler by constructing, for every real $τ\ge4$, a Cantor set of numbers of irrationality exponent $τ$, each having infinitely many regular continued-fraction convergents of the form $2^a/3^b$.

papers.title: Existence and uniqueness of asymptotic traveling waves in a time-fractional bistable reaction-diffusion equation
papers.abstract: We study asymptotic traveling waves for a reaction-diffusion equation with a Caputo time derivative. For general $C^1$ bistable imbalanced nonlinearities, we prove the existence of an asymptotic traveling wave connecting the two stable states. The asymptotic wave speed is unique, and the asymptotic profile is strictly increasing and unique up to translation. The proof uses continuation from a stationary front and the sliding method. For a cubic nonlinearity, we also derive an asymptotic formula for the speed near the balanced case, with an explicit leading coefficient. Finally, we perform numerical simulations to compare the speed predicted by the asymptotic formula with the front propagation speed in the original equation.

papers.title: A Threshold-Crossing Condition for the Least Colossally Abundant Counterexample to Robin's Inequality
papers.abstract: We study the constraints that a hypothetical least Colossally Abundant (CA) counterexample to Robin's Inequality would place on the non-trivial zeros of $ζ(s)$. In the single-prime case we express the least CA counterexample $N$ as $M\cdot p$, where $M$ is its CA predecessor and $p$ is prime. Using the von Mangoldt explicit formula for $ψ(x)$, we express $\ln p$ in terms of a sum over the non-trivial zeros of $ζ(s)$ and split that expression into its baseline contribution $\mathcal{R}_0(p)$ and its off-line distortion. When both converge, we show that the off-line distortion is negative whenever $1+1/(e^{\mathcal{R}_0(p)}+e^{2\mathcal{R}_0(p)}+\cdots+e^{(v+1)\mathcal{R}_0(p)})\le\ln(\ln M+\mathcal{R}_0(p))/\ln\ln M$, where $v$ is the $p$-adic valuation of $M$. In the case where the least CA counterexample is the product of its CA predecessor and two primes (the semiprime case), the logarithm of the product of the two primes is the sum of two von Mangoldt expansions. An analogous inequality implies that at least one of the off-line distortions of the two expansions is negative.

papers.title: Triangles without a common vertex
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a graph with $m$ edges, $t(G)$ triangles, and adjacency spectral radius $λ(G)>\sqrt m$. Li, Feng and Peng (2025) conjectured that $t(G)\ge\sqrt m-O(1)$ if no vertex belongs to every triangle of $G$. We prove the stronger bound $t(G)\geλ(G)-C$ for an absolute constant $C$, and give an explicit choice of $C$. The proof bounds the sum of the squared adjacency eigenvalues other than the largest and smallest. Interlacing and matrix perturbation estimates then restrict the neighbourhood of a vertex corresponding to a largest entry of a Perron vector to two disjoint edges and isolated vertices. A weighted count of the triangles completes the proof.

papers.title: The directed Hamilton--Waterloo problem for cycle lengths $3$ and $n$
papers.abstract: The directed Hamilton--Waterloo problem asks for a factorization of the complete symmetric digraph $K_v^*$ into directed $2$-factors, each of which is isomorphic to one of two given directed $2$-factors. In its uniform version, one seeks a decomposition of $K_v^*$ into $r$ factors consisting of directed $m$-cycles and $s$ factors consisting of directed $n$-cycles, where $r+s=v-1$. Let $m=3$, and let $n \geq 5$ be odd and not divisible by $3$. We show that, for every such $n$, the problem reduces to four decompositions of order at most $12n$: factorizations of $K^*_{3n}$ and $K^*_{6n}$ with every admissible number of factors of each kind, and two factorizations of the complete symmetric equipartite digraph with four parts of size $3n$. We construct these decompositions for $n=7$, and thereby give a complete solution for $(m,n)=(3,7)$: the obvious necessary conditions are also sufficient, with the single exception of $(v,r,s)=(6,5,0)$.

papers.title: First-order asymptotic expansions for spectral convergence of normalized graph Laplacians constructed from samples on manifolds
papers.abstract: Under i.i.d. uniform sampling from a closed Riemannian manifold embedded in Euclidean space, we derive first-order asymptotic expansions for the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of symmetrically normalized graph Laplacians constructed via Gaussian kernels and provide concentration inequalities for the remainder terms. As a direct consequence, we establish the corresponding weak convergence results. Unlike most related works, our analysis does not impose a multiplicity-one assumption on the eigenvalues, thereby extending the applicability of the framework to general manifolds with potentially nontrivial eigenvalue multiplicities.

papers.title: On Isomorphic Embeddings of Noncommutative Lorentz Spaces
papers.abstract: It is shown that for $0<p_1,p_2,q_1,q_2<\infty$, the Lorentz operator ideal $C_{p_1,q_1}$ embeds isomorphically into $C_{p_2,q_2}$ if and only if (1) $p_1=q_1=2$ or (2) $p_1=p_2$ and $q_1=q_2$, which is in contrast to the classical result that $\ell_{q}$ embeds into $\ell_{p,q}$ as a (complemented) subspace. We also study the isomorphic embeddings between operator ideals generated by the weighted Lorentz sequence spaces $d(w,p)$ ($0<p<\infty$). We characterize those (commutative/noncommutative) Lorentz function spaces $L_{W}^p$ that are isomorphic to subspaces of noncommutative $L_p$-spaces for $1\leq p<2$ over some noncommutative probability spaces, which is a noncommutative version of Schütt's theorem.

papers.title: Robustness of controllability scores for stable linear network systems
papers.abstract: Controllability scores quantify node importance in linear network systems by optimizing the allocation of input strength. Although the volumetric controllability score (VCS) and average-energy controllability score (AECS) are uniquely defined for Hurwitz systems, their sensitivity to perturbations of the system matrix remains unclear. In this paper, we investigate the robustness of these scores to such perturbations. We first prove that both scores are locally Lipschitz continuous in the system matrix and establish a robustness bound for Hurwitz comparison matrices. We then characterize the directional derivative of the optimal allocation along a differentiable matrix path as the unique solution of a critical-cone quadratic program, whose linear term is computed using differentiated Lyapunov equations. For single-edge weakening, the norm of the resulting response vector provides a robustness-based measure of edge importance. Numerical experiments show that the response, and hence the edge importance, depends on both the criterion and the dynamics, not only on the network topology.

papers.title: The Fermat--Torricelli problem under isosceles orthogonality-type conditions
papers.abstract: The location problem studied by Weber \cite{Weber} leads to the Fermat--Torricelli problem of minimizing sums of distances. Benítez, Fernández and Soriano \cite{BFS} proved that a real normed space of dimension at least three is an inner-product space if and only if every triple of points has a Fermat--Torricelli median in its convex hull. Pakhrou \cite{Pakhrou} showed that it suffices to test equilateral triangles. We establish a characterization using triangles $\{0,x,y\}$ satisfying \[ \|x+y\|=λ\|x-y\|,\qquad \forall\,λ>2/3, \] with the parameter fixed in each characterization. The case of parameter one gives an isosceles orthogonality criterion. The proof combines radial rescaling with the transfer of planar minimality to the ambient space, without completeness or regularity assumptions on the norm.

papers.title: Classical solvability of the Cauchy problem for multi-order time-fractional systems with full matrices of differential operators
papers.abstract: This article investigates the Cauchy problem in the whole space for a system of linear time-fractional partial differential equations with an arbitrary fixed number of components and a full matrix of constant-coefficient spatial differential operators. Each component is governed by its own Caputo derivative, and no rational relation between the fractional orders is required. We assume that the diagonal spatial symbols are homogeneous, positive and elliptic, while the off-diagonal entries have strictly lower order than the diagonal operator in the corresponding column. Using spatial Fourier and temporal Laplace transforms, we construct solution operators through convergent series of time convolutions involving scalar Mittag--Leffler kernels. These series account for all coupling paths, including repeated interactions between components. A fractional Duhamel representation incorporates nonhomogeneous source terms. We establish uniform convergence on bounded frequency regions and weighted multiplier estimates by separating low and high spatial frequencies. Under suitable Sobolev regularity assumptions on the initial data and continuously differentiable source terms, we prove existence and uniqueness of a classical solution, together with continuity and regularity properties in the appropriate Sobolev spaces. The general result includes two-component systems and is illustrated by fully coupled examples.

papers.title: On Lévy type subgroups of the symmetric group of $ω$ associated with simple density functions
papers.abstract: The Lévy group, introduced by Lévy in (Lévy (1951)), is defined by \[\mathcal{L} = \left\{σ\in aut : \lim_n \frac{|\{k\in n : σ(k)\notin n\}|}{n} = 0\right\},\] where $aut$ denotes the group of all permutations of $ω$. This group happens to be closely connected with the notion of asymptotic density as it consists of permutations that map sets with an asymptotic density back to sets with the same density. Our aim is to replicate the construction by replacing $n$ in the denominator by $g(n)$ for a function $g:ω\to [0,\infty)$ with $g(n)\to \infty$ (weight), which leads us a class of Lévy type groups. Specifically we define simple Lévy group with weight $g$ as \[\mathcal{L}_g = \left\{σ\in aut : \lim_n \frac{|\{k\in n : σ(k)\notin n\}|}{g(n)} = 0\right\}.\] As a natural consequence we first study its relationship with the notion of simple density functions (which had been introduced in \cite{gd2} as a general class of density functions by similar manner) paving way for the class of simple density functions and ideals $\mathcal{I}_g$. We have $\mathcal{L}_g = aut$ if and only if $n/g(n)\to 0$ (just like $\mathcal{I}_g = 2^ω$ if and only if $n/g(n)\to 0$). The relation between simple density functions and simple Lévy groups is in expected line. What seems more interesting is the comparative study of these groups. We start with the relation between $\mathcal{L}$ and $\mathcal{L}_g$ and constructing suitable examples it is shown that strict inclusions and incomparability may occur. Finally we come up with an interesting observation that there are continuum many pairwise incomparable simple Lévy groups, each of which is incomparable with $\mathcal{L}$.

papers.title: Uniquely $K_{4}$-saturated graphs with large maximum degree
papers.abstract: A graph $G$ is \textit{uniquely $H$-saturated} if it contains no copy of $H$ as a subgraph, but adding any edge to $G$ creates exactly one copy of $H$ in the resultant graph. In this paper, we consider the uniquely $K_{4}$-saturated graphs and characterize the uniquely $K_{4}$-saturated graphs on $n$ vertices with maximum degree $Δ\geq n-5$. We prove that if $G$ is a uniquely $K_{4}$-saturated graph with universal vertex $x$, then $G-x$ is either a star or a Moore graph of diameter 2. The uniquely $K_{4}$-saturated graphs with maximum degrees $n-3$ and $n-5$ are $\overline{C_{7}}$ and $G_{10}$ in Figure 2, respectively. But there are no uniquely $K_{4}$-saturated graphs with maximum degree $n-2$ or $n-4$.

papers.title: Global existence and blow-up for a fractional wave equation with logarithmic nonlinearity and strong damping
papers.abstract: This paper studies a fractional strongly damped wave equation with logarithmic nonlinearity. Based on local well-posedness of weak solutions via the Galerkin approximation, we employ the potential well theory to derive the existence of global solutions under subcritical and critical initial energy conditions. Moreover, infinite time blow-up phenomena are obtained under subcritical, critical, and arbitrarily high supercritical initial energy conditions.

papers.title: Judicious $r$-partitions of $r$-uniform hypergraphs
papers.abstract: Bollobás and Thomason conjectured that every $r$-uniform hypergraph with $m$ edges admits an $r$-partition such that each class meets at least $rm/(2r-1)$ edges. In this paper, we establish a lower bound of $(11-\sqrt{13})m/18$ for every $r\ge 2$. This improves Haslegrave's bound $rm/(3r-4)$ for every $r\ge 8$.

papers.title: Convex monohedral tilings: a sharp neighbor bound and rigidity in the equality case
papers.abstract: We study both side-to-side and non-side-to-side convex monohedral tilings of the Euclidean plane in which every tile has the same number of neighbors. Reflections are allowed, point contacts count as neighbors, and no periodicity assumption is imposed. Combining boundary estimates for sums of face curvatures, angle-incidence counts and side-length matching, we prove that the common neighbor number satisfies $N\le21$ and classify all equality cases. Equality holds precisely when the prototile is a $30^\circ$-$30^\circ$-$120^\circ$ triangle and the entire tiling is similar to the central subdivision of the standard equilateral triangular tiling. This resolves the open problem on the maximum common number of neighbors recorded in Adams's The Tiling Book.

papers.title: Tail Asymptotics for Gaps in Unitary Ensembles and the Airy Point Process
papers.abstract: We derive tail asymptotics for the gap between the $k$th and $(k+1)$st largest particles, with $k$ fixed, in unitary ensembles and in the Airy point process. For the finite-$N$ ensembles, we consider the probabilities of a rescaled gap larger than $a_N$ and of a rescaled gap smaller than $b_N$, in the joint limits $N\to\infty$, $a_N\to\infty$ with $a_N=o(N^{2/3})$, and $N\to\infty$, $b_N\downarrow0$, respectively. For the Airy point process, the right and left tails are analyzed as the gap size tends to infinity and zero, respectively. More precisely, in both models, we obtain logarithmic right-tail asymptotics up to the constant term and cubic left-tail asymptotics with coefficient $k/6$. As an application, we also derive the limiting conditional laws of the leading particles given the existence of an abnormally large or small gap. In particular, for $k=1$, large-gap conditioning leads to a transition from Tracy--Widom to Gaussian fluctuations of the largest particle, similar to the BBP transition. Further, among any fixed number of leading gaps, we also determine the limiting probabilities of which gap attains a large maximum or a small minimum.

papers.title: Proximal point algorithm for interval valued optimization problems with application to lasso problem
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider a class of unconstrained interval valued optimization problems and using a suitable scalarization technique, we formulate an associated scalarized optimization problem and establish the relationships between the optimal solution of the scalarized problem and the $LU$-nondominated solution of the considered optimization problem. Based on this framework, we propose a proximal point algorithm and derive the global convergence of the sequence generated by the proposed algorithm along with the sublinear and linear rate of convergence for convex and strongly convex cases, respectively. Finally, we provide suitable numerical experiments along with comparative analysis with an existing method and applicability of the proposed algorithm on an interval valued lasso regression problem, highlighting its potential in machine learning models with uncertain data.

papers.title: Uniqueness and Nondegeneracy of Ground States for Critical-Hardy Fractional Equations
papers.abstract: We study ground states of nonlinear fractional Schrödinger equations with the critical Hardy potential in $\mathbb{R}^d$, where $d\geq3$. We prove the existence and qualitative properties of ground states, based on which we analyze the uniqueness and nondegeneracy of ground states. As a byproduct, we also investigate the optimizers of the critical Hardy--Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality, from which a sharp Keller--Hardy--Lieb--Thirring inequality is analytically derived.

papers.title: An automated approach to structure theorems for minimally repetitive rich words
papers.abstract: Recent work on repetitions in rich words has led to the intensive study of the family of infinite rich words $\{{\mathbf u}_d:d\geq 2\}$, where ${\mathbf u}_d$ is the fixed point of the morphism $\varphi_d:Σ_d^*\rightarrow Σ_d^*$ defined by $\varphi_d(i)=\tt{0}(i+1)$ for $i\in\{\tt{0},\ldots,d-2\}$ and $\varphi_d(d-1)=\tt{0}(d-1)(d-1)$. For $d=2$ and $d=3$, it is known that the repetition threshold for infinite $d$-ary rich words is equal to the asymptotic critical exponent $E^*({\mathbf u}_{2d-1})$. Moreover, the structure of ${\mathbf u}_{2d-1}$ underlies the structure of all ``minimally repetitive'' $d$-ary rich words: there is a real number $t_d>E^*({\mathbf u}_{2d-1})$ such that every infinite $t_d$-power-free $d$-ary rich word contains the language of $π({\mathbf u}_{2d-1})$ for one of finitely many morphisms $π:Σ_{2d-1}^*\rightarrow Σ_d^*$. We conjecture that a similar situation holds for all $d\geq 2$, and prove this for the first unknown case $d=4$. To do this, we develop a new approach for proving such structure theorems. Two key new concepts are ``compatibility'' of return words to palindromes in recurrent rich words, and ``$t$-persistent repetitions''. They facilitate the automation of several aspects of the proofs which were previously done laboriously by hand. We first demonstrate our approach by giving a much shorter proof of the known structure theorem for infinite $\tfrac{16}{7}$-power-free ternary rich words. Then we prove a new structure theorem: every infinite $2.12$-power-free quaternary rich word contains the language of one of seven distinct words of the form $π({\mathbf u}_7)$, up to permutation of the letters. We prove that all seven words are rich and have critical exponent $E^*({\mathbf u}_7)$, so the repetition threshold for quaternary rich words is $E^*({\mathbf u}_7)\doteq 2.1197196907$.

papers.title: Unstable Entropy and Volume Growth for Partially Hyperbolic Diffeomorphisms
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be a $C^{1}$ diffeomorphism on a compact manifold $M$ admitting a partially hyperbolic splitting $TM=E^{cs}\oplus E^{u}$ where $E^{u}$ is uniformly expanding. We establish a lower bound for the unstable topological entropy (w.r.t. $E^{u}$): $$h^{u}_{\rm top}\left(f\right)\geq\limsup_{n\to+\infty}\frac{1}{n}\log\int_{M}\left|\det \left(Df^{n}_{x}|_{E^{u}}\right)\right|\,dx.$$ Moreover, if there exists a measure of maximal unstable entropy whose Lyapunov exponents along $E^{cs}$ are all non-positive, then equality holds and the $\limsup$ is in fact a limit.

papers.title: Proximal gradient method for multiobjective interval valued optimization problem with application in portfolio selection
papers.abstract: In this article, we consider a class of unconstrained multiobjective interval-valued optimization problems in which each objective function is a sum of a generalized Hukuhara(gH)-differentiable interval valued function and a proper, convex and gH-lower semicontinuous interval valued function, which is possibly non-gH-differentiable.
