Within this framework, we introduce the notion of a proximal gradient direction and characterize the Pareto critical points of the considered problem through a strongly convex auxiliary subproblem. Based on these characterizations, we develop a proximal gradient algorithm with an Armijo-type line search that ensures sufficient descent with respect to the interval partial order. We then establish the existence of an uniform lower bound on the admissible step length, the global convergence of the generated sequence to a Pareto critical point followed by a global rate of convergence in the general nonconvex setting. The theoretical findings of the proposed method are validated through some test problems and further illustrate its applicability on portfolio selection problems involving interval-valued data.

papers.title: Rotating Walks, Derandomized Squares, and Permutation Conjugated Walks
papers.abstract: Using the recent strong convergence results of Bordenave and Collins (Annals of Mathematics) and Chen et al. (Annals of Mathematics), we study the average case behavior of rotating random walks of Cohen and Maor (STOC 2023) and the derandomized square construction of Rozenman and Vadhan (RANDOM 2005). Concretely, we prove a conjecture of Cohen et al. (ITCS 2025) regarding the average case behavior of derandomized squaring for random graphs and show that the existential bounds of Cohen and Maor for their rotating random walk construction hold with high-probability for random graphs. Using the results of O'Donnell and Wu (FOCS 2020), we can in polynomial time construct a family of graphs and rotations which almost saturate the bounds of Cohen and Maor, and meet the bounds conjectured by Cohen et al. for all vertex-transitive auxiliary graphs of fixed degree in the derandomized square. Finally, we study independent random permutation conjugates of deterministic regular graph adjacency matrices. We prove quantitative weak convergence to freely independent tree adjacency operators when the degrees are fixed and the girths tend to infinity. Separately, a covering argument gives deterministic spectral lower bounds for polynomials with non-negative coefficients, recovering the lower bound of Cohen et al. for rotating walks.

papers.title: Gödel's Incompleteness Theorems in Grounded Arithmetic
papers.abstract: Reflective Grounded Arithmetic (RGA) is a paracomplete arithmetic in which every term is a program and truth is grounded evaluation. RGA discharges a hypothesis only when it proves the hypothesis decided. This paper shows, in a machine-checked Isabelle/HOL development, how Gödel's incompleteness theorems hold for RGA and for systems built on it. RGA's implication is material and RGA has the disjunction property, so the implications the textbook proof of the second theorem uses fail while its entailments and rules hold: Gödel's proof survives as entailments. RGA does not prove its consistency sentence Con, and RGA derives its own second theorem as the entailment $\mathit{Con}\vdash\neg\mathit{Pr}(\ulcorner\mathit{Con}\urcorner)$ and as one sentence quantified over proofs. The second theorem is then proved once, for every Gödel extension of RGA: an entailment relation on RGA's language, closed under RGA's rules, with a checker that meets three structural conditions, NEC, D3 and EXPL as proof transformers, D1 as closed acceptance, and consistency. D2 is not among the conditions. RGA with its checker is one instance. Inductive Grounded Arithmetic (IGA), RGA with ground induction, is another, its checker adding one rule detector, and IGA does not derive its consistency sentence for it. Adoption, a reflection rule whose premise is a derived warrant that the checker accepts computed proofs of every instance of a universal, gives consistent extensions RGA$^+$ and IGA$^+$. RGA$^+$ derives RGA's consistency sentence and IGA$^+$ derives RGA's and IGA's, so each strictly extends its base, and IGA$^+$ both. The second theorem holds at every adopted notation claim, and adopting Turing's code for that claim's checker derives its consistency sentence, so no claim certifies itself. Whether IGA alone derives RGA's consistency sentence is open, and the paper names what two routes to an answer need.
papers.comments: 103 pages; splits the Goedel incompleteness material out of Internal Reasoning companion paper 2608.16140, which is getting a corresponding major update

papers.title: The Proof of the Alon--Kim Conjecture
papers.abstract: In 1997, Alon and Kim proposed an asymptotic edge-coloring bound motivated by a bound on the number of edges in intersecting uniform hypergraphs. The Alon--Kim conjecture asserts that, for fixed integers $k\ge t\ge1$ and $\varepsilon>0$, every $k$-uniform multihypergraph $H$ in which any two distinct edges intersect in at most $t$ vertices satisfies $χ'(H)\le(t-1+\frac{1}{t}+\varepsilon)Δ(H)$ whenever $Δ(H)$ is sufficiently large. In this paper, we prove the Alon--Kim conjecture. Our method combines finite-dimensional convex optimization with probabilistic methods.

papers.title: Berry phase and Hannay angle as Taylor coefficients of the minimal action
papers.abstract: For a Hamiltonian system with one degree of freedom whose parameters are varied slowly around a closed loop, with slowness $δ$, we study the minimal action $β_δ$ of the resulting time-periodic system and its convex conjugate, Mather's $α$-function $α_δ$, both normalized per unit time. The cycle map of such a system is an area-preserving map of the cylinder which in general is not integrable. We prove that $β_δ(ρ)$ and $α_δ(c)$ have asymptotic expansions in $δ$ to every finite order, locally uniformly in the rotational regime of the frozen systems, and we identify the coefficients geometrically. The zeroth coefficient of $α_δ$ is the average of the frozen effective Hamiltonians, as shown by Evans and Gomes. The first coefficient is the classical Berry phase: at fixed rotation number $ρ$, the first Taylor coefficient of $β_δ(ρ)$ is, modulo periods, Weinstein's Berry phase of the loop of frozen invariant curves of the class whose averaged frozen frequency is $ρ$, each curve weighted by its Mather measure. In particular, the minimal action selects the weighting in Weinstein's construction. The Hannay angle, the derivative of the Berry phase, governs the rotation numbers of all minimizing measures, including those supported on Aubry--Mather sets of the cycle map, where no invariant curve exists; and the intervals of classes on which a rotation number is locked have length $O(δ^\infty)$. Since the expansions concern exact convex functions, no adiabatic approximation is involved. A transformation rule under loops of point transformations explains why the Berry phase is defined only modulo $2πc\mathbb{Z}$. Linear oscillators, treated by the same method, recover Berry's formula for the generalized harmonic oscillator and show that the expansions are asymptotic only.

papers.title: Mean Curvature Flow with Thermal Fluctuations in Dimensions Two and Higher
papers.abstract:
Surface tension drives interfaces towards smaller area, while thermal motion produces shape fluctuations whose strength is linked to the interfacial mobility through the fluctuation--dissipation relation. These mechanisms lead to mean-curvature flow with thermal noise, whose graph formulation is known as the Kawasaki--Ohta equation. We establish global-in-time existence of energy martingale solutions to the spatially regularized Kawasaki--Ohta equation for periodic graphs in every dimension $d\geq2$, with initial data in $H^1(\mathbb T^d)$. No restriction on the noise intensity is needed for $d=2$, while a smallness condition is required for $d\geq3$. The key new challenges arise from the thermal noise, which has a $(1+|
abla u|^2)^{1/4}$-type coefficient. This coefficient gives rise to an irregular Stratonovich-to-Itô correction term of the form $
abla u\cdot D^2u
abla u/(1+|
abla u|^2)^{3/2}$. Our main innovation is a compactness argument tailored to the structure of the correction. By combining a factorization of this term with $H^1(\mathbb T^d)$ and area estimates, we establish strong convergence of the normalized gradients and reconstruct the weighted Hessian, which allows us to define the correction at energy regularity and identify its approximation limit.

papers.title: Topology idealized
papers.abstract: Inspired by recent work of A. Njamcul and A. Pavlović, we study topological spaces expanded by ideals of sets. We investigate the relationship between the cardinal invariants of the ideal topological space $(X, τ_\mathcal{I})$, the underlying topology $(X, τ)$, and the cardinal characteristics of the ideal $\mathcal{I}$. Furthermore, we analyze continuous maps between standard Polish spaces and their ideal expansions. We establish rigidity phenomena showing that continuous functions from $(X, τ)$ into $(X, τ_\mathcal{I})$ are severely constrained (e.g., taking at most countably many values on Polish spaces and being strictly constant on $\mathbb{R}$), whereas continuous functions from $(\mathbb{R}, τ_\mathcal{I})$ to $(\mathbb{R}, τ)$ collapse to standard continuous functions under mild conditions on the ideal.

papers.title: On the equidistribution of eigenfunctions of higher dimensional cat maps modulo prime powers
papers.abstract: The so-called $\mathit{Cat\ Map}$, which is a linear map generated by symplectic matrices $A \in \operatorname{Sp}(2d,\mathbb Z)$ modulo an integer $N\ge 1$ is a classical discrete model of quantum ergodicity. For $d=1$ it has been investigated by P. Kurlberg and Z. Rudnick (2001), J. Bourgain (2007) and A. Ostafe, I. E. Shparlinski and J. F. Voloch (2023). The significantly more difficult case of $d>1$ has been studied by P. Kurlberg, A. Ostafe, Z. Rudnick and I. E. Shparlinski (2025). All these works apply only to almost all $N$ and are unable to provide an explicit sequence of such ``good'' values of $N$. The authors (2026) have given such a construction with a polynomial decay on the corresponding matrix coefficients. Here we use some new ideas and improve this bound.

papers.title: Periods and CM motives of abelian type
papers.abstract: We associate algebraic Hecke characters to certain invertible motives for absolute Hodge cycles with coefficients in a number field $K$, reversing a viewpoint of Schappacher. These motives $N$ include abelian motives and a new notion of algebraic motive. This Hecke character determines the complex and the $p$-adic periods of $N$, and is determined by the latter; this gives a proof of the Mumford-Tate conjecture for $N$. When $K$ and $N$ are abelian, we prove a refinement of the Gross-Deligne conjecture, as well as $l$-adic and $p$-adic variants. We also formulate a version of the algebraic relations between rational values of the gamma function given by Koblitz and Ogus in terms of a distribution with values in the Picard group of the category of (abelian) Chow motives.

papers.title: Stochastic homogenization of $p$-resistance forms on nested fractals
papers.abstract: We study the stochastic homogenization of $p$-energies on infinite nested fractals. We assign i.i.d. random $p$-resistance forms $D_{0,α}$ to level-$0$ cells of an infinite pre-nested fractal, and study the scaling limit of the resulting random $p$-resistance form $\mathcal{D}^{(0)}$. Under a moment condition on the reciprocal of $D_{0,α}$, we prove that the sequence of rescaled and renormalized random energies is almost surely Mosco convergent to an equally weighted self-similar $p$-resistance form. As an application, when $p=2$, we prove the almost sure weak convergence of the associated rescaled continuous-time random walk. In particular, we allow arbitrarily small random conductances and impose no condition on the upper bound of random conductances.

papers.title: Quasisymmetric rigidity of self-similar square carpets
papers.abstract: Let $S$ be a self-similar square carpet obtained by subdividing the unit square into $n^2$ congruent cells, deleting a nonempty collection of strictly interior open cells with pairwise disjoint closures, and repeating the same pattern with the same orientation in every retained cell. We prove that every quasisymmetric self-homeomorphism of $S$, equipped with the Euclidean metric, is a Euclidean isometry. The result holds for every integer $n\ge3$ and imposes no symmetry condition on the deletion pattern. Consequently, the quasisymmetric and isometric groups coincide with the stabilizer of the first-generation holes in the symmetry group of the square. The proof combines round uniformization and Schottky-map stabilization with a propagation argument across retained cells. This produces global homothety relations for conjugates of cell contractions and forces preservation of the outer peripheral square. Periodic points on its sides then yield preservation of the corners, reducing the conclusion to the four-corner rigidity theorem for square carpets.

papers.title: Two Types of Cards in Kelly-Ulam Conjecture
papers.abstract: We consider the case in Kelly-Ulam conjecture where there are only two types of cards in deck. It was possible to prove that graphs with this property are uniquely reconstructed by their card deck.

papers.title: Multivariate Bernstein duality for tournament Wright--Fisher diffusions
papers.abstract: We give a probabilistic proof of a multivariate Bernstein duality for a multivariate Wright--Fisher frequency process with selection encoded by a finite tournament. The construction includes nontransitive interactions, such as rock--paper--scissors selection. Its dual is a pure-jump process of coefficient functions in the multinomial Bernstein basis. Selection increases the Bernstein degree through a winner--loser averaging operator, whereas neutral resampling decreases it through a duplication operator. For the proof, we construct a continuous forward process independently of duality, use duality to establish uniqueness, and obtain a weak stochastic differential equation representation and invariance of the simplex faces. This provides a sampling-based treatment of the tournament specialization of multitype Bernstein duality, extending an open problem in the binary Kingman setting of Cordero, Hummel, and Schertzer (2022).

papers.title: Local well-posedness, wave breaking and ill-posedness for the unidirectional non-local wave model
papers.abstract: In this paper, we first establish local well-posedness (existence, uniqueness and continuous dependence) for the Cauchy problem associated with the unidirectional non-local wave model in the Besov spaces $B^s_{p,r}$ with $s>1+\frac{1}{p}$ and $1\leq p,r\leq\infty$, as well as in the critical Besov spaces $B^{1+\frac{1}{p}}_{p,1}$ with $1\leq p<\infty$. Next, by exploiting the fine structure of the equation and performing a delicate analysis of the commutator terms, we establish a new sufficient condition for wave breaking without using any conservation law. Finally, we prove that the model is ill-posed in $B^{1+\frac{1}{p}}_{p,r}$ for $1\leq p\leq\infty$ and $1<r\leq\infty$. Our analysis further clarifies the well-posedness theory and wave-breaking behavior of the unidirectional non-local wave model arising from the motion of a cold plasma in a magnetic field, which refines and improves previously known related results.

papers.title: Uniqueness and nondegeneracy of ground states for the pure-power Born-Infeld equation
papers.abstract: For \(N\ge3\) and \(p>2N/(N-2)\), we study the Born--Infeld equation \[ -\diver\!\left(\frac{\nabla u}{\sqrt{1-|\nabla u|^2}}\right) =|u|^{p-2}u \qquad\text{in }\R^N . \] We prove that the positive ground state \(Q\) is unique up to translation. We also prove that the kernel of the linearized operator at \(Q\) is spanned by \(\partial_{x_1}Q,\ldots,\partial_{x_N}Q\), and determine all nonzero optimizers of the sharp Born--Infeld Sobolev inequality. To prove nondegeneracy, we first rule out nonzero radial kernel functions using the Morse index and a Wronskian identity. We then treat the angular modes by spherical harmonics. To prove uniqueness, we compare radial solutions for large \(p\), and extend the result to all \(p>2N/(N-2)\) by compactness and continuation.

papers.title: Non-existence of solutions to a system of quadratic derivative nonlinear Schrödinger equations
papers.abstract: We consider the Cauchy problem for a system of quadratic derivative nonlinear Schrödinger equations introduced by M. Colin and T. Colin (2004) as a model of laser-plasma interaction. Under a coefficient condition, we prove that there are initial data admitting no solution in Sobolev spaces, both on the torus and on the Euclidean space.

papers.title: The anisotropic De Giorgi conjecture in $\mathbb{R}^4$
papers.abstract: We establish the anisotropic De Giorgi conjecture in $\mathbb{R}^4$ under the limiting assumption. More precisely, every entire solution of the anisotropic Allen-Cahn equation satisfying $u_{x_4}>0$ and $u(x,x_4)\to\pm1$ as $x_4\to\pm\infty$ for each $x\in\mathbb{R}^3$ is one-dimensional. We show that every nontrivial generalized subgraph globally minimizing the anisotropic perimeter in $\mathbb{R}^4$ is a halfspace. Combining an anisotropic tilt-excess decay estimate with a Liouville argument, we then deduce one-dimensional symmetry.

papers.title: Essential $p$-dimension of simple algebras and noncrossed products of prime exponent
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be a prime and $F$ a field of characteristic different from $p$. For integers $n\ge2$ and $1\le m\le n$, we complete the determination of the essential $p$-dimension of the class of central simple algebras of degree $p^n$ and exponent dividing $p^m$. In particular, we have $\operatorname{ed}_p(\operatorname{PGL}(p^n))=p^{2n-2}+1$, extending a result of Merkurjev for $n=2$. Using the comparison theorem of Chernousov and Merkurjev, we also determine the essential $p$-dimension of every split simple group of type $A$. To obtain the lower bounds, we apply a theorem of Ofek to block centralizers. As an application, we prove the existence of division algebras of exponent $p$ over field extensions of $F$ which remain noncrossed products after any field extension of degree prime to $p$, and answer in the negative a problem in the survey by Auel, Brussel, Garibaldi, and Vishne. The algebras can be chosen to have degree $p^n$ for every $n\ge3$ if $p$ is odd and every $n\ge4$ if $p=2$. For $p=2$ and every $n\ge3$, we also determine the essential $2$-dimensions of the classes of central simple algebras of degree $2^n$ with orthogonal involution and with symplectic involution.

papers.title: Beyond Frankl's conjecture: Maximum sum of sizes of cross-intersecting families with restricted conditions
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{G}$ be two families of subsets of $[n]$. We say that $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{G}$ are \emph{cross-intersecting} if $F \cap G \neq \emptyset$ for all $F \in \mathcal{F}$ and $G \in \mathcal{G}$. Let $n, k_1, k_2, m, r, t$ be positive integers satisfying $n > k_1 + k_2$. Suppose that $\mathcal{F} \subseteq \binom{[n]}{k_1}$ and $\mathcal{G} \subseteq \binom{[n]}{k_2}$ are two cross-intersecting families such that $\left\{F \in \binom{[n]}{k_1} : |F \cap [m]| \geq r\right\} \subseteq \mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{F}$ is $t$-intersecting. In this paper, we determine the maximum sum $|\mathcal{F}| + |\mathcal{G}|$ under these assumptions. By taking $k_1=k_2+t-1$, $m = k_2+t+s-1$ and $r=k_2+t-1$ for $s\ge 0$, our result recovers a conjecture of Frankl \cite{frankl2016new}, which was recently confirmed by Wu, Feng, and Li \cite{wu2025proof}. Further, we establish a complete characterization of all extremal families. Our approach extends the Ahlswede--Khachatrian generating set method to handle the simultaneous constraints of cross-intersection and $t$-intersection, subject to additional structural conditions.

papers.title: A remark on Liouville-type theorems for the stationary Navier--Stokes equations in $\mathbb{R}^3$ under pointwise conditions on the head pressure
papers.abstract: We study the stationary Navier--Stokes equations in the three-dimensional whole space and the Liouville-type problem under the condition of finite Dirichlet integral. We give a remark on the recent result by Chae [7, Theorem 1.2], in which an upper bound of the gradient of the head pressure and a lower bound of the head pressure with certain rates were assumed to prove triviality of solutions. In this paper, we extend the range of admissible rates by two different arguments. One relies on the pointwise decay of head pressure and the classical argument of Galdi [11]. The other is similar to the argument of Chae [4, 6] and is based on the maximum principle for the head pressure, the integral identity between the vorticity and the gradient of the head pressure on the upper level set of the head pressure, and the coarea formula. This also gives a more refined proof for [7, Theorem 1.2].
papers.comments: Dedicated to Professor Yoshikazu Giga on the award of the Kodaira Kunihiko Prize

papers.title: Gaussian limits for non-cyclic and elementary abelian Sylow subgroups of the multiplicative group
papers.abstract: We study the number of non-cyclic Sylow subgroups of $(\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z)^\times$. Pollack suggested investigating whether this count has a limiting distribution after suitable normalization. For uniformly chosen $n\le x$, we prove a Gaussian limit with variance asymptotic to $\tfrac12\log_2x/\log_3x$. Motivated by the fixed-rank normal-order results of Morales, Polanco, and Pollack, we further prove joint Gaussian limits for this count and the numbers of elementary abelian Sylow subgroups of any fixed finite collection of ranks at least two. We give explicit prime-sum centers and asymptotics for all arithmetic covariances. The same joint theorem includes the number of common prime divisors of Euler's and Dedekind's functions. The proof uses the integer Kubilius model, estimates for the dependence between distinct output primes, and mean-square bounds for arithmetic truncation.

papers.title: Finite Numerical Joyce Transport and Derived Hall Scattering Groupoid
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{D}$ be a triangulated category over a finite field $k$ satisftying certain finiteness conditions. Let $Σ$ be a connected component of the space of numerical stability conditions on $\mathcal{D}$ with one element $σ\inΣ$ satisfying the support property and the finite counting condition. We prove that each of the Joyce elements with respect to $σ_1\inΣ$ is a finite rational Lie polynomial in those of any other $σ_0\inΣ$, so the generated Lie subalgebra $\mathfrak{L}_σ,σ\inΣ$ in the uncompleted derived Hall algebra $\mathcal{H}(\mathcal{D})$ is constant on $Σ$. Our proof combines completions on strict sectors with a uniform mass bound for successive local substitutions. We use the method of Hall scattering diagrams on phase categories to provide a realization of the transform of Joyce elements. For the finite-length case, we also give an alternative proof using finite-length hearts instead of phase categories. As an application, we explicit the generators of the Lie subalgebra $\mathfrak{L}$ in the Dynkin case.

papers.title: Diophantine approximation with prime denominators in short intervals
papers.abstract: For any real number $x$, let $\|x\|$ denote the distance from $x$ to the nearest integer, and let $α$ be any irrational number. We prove that, for $Y=X^γ$ with $7/12<γ\le 1$ and $0<θ<\min \{(12γ-7)/24, 1/9\}$, there exist infinitely many $X$ for which there are primes $p$ satisfying $$ \|αp\|<p^{-θ},\quad X-Y<p<X. $$ Moreover, we obtain an asymptotic formula for the number of such primes. Our result extends the admissible range of short intervals in the corresponding result of Baier and Roy from $2/3<γ\le 1$ to $7/12<γ\le 1$, reaching Huxley's classical range for primes in short intervals and also improves the exponent $θ$ in $2/3\le γ\le 3/4.$

papers.title: Unified Far-field and Near-field Codebook Design for XL-array Systems
papers.abstract: While extremely large-scale antenna arrays (XL-arrays) hold immense promise for next-generation wireless networks, the paradigm shift encompassing new near-field communications renders conventional discrete Fourier transform (DFT)-based Type-I codebooks inefficient. Meanwhile, existing near-field alternatives usually impose prohibitively high storage and/or feedback burdens. To tackle these challenges, we propose in this letter a unified codebook applicable to both far-field and near-field XL-array systems. Our key idea is to express the near-field channel steering vector in an equivalent form, which is a Hadamard product of an angular vector and a curvature-related vector. This new representation allows direct reuse of the legacy Type-I codebook for angle quantization, while only a lightweight auxiliary codebook is newly added for additional curvature quantization. Subsequently, we optimize the auxiliary curvature codebook by maximizing the average beamforming gain given the information of user distribution. By leveraging the local monotonicity of the beamforming gain with respect to curvature mismatch, the optimization problem is further reduced to a quantization-error minimization problem, for which suboptimal curvature codewords are obtained. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed unified codebook achieves near-optimal beamforming performance that approaches its upper bound based on perfect channel state information (CSI), while significantly reducing the required feedback overhead as compared to various benchmark schemes.
papers.comments: 5 Pages, 2 figures, submitted to IEEE for possible publication

papers.title: The Grothendieck property of noncommutative Marcinkiewicz spaces
papers.abstract: We study sufficient and necessary conditions of a noncommutative Marcinkiewicz space to have the Grothendieck property. In particular, we show that every noncommutative weak $L_p$-space, $1<p<\infty$, is Grothendieck. This answers questions due to several open problems in the literature.

papers.title: Besicovitch-like Pseudo Almost Automorphic Stochastic Processes: Theory and Applications to Semilinear SDEs
papers.abstract: This paper introduces, for the first time, the concept of Besicovitch-like pseudo almost automorphic stochastic processes. As a meaningful application, we investigate a class of semilinear stochastic equations driven by Brownian motion in a separable Hilbert space. By combining the Banach fixed point theorem with refined inequality techniques, we establish sufficient conditions guaranteeing the existence, uniqueness, and global exponential stability of Besicovitch-like pseudo almost automorphic solutions in distribution for the considered equations. An example is provided to show the validity of the obtained results.

papers.title: Limit theorems for dispersing billiards with infinite cusps
papers.abstract: Extending Lenci's work in CMP (2002), Chaos (2003), we present new insights into semi-dispersing billiards with infinite cusps. We investigate the Convergence to Stable Processes (CSP) and Functional Central Limit Theorems (FCLT) both for the collision map and for the billiard flow. Whereas the billiard map always preserves an infinite measure equivalent to Lebesgue, the billiard flow preserves the Lebesgue measure, which is either finite or infinite depending on the finiteness of the area of the billiard table. When the reference measure is infinite, the usual LLN fails, but we are able to prove the CSP and FCLT. We also prove classical FCLT for the flow when the area of the billiard table is finite. These results are obtained through a precise study of the properties of the billiard map, combined with a general approach based on induction and on coupling involving point processes.

papers.title: On the proof of Falconer distance conjecture
papers.abstract: We are able to catch the main idea from OpenAI's recent release and present a proof of Falconer distance conjecture in our own words. Arguments are judiciously simplified and carefully designed for graduate-level readers.
papers.comments: 20 pages, 5 figures, carefully written for graduate-levels. The first draft was hand-typed (40% left-handed + 60% right-handed as the corresponding author injured his left wrist at page 15). LLM then came in for proofreading and making figures

papers.title: A congruence-group counterexample to Kourovka Problem 21.7
papers.abstract: For every prime $p>24$, let $H$ be the kernel of $\SL_2(\Z/p^9\Z)\to\SL_2(\F_p)$. We prove that $H$ is not IYB, whereas $H\times C_{p^8}$ is IYB. The proof excludes a pre-Lie multiplication on the rank-three Lie ring with bracket $p[x,y]$ over $\Z/p^8\Z$ using three trace identities. It follows that the supersoluble group $H\times(C_{p^8}\rtimes C_2)$, with the involution acting by inversion, has IYB Sylow subgroups and is not IYB. Its nilpotent residual is cyclic and its Sylow $p$-subgroup has nilpotency class eight. For $p=31$, an action of order three gives a supersoluble counterexample of odd order $3\cdot31^{32}$. The same construction gives an IYB $p$-group with a specified central cyclic direct factor such that the quotient of the whole group by the unique subgroup of order $p$ in that factor is non-IYB.

papers.title: Learning the Brownian Motion in Machine Learning for Parametric Parabolic PDEs: A Backward Quadrature Approach
papers.abstract: We propose a backward quadrature learning (BQL) method for solving high dimensional parametric semilinear parabolic partial differential equations (PDEs). To the best of our knowledge, this work is the first to extend the applicability of BSDE-based stochastic numerical methods to this class of PDEs. Specifically, inspired by the approach of learning the random variables (LRV)~\cite{BeckerJentzenMullerWurstemberger2024}, BQL incorporates learnable quadrature for Brownian increments at each time level into the backward recursion of BSDEs, enabling more efficient layerwise approximation of local conditional expectations. Furthermore, BQL introduces a continuation surrogate to facilitate the transfer of value-function information from subsequent to preceding time levels, avoiding nested quadrature while controlling the propagation of local approximation errors. Our main theoretical contribution is the derivation of a global error bound that explicitly characterizes the decomposition of the total error, together with a proof of first-order mean-square convergence under suitable approximation and integrability assumptions. Finally, numerical experiments demonstrate that BQL achieves competitive solution accuracy while substantially reducing the amortized computational cost per query. For the HJB benchmark across the tested dimensions, with $Q=7$ parameter queries, BQL achieves computational cost reductions of approximately 40-fold and 4-fold compared with P$^2$INN~[2] and FBSNN~[3], respectively.

papers.title: Elliptic hypergeometric sum/integrals for orthogonal groups and Seiberg duality on the lens space
papers.abstract: We derive new transformation formulas for elliptic hypergeometric sum/integrals associated with the orthogonal groups $\mathrm{SO}(N)$. The sum/integrals are written in terms of the lens elliptic gamma function, which depends on an integer $r\geq 1$ in addition to the usual complex variables, and they reduce to the elliptic hypergeometric integrals of Spiridonov and Vartanov for $r=1$. The derivation uses the $BC_n\leftrightarrow BC_{\tilde n}$ transformation formula proven in our previous paper, together with a duplication formula for the lens elliptic gamma function proven here. The duplication formula takes a different form depending on whether $r$ is even or odd. Physically, the new transformations show that the supersymmetric lens indices on $S^1\times S^3/\mathbb{Z}_r$ of the 4d $\mathcal{N}=1$ $\mathrm{SO}(N)$ and $\mathrm{SO}(N_f-N+4)$ gauge theories related by Seiberg duality are equal for odd $r$. For even $r$, where the lens index depends on the global form of the gauge group, they show the equality of the contributions from flat connections whose holonomies lie in a common maximal torus. The $BC_n$ formula itself gives the corresponding statement for the symplectic groups.

papers.title: Uniqueness of generalized conformal restriction measures
papers.abstract: We provide a new and unified approach (called the SLE arc test) for proving the uniqueness of generalized chordal and radial conformal restriction measures for $c\le 1$, where the $c<-2$ case is unknown before. This approach is inspired by the completely conformally invariant (CCI) measure introduced by Lawler and Werner (2000), and also by Cai's recent Green's function test for the Brownian loop catcher (2026).

papers.title: Combinatorial curvature flows for spherical vertex scalings on infinitely triangulated surfaces
papers.abstract: We study the combinatorial Yamabe and Calabi flows for spherical vertex scalings on infinitely triangulated surfaces. Under the assumptions of uniformly bounded vertex degree and an $ε$-uniformly nondegenerate initial metric, we establish the short-time existence of smooth solutions to both combinatorial curvature flows. We also establish short-time uniqueness for the combinatorial Yamabe flow. For the combinatorial Calabi flow, we establish short-time uniqueness among solutions that are continuous in time with respect to the $L^\infty(V)$ norm.

papers.title: Optimal radio labelings for the Cartesian product of a path and the Heawood graph
papers.abstract: For a simple graph $G$, let $d(u,v)$ denote the distance between two vertices $u$ and $v$ in $G$, and let $diam(G)$ denote the diameter of $G$. A radio labeling of $G$ is a mapping $f : V(G) \rightarrow \mathbb{N} \cup \{0\}$ such that $|f(u)-f(v)|\geq diam(G) + 1 - d(u,v)$ holds for every pair of distinct vertices $u, v \in G$. The span of $f$ is the difference between the largest and smallest integers assigned by $f$, and the radio number $rn(G)$ is the minimum span taking over all radio labelings of $G$. Let $P_n$ denote the path on $n$ vertices and let $H$ denote the Heawood graph (see Figure-1). In this paper we determine the radio number for the Cartesian product of a path and the Heawood graph, and characterize all optimal radio labelings of $P_n \Box H$. Moreover, we show that the radio number of $P_n \Box H$ exceed the lower bound given for $rn(G)$ in [6], where $G$ is any graph, and that this gap is arbitrarily large.

papers.title: C-embeddings of spaces of signed measures
papers.abstract: For a Tychonoff space $X$ let $M_a(X)\supset M_σ(X)\supset M_τ(X)\supset M_R(X)$ be the spaces of finitely additive, $σ$-additive (Baire), $τ$-additive and Radon signed measures on $X$, and let $M_β(X)$ and $M_d(X)$ be the spaces of compactly supported and discrete measures; all of them are regarded as subspaces of $M(βX)=C(βX)^*$ with the weak$^*$ topology. We study when $M_p(X)$ is $C$-embedded ($C^*$-embedded) in $M_q(X)$. We prove that $C$-embeddedness, $C^*$-embeddedness and $G_δ$-density of $M_p(X)$ in $M_q(X)$ are equivalent, and that they are equivalent to a lifting property: for every continuous map $f$ of $X$ into a metrizable compact space, the image of every probability measure in $M_q(X)$ is the image of a probability measure in $M_p(X)$. The main tool is a general theorem, proved in a separate paper, asserting that $C$-embeddedness, $C^*$-embeddedness and $G_δ$-density are equivalent for dense subspaces of locally convex spaces in the weak topology, and, more generally, of products of first-countable spaces. We characterize the spaces $X$ for which $M_σ(X)$, $M_β(X)$, $M_d(X)$ and $M_R(X)$ are $C$-embedded in $M_a(X)$ (pseudocompactness, pseudo-$ω$-boundedness, scatteredness of $βX$, and a lifting property of Radon measures, respectively). We give an example of a pseudocompact locally compact space $X$ for which $M_τ(X)$ is not $C^*$-embedded in $M_σ(X)$, and we show that $M_τ(X)$ is $C$-embedded in $M(βX)$ for every $G_δ$-dense subspace $X$ of a product of metrizable compact spaces. Using a set of universal measure zero, we construct a pseudocompact space $X$ for which $M_R(X)$ is $C$-embedded in $M(βX)$, although the restriction to $X$ of a coordinate projection onto $[0,1]$ maps no $σ$-compact subset of $X$ onto $[0,1]$.

papers.title: $\mathbb{R}$-linear unitary preservers of C$^*$-algebras
papers.abstract: We study the structure of general $\mathbb{R}$-linear unitary preservers between unital C$^*$-algebras. Representing any unital $\mathbb{R}$-linear unitary preserver in terms of three $\mathbb{R}$-linear maps on the self-adjoint part of the domain yields a canonical decomposition into a Jordan-type summand and a purely non-Jordan summand. When the domain is abelian, we completely classify the purely non-Jordan summand via type $\mathrm{I}_2$ JW-algebras. For unital C$^*$-algebras with no two-dimensional irreducible representations, we characterize a natural class of purely non-Jordan unitary preservers governed by pairs of Jordan $*$-homomorphisms.

papers.title: Rank Additivity and Comon's Conjecture for Real Hankel Tensors
papers.abstract: Let $\mathscr{H}_m(n)$ denote the set of real Hankel tensors of order $m$ and dimension $n$, and let $\textbf{H}\in\mathscr{H}_m(n)$, where $m\ge3$ and $n\ge1$. Set $M=(m-1)(n-1)+1$. First, we prove that the CP rank $r(\textbf{H})\le M$ and that CP rank is additive under direct sums of $\textbf{H}$ with any real tensor $\textbf{T}$ of the same order. Second, we prove that partially symmetric rank $p_j(\textbf{H})=r(\textbf{H})$ for $1\le j\le m-1$ and that, if $r(\textbf{H})\le M-1$, these ranks also equal its symmetric rank $s(\textbf{H})$. Third, we construct a fourth-order Hankel tensor $\textbf{H}_*\in\mathscr{H}_4(4)$ that attains this CP rank bound and satisfies $r(\textbf{H}_*)=10$ and $s(\textbf{H}_*)=11$. Moreover, for the direct sum $\textbf{H}_*^{(k)}=\bigoplus_{a=1}^k\textbf{H}_*$, we further prove that $r(\textbf{H}_*^{(k)})=10k$ and $s(\textbf{H}_*^{(k)})=11k$. This provides a low-dimensional counterexample to Comon's conjecture over the real numbers and further shows that the Comon rank gap is unbounded among real symmetric tensors of order four.

papers.title: On funnel control with star-shaped funnels
papers.abstract: Funnel control for the trivial control-affine prototype is extended to the case of star-shaped funnels, both in the special case that the dynamical system is formulated in an Euclidean space and the general case of a Riemannian manifold.

papers.title: Towards funnel control on Riemannian manifolds
papers.abstract: Funnel control for time-invariant control-affine systems with relative degree one is transferred to the case of dynamical systems evolving on a Riemannian manifold. It is shown that, under some regularity assumptions, the classical proofs carry over. The regularity assumptions reflect the particularities of the nonlinear theory and degenerate in the classical Euclidean case.

papers.title: Nonzero-Sum Stochastic Exit Games with Singular Belief Dynamics
papers.abstract: We study a two-player nonzero-sum stochastic exit game with asymmetric information. Each firm chooses the time to exit a duopoly and, conditional on remaining active, when to exit a monopoly. The asymmetry stems from privately observed exit values, while profit flows are driven by a general one-dimensional diffusion. Allowing for exit from monopoly induces singular dynamics of the associated belief process, so we construct it as a limit of regular approximations. The underlying dynamics are not described by a system of SDEs, which requires a new mathematical approach. We construct a symmetric Nash equilibrium in which the duopoly exit is a hitting time of the belief process while the monopoly exit is described through the underlying diffusion. Our equilibrium exhibits novel phenomena: the market may be abandoned by both firms in finite time (market collapse), and firms with heterogeneous exit values may optimally exit simultaneously (clustering). These features are absent when monopoly is always preferred to exit.

papers.title: Optimal Last-Iterate Bounds for Nonexpansive Stochastic Approximation
papers.abstract: We establish last-iterate mean-square residual bounds for nonexpansive stochastic approximation (SA), or stochastic Krasnoselskii-Mann (KM) iterations. In particular, we consider fixed-point mappings that are nonexpansive with respect to the Euclidean norm, and focus on polynomially decaying stepsizes. We study three conditions on the conditional second moment of the noise, and obtain bounds that are optimal up to logarithmic factors in each case. When it scales linearly with the squared residual, the best rate is $O(1/k^{1-ε})$ for any $ε>0$. In this case, for all considered stepsizes, our bounds match those of the noiseless KM iteration. When it is bounded by a constant, the best rate is $O(\log^2 k/\sqrt{k})$. When it scales affinely with the squared norm of the iterate, the best rate is $O(1/k^{1/2-ε})$, and the mean-square residual can diverge if the stepsizes are not square-summable. Thus, unlike for contractive SA, square-summable stepsizes are necessary for nonexpansive SA. We demonstrate how various algorithms with cocoercive maps, such as stochastic gradient descent, linear SA, and learning in cocoercive games, fit into our framework, and how the different noise conditions arise in each of them.

papers.title: Counting $K_4$-saturating non-edges in Nosal graphs
papers.abstract: A non-edge of a $K_4$-free graph is $K_4$-saturating if adding it creates a copy of $K_4$, and $f(G)$ counts these non-edges. Erdős and Tuza showed that the minimum of $f$ over $n$-vertex $K_4$-free graphs jumps from zero to a quadratic quantity once the number of edges exceeds $\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor$. Balogh and Liu [J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 109 (2014)] determined the asymptotic size of this jump. In this paper, we study the jump phenomenon at Nosal's spectral threshold $λ(G)>\sqrt m$, where $λ(G)$ is the spectral radius and $m$ is the number of edges. This spectral threshold does not involve the order, and its boundary contains unbalanced graphs far below the Mantel threshold. We prove that every $K_4$-free graph $G$ with $λ(G)>\sqrt m$ satisfies $f(G)+ \frac{1}{2}q(G)> \frac{1}{9} λ(G)^2$, where $q(G)$ counts the vertices in triangles. The constant $\frac{1}{9}$ is best possible, and the triangle-free case of this inequality reduces to Nosal's theorem. Consequently, the minimum of $f$ over $K_4$-free graphs with $m$ edges jumps from $0$ to $\frac19m+O(\sqrt m\,)$ at the Nosal threshold, and the error order $\sqrt m$ is best possible. For large $λ(G)$, we also prove $f(G)>\frac19λ(G)^2-\frac13λ(G)$, and graphs on the boundary $λ(G)^2=m$ attain this value. In the extremal graphs, the three edges of every triangle have booksizes in the ratio $4:1:1$, so these graphs are different from those of Balogh and Liu. We also show that the spectral Mantel condition $λ(G)>λ(T_{n,2})$ forces asymptotically fewer $K_4$-saturating non-edges than the condition $e(G)>\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor$. Our proof transfers the Balogh-Liu theorem through a weighted blow-up and replaces the choice of an extremal edge by a zero-sum comparison over all edges of a neighborhood.
papers.comments: 24 pages, 3 figures and 1 table. We proposed several spectral extremal problems for readers. Any suggestions are welcome

papers.title: A Moment Proof of the Hollman-Xiang Conjectures on Kloosterman Polynomials
papers.abstract: Let $F=\F_{2^n}$ and let \[ \mathcal T_1=\{t\in F:\Tr_{F/\F_2}(t)=1\}. \] For an integer $u=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}u_i2^i$ of even binary weight, put \[ L_u(X)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}u_iX^{2^i}, \qquad L_{1,u}(t)=t+L_u(t^{-1}). \] Hollmann and Xiang conjectured that $L_{1,u}$ permutes $\mathcal T_1$ if and only if $u\in\{0,3,6,10\}$. We prove the necessity by a moment method; the sufficiency is their Theorem~4.1. The quadratic moment yields a cyclic autocorrelation identity, while the cubic moment gives a two-variable group-algebra identity. An elimination argument reduces the coefficient word to a monomial or a complementary monomial, and explicit cubic and quartic moments complete the classification. We also prove Hollmann and Xiang's Conjecture~4.5. Namely, if $n>3$ and \[ L_{c,d}(x)=L_c(x)+L_d(x^{-1}) \] is a Kloosterman polynomial on $\F_{2^n}$, then its positive linearized part $L_c$ is injective on both trace fibers. This second result follows from relative quadratic and cubic moment identities and a spectral-zero rigidity argument. Consequently every Kloosterman polynomial is obtained by composing one of $L_{1,0},L_{1,3},L_{1,6},L_{1,10}$ with a linearized map that is injective on both trace fibers.

papers.title: Existence and Splitting of Dirac Points in Honeycomb Gyromagnetic Photonic Crystals
papers.abstract: We establish the existence of Dirac cones and magnetically induced local band gaps for the transverse magnetic Maxwell system in a two-dimensional honeycomb array of circular yttrium iron garnet (YIG) cylinders. For fixed positive material parameters with nonzero permeability contrast, we prove that sufficiently small cylinders support a Dirac point in the nonmagnetic case $κ_g=0$: two Bloch dispersion surfaces meet at a double eigenfrequency and form a nondegenerate cone. For each fixed sufficiently small nonzero gyrotropic bias $κ_g$, we show that this degeneracy splits and a local band gap opens near the original Dirac point. Our approach combines a quasi-periodic layer-potential formulation with honeycomb symmetry and rigorously controlled finite-dimensional reductions. The central contribution is a unified derivation of the conical crossing and magnetic gap opening directly from the full Maxwell transmission problem, without assuming an effective discrete model. This establishes the transition from Dirac dispersion to a locally gapped spectrum in a small-inclusion regime with fixed material contrast.

papers.title: Morse index and bifurcation of Clifford hypersurfaces under Hopf squashing
papers.abstract: Clifford hypersurfaces are products of two spheres embedded in a round sphere. We call them balanced when their radii are chosen so that the product is minimal in the round metric. We study how their Morse index and nullity change when the ambient metric is deformed along the fibers of a Hopf fibration. This deformation, called \emph{Hopf squashing}, rescales the fiber metric by a parameter $t>0$ while leaving the horizontal metric unchanged. For the complex, quaternionic, and octonionic Hopf fibrations, we determine the index and nullity of balanced Clifford hypersurfaces throughout the fiber-shortening range and show that their Jacobi potential is independent of $t$. In the octonionic case we also determine the first positive Jacobi eigenvalue and its multiplicity. In the octonionic case, at $t=27$, a branch of nonhomogeneous minimal hypersurfaces bifurcates from the balanced Clifford hypersurface; its members have Morse index $1432$ and nullity $15$.

papers.title: C*-embeddings of spaces of probability measures, nonnegative measures and unit balls
papers.abstract: For a Tychonoff space $X$ and $p\in\{d,β,R,τ,σ,a\}$ let $M_p(X)$ be the space of discrete, compactly supported, Radon, $τ$-additive, $σ$-additive or finitely additive signed measures on $X$, regarded as a subspace of $M(βX)=C(βX)^*$ with the weak$^*$ topology, and let $M^+_p(X)$, $U_p(X)$ and $P_p(X)$ be its subsets of nonnegative measures, measures of norm at most one, and probability measures. In the companion paper it was shown that $M_p(X)$ is $C$-embedded in $M_q(X)$ iff it is $C^*$-embedded iff it is $G_δ$-dense. We show that $G_δ$-density of $Q_p(X)$ in $Q_q(X)$ is the same condition for all $Q\in\{M,M^+,U,P\}$, and that $C^*$-embedding of $Q_p(X)$ in $Q_q(X)$ implies $G_δ$-density, while the converse fails for $Q\in\{M^+,U,P\}$. We prove that $M^+_p(X)$ is $C^*$-embedded in $M^+(βX)$ iff $P_p(X)$ is $C^*$-embedded in $P(βX)$, that pseudocompactness of $P_p(X)$ implies pseudocompactness of all its powers, and that the unit ball $U_R(X)$ is $C^*$-embedded in $U(βX)$ iff $P_R(X)$ is pseudocompact. If $βX$ is $κ$-metrizable (e.g., a product of metrizable compact spaces or a compact group), then pseudocompactness of $P_p(X)$ and the $C^*$-embeddings of $P_p(X)$, $U_p(X)$ and $M^+_p(X)$ in $P(βX)$, $U(βX)$ and $M^+(βX)$ are equivalent to the $C$-embedding of $M_p(X)$ in $M(βX)$. Consequently, $P_τ(X)$ is pseudocompact for every pseudocompact dense subspace $X$ of a Tychonoff cube. This gives a space $X$ for which $P_τ(X)$ is pseudocompact while the space $P_R(X)$ of Radon probability measures is not, and answers a question of the first author.
papers.comments: 20 pages; companion paper to "C-embeddings of spaces of signed measures"

papers.title: A Second Order Extended Zarankiewicz Number for Biquadratic SOS Rank
papers.abstract: We introduce the \emph{second order extended Zarankiewicz number} $z_{2M}(m,n)$, obtained from the second order Zarankiewicz number $z_2(m,n)$ of Löfberg and Qi by relaxing the simplicity condition $(S)$ for the \emph{secondary halves} of 2-edges, while keeping the limited condition $|E_1|=z(m,n)$. We prove the hierarchy $$ BSR(m,n)\ge z_{2M}(m,n)\ge z_2(m,n)\ge z_{SL}(m,n)\ge z_{RL}(m,n)\ge z_{wL}(m,n)\ge z(m,n), $$ and show that $z_{2M}$ is not capped by the universal cell bound. We prove the counting bound $z_{2M}(m,n)\le mn-1$, and a sharper linear-in-$m$ bound for fixed $n$ obtained from orthogonality of coefficient vectors. We analyse how the recursive criterion $(RW3^{+})$ of Löfberg and Qi must be modified under $(S_M)$, prove soundness of the resulting $(RW3^{+}_M)$ for multiplicity-one sharing, and show that a signed sharing closure $(SC)$ can supplement but not replace it. We prove $$ z_{2M}(21,4)\ge 56>55=z_2(21,4). $$ The witness is an explicit $56$-edge $(S_M)$-admissible configuration, and its irreducibility is certified by a full-rank system of $2255$ linear equations in the $1540$ off-diagonal inner products. This reaches Marin's lower bound $BSR(21,4)\ge 56$.

papers.title: From Complex Regularization to Polynomial Flow: Capture and Escape in Rocking Dynamics
papers.abstract: We develop a planar polynomial system based on a complex regularization of free rocking and analyze the equilibrium states and phase portraits via an effective radial potential. The conflict between the centrifugal effect, which is introduced by means of regularization, and gravity yields a potential well and an escape barrier for 0 < beta < 27/256; both vanish at a saddle-node bifurcation point. The exact energy conservation law allows us to separate dissipative relaxation, conservative periodic motions along the radial direction, and energy creating trajectories. The node-focus boundary of finite equilibria is different from the degeneracy condition for compactification at infinity. As the last step of analysis, we reconstruct the complex phase portrait and discover that a stable radial equilibrium corresponds to a relative equilibrium in the regularized dynamics, whereas the reconstruction of an impact dynamics requires taking a singular limit.

papers.title: Frames Associated with $C_0$-Semigroups
papers.abstract: A central question in dynamical frame theory asks when the orbit $\{Λ^n f\}_{n\in\mathbb{Z}_+}$ of a vector $f$ under a bounded operator $Λ$ on a separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space $H$ is a frame. Christensen, Hasannasab and Philipp answered it, showing in particular that such an operator must be similar to the compression of the unilateral shift on $H^2(\mathbb{T})$ to a coinvariant subspace. We prove a continuous analogue: if a $C_0$-semigroup $\{T(t)\}_{t\ge0}\subset B(H)$ generates a continuous frame $\{T(t)\varphi\}_{t\ge0}$, then the operators $T(t)$ are simultaneously similar to the compressions of the shift semigroup to a fixed coinvariant subspace. Moreover, $\{T(t)\varphi\}_{t\ge0}$ is a continuous frame if and only if $\{C^n(I-A)^{-1}\varphi\}_{n\in\mathbb{Z}_+}$ is a frame, where $A$ is the infinitesimal generator and $C=(I+A)(I-A)^{-1}$ the cogenerator; the frame bounds of the two systems differ by a factor $2$. We also derive necessary conditions for the existence of frame vectors and discuss several examples. Finally, we show that the compressed shift on a model space $K_θ$ is the cogenerator of a $C_0$-semigroup admitting frame vectors if and only if the inner function $θ$ has a finite angular derivative at $1$; in that case we describe all frame vectors, and the boundary reproducing kernel at $1$ generates a tight continuous frame.

papers.title: LongTails: Automated Research in Optimization
papers.abstract: We introduce LongTails, a framework for discovering and improving oracle-complexity bounds with formal verification in Lean 4. Using LongTails, we have already obtained more than 100 new results across a broad range of optimization problems, including generalized smoothness, heavy-tailed noise, finite-sum and composite optimization, and higher-order and zeroth-order methods. Our goal is to scale discovery and continually develop new methods with non-trivial and valuable theoretical guarantees using modern agentic systems. The framework is specialized for optimization, where we separate a Setup, specifying the problem class, assumptions, available information, and success criterion, from a Complexity, specifying a sufficient oracle-call budget. Once a Setup is fixed (e.g., $L$-smooth convex optimization with the goal of finding $x_{\mathrm{out}}$ such that $f(x_{\mathrm{out}}) - f(x^\star) \leq \varepsilon$), agents search for better Complexities (e.g., $O(\sqrt{L R^2 / \varepsilon})$, where $R \geq \|x_0 - x^\star\|$) by designing algorithms and proving their convergence. The framework then checks the proofs and guarantees that every accepted Complexity can indeed be attained under the given Setup. This turns the search for new methods into an ongoing effort to improve their theoretical guarantees. To the best of our knowledge, LongTails is the first framework to scale automated research in optimization across such a broad range of problems with formally verified theoretical guarantees.

papers.title: Non-abelian $p$-adic Hodge theory and stacks
papers.abstract: In the first half of these notes, we survey some aspects of the stack-theoretic perspective on $p$-adic Hodge theory, with an emphasis on the non-abelian aspects. In the second half, we report ongoing joint work on ``quantizing'' non-abelian $p$-adic Hodge theory.
papers.comments: Notes accompanying the Takagi Lectures in June 2026; 47 pages

papers.title: Weak Quasi-Convexity: First- and Second-Order Conditions, Monotonicity, and Quadratic Functions
papers.abstract: In this paper we introduce weakly quasi-convex functions, which are a generalization of weakly convex functions. We study the behavior of weakly quasi-convex functions in Euclidean spaces. We provide several illustrative examples that demonstrate the scope and distinctive features of this new class of generalized convex functions. We derive a necessary condition for weak quasi-convexity under certain assumptions and provide an example showing that its converse is not true for discontinuous functions. Under the continuity assumption on the function involved, a sufficient condition is provided with an adjusted weak quasi-convexity modulus. Also, we bring out various kinds of monotonicity in connection with weakly quasi-convex functions through the gradient mapping. We provide several illustrative examples that interpret and emphasize the newly introduced notions. We establish a first-order necessary condition for the class of differentiable weakly quasi-convex functions. Conversely, we show that a differentiable function satisfying this first-order condition is weakly quasi-convex with an adjusted modulus. We provide a second-order necessary condition under appropriate assumptions using second-order Dini derivatives. As a consequence, we derive a Hessian-based necessary condition for the class of twice continuously differentiable weakly quasi-convex functions. We provide an example to show that the converse of the second-order characterization does not hold. Furthermore, we establish various kinds of necessary conditions concerning general quadratic functions and provide many counterexamples for the failure of their sufficiency. Finally, we derive several consequences of weak quasi-convexity for optimization problems.

papers.title: Congruences for Dedekind numbers
papers.abstract: We study congruence properties of Dedekind numbers $d_n$. Our approach relies on actions of $p$-subgroups of symmetric groups on posets of monotone functions and leads to the congruences $d_{10}\equiv 106\pmod{210}$, $d_{11}\equiv 117\pmod{210}$, and $d_{12}\equiv 12\pmod{30}$. In particular, $d_{11}$ is odd, confirming a claim stated by Yamamoto without a proof.

papers.title: E-symmetric algebras II
papers.abstract: We introduce generalized Jacobian algebras and show that a finite-dimensional algebra is E-symmetric if and only if it is generalized Jacobian. We also characterize E-symmetric algebras in terms of its simple modules. We show that Enomoto's counterexample to the Periodicity Conjecture is a generalized Jacobian algebra, which is not Jacobian in the classical sense.

papers.title: Face lattices of polytopes and bipolar polytopes
papers.abstract: We show that the face lattice of every convex polytope $Q$ is, on the combinatorial level, the vertex set of a polytope one dimension higher: the faces of $Q$ are the vertices of a \emph{bipolar polytope} $W(\mathcal{F}(Q))$, and the intervals of the face lattice are its faces. Here a bipolar polytope is a polytope with two distinguished vertices, the poles, such that every facet contains exactly one of them and an intersection property holds. The vertices of every bipolar polytope carry a lattice order whose intervals are the faces, and this lattice is the face lattice of the vertex figure at either pole; conversely, every atomistic and coatomistic lattice that is an abstract polytope arises in this way. Geometrically, the polar of the Cayley polytope of $Q$ and $Q^\circ$ is a convex realization of $W(\mathcal{F}(Q))$ whenever the normal fan and the face fan of $Q$ satisfy a certain interval condition; this holds for cubes and cross-polytopes and for suitable realizations of all polytopes of dimension at most three. Finally, every combinatorial type of $3$-polytope has a realization that decomposes into convex bipolar polytopes, one for each vertex.
papers.comments: 30 pages, 6 Figures, to be submitted in Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series A

papers.title: On the strong Dixmier-Moeglin equivalence for the quantum semisimple groups
papers.abstract: The Dixmier-Moeglin equivalence, when it holds for an algebra, characterizes its primitive ideals ( that is, the annihilators of irreducible representations) both algebraically and topologically within the prime spectrum. A stronger form, known as the strong Dixmier-Moeglin equivalence, was introduced by Bell, Launois, and Nolan in their work on 'A strong Dixmier-Moeglin equivalence for quantum Schubert cells'. In this paper, we prove that the generic quantized coordinate rings of connected, simply connected semisimple complex algebraic groups satisfy the strong Dixmier-Moeglin equivalence.

papers.title: Switching reconstruction of signed graphs: net-degree and balance
papers.abstract: The switching reconstruction problem for $2$-edge-colored graphs, introduced by Bondy and Mercier, asks whether such a graph is determined up to isomorphism by the multiset of the graphs obtained by exchanging the colors of the edges at each vertex; for complete underlying graphs it is the vertex-switching reconstruction problem of Stanley. We study this problem in the language of signed graphs, where the net-degree of a vertex and the notion of balance come naturally into play. We prove that a signed graph on $n\neq4$ vertices is reconstructible when its net-degrees are all positive, all negative or all zero, which generalizes the reconstructibility of regular graphs in Stanley's problem. For connected balanced signed graphs, whose switching reconstruction problem we show to be equivalent to that of connected graphs with a distinguished bipartition of the vertex set, we prove reconstructibility when the two parts of the bipartition differ in size by more than two, and when all net-degrees are non-negative.

papers.title: Thermodynamic Formalism for Non-Invariant Probabilities: Entropy, Divergence, Channels
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{M}$ and $\mathcal{M}_σ$ denote, respectively, the sets of Borel and $σ$-invariant probabilities on the uncountable set $Ω=\{1,2,...,d\}^\mathbb{N}$. Given a Hölder Jacobian $J$, the dual Ruelle operator $μ\in \mathcal{M} \mapsto \mathcal{L}_{J}^* (μ)$ will play the role of a dynamical channel; generalizes the action of a stochastic matrix on probability vectors. Since $\mathcal{L}_{J}^*$ generally breaks $σ$-invariance, we introduce the \emph{ni-entropy} $h_{ni}(μ)$ for non-invariant measures, employing the concept of the expected value function on cylinders of size one. $h_{ni}(μ)$ differs from Shannon entropy but extends the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy from $\mathcal{M}_σ$ to $\mathcal{M}$; $h_{ni}$ is concave and u.s.c. This leads us to the concept of ni-pressure $\mathcal{P}(A)$ of a potential $A:Ω\to \mathbb{R}$. $μ\in \mathcal{M}$ is not a density with respect to a dominating measure. We define an {\it ni-Kullback-Leibler divergence} $D_{ni}(ρ|| ν)$ not assuming absolute continuity. We investigate concepts of Information Theory such as Minimal Output Entropy, Donsker-Varadhan variational principle, a variational formula for $h_{ni}$, bounds for divergence, information projections, and their connections to the ni-pressure $\mathcal{P}$.

papers.title: An Accelerated Dynamic Stochastic Primal-Dual Method for Multi-stage Stochastic Optimization
papers.abstract: We consider multi-stage stochastic optimization problems with smooth convex stage costs and linear linking constraints. Dynamic stochastic approximation (DSA), a stochastic first-order method, uses a recursive structure whose memory requirement grows only linearly with the number of stages. Its implementation, however, requires an exact solution of the proximal subproblem associated with the stage cost, and this subproblem often admits no closed-form solution. To resolve this issue, we develop an accelerated dynamic stochastic primal-dual (A-DSPD) framework that retains the recursive value-function structure and only requires the gradient of the stage cost. Within this framework, each stagewise saddle-point subproblem is solved by an inexact accelerated stochastic primal-dual method (iASPD), which applies Nesterov acceleration to the smooth stage cost and uses recursively generated stochastic $ε$-subgradients for the nonsmooth downstream value function. For the stochastic composite saddle-point problem, after $N$ primal-dual updates, iASPD yields optimality and feasibility bounds in which the contribution of the smooth stage cost decays at a faster rate $O(1/N^2)$, while the terms associated with stochastic $ε$-subgradients of the nonsmooth value function decay as $O(1/\sqrt{N})$, up to the prescribed oracle inexactness. We also develop bounds for the stochastic $ε$-subgradient estimators and the dual iterates, which yield complexity guarantees for A-DSPD. Specifically, A-DSPD computes an $ε$-solution using $O(1/ε^4)$ sampled scenarios and $O(1/ε^5)$ primal-dual updates for three-stage problems. We further extend the method and its convergence analysis to problems with an arbitrary finite number of stages. Numerical experiments on three-stage stochastic portfolio models illustrate the empirical advantage of the proposed method.

papers.title: Connectivity and the equilibration of Boltzmann-type equations on dense graphs
papers.abstract: We investigate the equilibration of solutions to a homogeneous Boltzmann-type equation whose collision kernel is given by a graphon encoding the connectivity structure of interacting agents. For a broad class of Lipschitz-continuous binary interaction rules, we show that, under suitable conditions relating the interaction parameters to the connectivity properties of the graphon, solutions converge exponentially fast towards those of the classical homogeneous Boltzmann-type equation without preferential connections, and hence towards its equilibrium distributions. We then consider in detail compromise-diffusion interaction rules and establish a quasi-invariant limit leading to a Fokker-Planck-type equation parametrised by the graphon connectivity. This limiting equation allows us to characterise explicitly both connectivity-independent and connectivity-dependent equilibrium distributions.

papers.title: The Role of Insurance in Power-System Risk Management: A Critical Review
papers.abstract: Modern power systems are becoming more renewable-rich, digitalized, and interconnected, making risk propagation and economic consequences increasingly complex. Physical mitigation remains the primary means of risk control, but technical and economic limits leave residual risk. Insurance can complement these measures by transferring associated economic losses and influencing power-system decisions through risk-responsive terms. Despite growing interest, the literature remains fragmented across power-system engineering, actuarial science, and risk finance. This review develops an integrated physical-financial perspective for reviewing insurance in power systems. It examines how power system risks generate residual economic losses and the conditions under which these losses can be insured and transferred. It then develops an actuarial framework for insured-loss assessment and pricing. Insurance-aware decision-making is synthesized through four coupling levels describing how financial protection interacts with power-system decisions. Further progress is constrained by weak physical-financial loss validation, incomplete representation of systemic and evolving portfolio risk, and limited empirical and actuarial grounding of insurance-decision feedback. Research priorities include stronger physical-financial data linkage, forward-looking portfolio assessment, multi-timescale decision feedback, and empirical validation. Addressing these priorities would help move power-system insurance from fragmented applications toward a more coherent approach to residual-risk management in future power systems.

papers.title: Pólya's conjecture for hyperbolic balls and Berezin--Li--Yau type inequalities
papers.abstract: We prove the strict shifted Dirichlet Pólya inequality \[ λ_k(B_R)>\frac{(d-1)^2κ^2}{4}+4π^2\left(\frac{k}{ω_d\operatorname{Vol}_κ(B_R)}\right)^{2/d},\qquad k\ge1, \] for every geodesic ball $B_R$ in hyperbolic space of constant sectional curvature $-κ^2$, in every dimension $d\ge2$. As a consequence, we obtain the shifted Berezin--Li--Yau type inequality for hyperbolic balls, thereby providing a concrete family of domains satisfying both conjectures proposed by Laptev in 2023. For arbitrary nonempty open subsets $Ω\subset\mathbb{H}^d_κ$ of finite volume, we establish the weak Berezin--Li--Yau type inequality \[ \sum_{j=1}^{m}λ_j(Ω)\ge a_{d,κ}m+\frac{d}{d+2}\,4π^2\left(\frac{m}{ω_d\operatorname{Vol}_κ(Ω)}\right)^{2/d}m,\qquad m\ge1, \] with the optimal leading coefficient, where $a_{2,κ}=κ^2/4$ and $a_{d,κ}=d(d-1)κ^2/6$ for $d\ge3$. We also establish the global two-sided estimate for the renormalized eigenvalue sum on hyperbolic space, originally proposed by Strichartz in 1996 and valid for $d\ge3$.

papers.title: Dual-Space Preconditioning for Variational Inequalities and Root-Finding Problems
papers.abstract: This paper develops a dual-space preconditioning framework for variational inequalities and root-finding problems beyond classical cocoercivity and Lipschitz continuity assumptions. To this end, we introduce both a novel cocoercivity-type condition and a relaxed Lipschitz continuity condition, and derive convergence of deterministic and stochastic methods under these generalized conditions. For isotropic preconditioners, the resulting algorithms can be interpreted as variable-stepsize variants of classical methods, extending recent analyses based on $(L_0, L_1)$-type growth conditions while allowing simpler proofs and larger stepsize ranges. We also show that the framework naturally handles variational inequalities through weak Minty-type arguments. Finally, we study the associated continuous-time dynamics and derive a variational and optimal control interpretation of the preconditioned flow. Overall, the results show that dual-space preconditioning provides a flexible mechanism for designing and analyzing operator methods beyond the standard Euclidean Lipschitz setting.

papers.title: Generalized Frobenius manifolds: symmetries and their classification in 2-dimensions
papers.abstract: A theory of symmetries of generalized Frobenius manifolds is developed. This is used to study the solution space of all generalized Frobenius manifolds that are "above" a specific Frobenius manifold. Since all (semi-simple) Frobenius manifolds in 2-dimensions are known, by constructing all homogeneous Legendre fields associated to these manifolds we classify all 2-dimensional generalized Frobenius manifolds. With this description, the known examples of generalized Frobenius manifolds correspond to distinguished points in this solution space. For Hurwitz-Frobenius manifolds the action of a Legendre transformation on Hurwitz space data, and in particular the primary differential, is given.

papers.title: An Equivariant Coarse Green-Julg Theorem for Proper Actions
papers.abstract: We prove an equivariant coarse Green--Julg theorem for proper isometric actions of countable discrete groups on bounded geometry metric spaces. We introduce the $(Γ, X)$-controlled proper $C^{*}$-algebra, and show that the evaluation-at-zero map between the equivariant localization and Roe algebras with such coefficients induces an isomorphism on $K$-theory.

papers.title: Asymptotic Bayes Optimality of Sparse Multiple Testing Procedures under One-Factor Dependence
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study sparse multiple testing under a Gaussian two-group model with known one-factor covariance and centered Gaussian signals. We derive a first-order risk expansion for the observed-data Bayes Oracle, including a finite-dimensional loading average for heterogeneous loadings and an explicit limiting constant for homogeneous loadings. Under the stated factor-estimation and signal-calibration conditions, the homogeneous one-factor Oracle has strictly smaller leading risk than its independent-coordinate counterpart; observing the latent factor yields no further first-order reduction. We establish asymptotic Bayes optimality under sparsity (ABOS) for the Maximum Residual Down (MRD) step-down procedure with Gavrilov--Benjamini--Sarkar (GBS) stagewise calibration (MRD--GBS). Uniform control of residual errors along the rejection path permits comparison with a fixed factor-known rule without requiring the rejection paths to coincide. Fixed-residual versions of GBS and Benjamini--Hochberg (BH) attain the same leading risk. We also prove ABOS for the Bayesian Step-Down (BSD) rule when supplied with the true mixture, signal variance, covariance, and loss parameters; this is an Oracle-parameterized result. When the expected signal count grows faster than the logarithm of the reciprocal signal proportion, BSD and the observed-data Oracle disagree on several coordinates negligible in probability relative to the expected signal count, explaining BSD's near-Oracle behavior in companion simulations. The results cover diverging and bounded positive expected signal counts, including every fixed polynomial sparsity rate up to the bounded-count regime, under the stated calibrations. A fixed-dimension simulation illustrates absolute-risk behavior but does not establish ABOS.

papers.title: Lengthscale Estimation for the Gaussian Kernel and Deterministic Response Functions
papers.abstract: The uncertainty estimates Gaussian processes output rely on the chosen covariance kernel and its hyperparameters. We study the fixed-domain asymptotics of the maximum likelihood and cross-validation estimators of the lengthscale parameter of the popular infinitely smooth Gaussian kernel when the observations are produced by a fixed univariate response function. No theoretical results for Gaussian lengthscale estimation exist in this setting. We prove lower bounds on the lengthscale estimators that depend on the regularity of the response function, as measured by the rate of decay of its Fourier transform. If the response function lives in the Hilbert space of the Gaussian kernel with lengthscale $\ell$, the lower bounds have a straightforward dependency on $\ell$. For bandlimited functions and functions whose Fourier transforms decay as $\exp(-a \lvert ω\rvert^γ)$ for $a > 0$ and $γ> 2$, we prove that the estimators blow up essentially at least as fast as $(\log n)^{(γ-2)/(2γ)}$ in the number of data points, $n$. Bandlimited functions are identified with $γ= \infty$. Unlike analogous results for finitely smooth Matérn kernels, our results make no assumptions on the geometry of the observation points. Numerical experiments illustrate the results.

papers.title: Transforms between multivariate Laguerre and Meixner polynomials and their applications to gateways
papers.abstract: We establish gateways in both directions between the Laguerre process and a discrete Markov process for every inverse temperature $2θ\geq 1$. Here, a gateway is an intertwining relation between Markov processes with continuous and discrete state spaces. A key ingredient is a pair of generating function identities that relate two double generating functions for multivariate Meixner polynomials to a single and a double generating function for multivariate Laguerre polynomials, respectively. These identities reveal a close relationship between the two families of polynomials and yield integral transforms that underlie the gateway relations. Gateway relations provide a means of transferring properties between continuous and discrete processes. As an application, we derive the Feller-Dynkin property and the uniqueness of the invariant distribution for the Laguerre process from the corresponding properties of the discrete process.

papers.title: Phase transitions and sharp localisation in anomalous localised resonance
papers.abstract: We study how detuning and absorption determine the strength and spatial extent of anomalous localised resonance in a two-dimensional quasistatic coated structure with shell permittivity $-1+c\ell^p+i\ell$, where $\ell>0$ is the loss and $c\ne0$, $p>0$ are fixed. Detuning can carry the material path through narrow resonances, producing intermittent rather than sustained power growth. For an explicit family of noncircular shells and a smooth exterior dipole source, both fixed, we classify the dissipated power under a quantitative smallness condition on the deformation. Depending on the detuning exponent and conformal source distance, the power diverges along the entire path, exhibits divergent peaks with vanishing gaps, or decays, including the threshold cases. We also identify the sharp conformal boundary beyond which the field, normalized by the square root of the dissipated power, converges locally to zero along every divergent-power sequence. For resonant sources, tangential reference crossings yield an explicit nonzero limit for the exterior gradient energy divided by the dissipated power at the critical radius.

papers.title: On Monotonicity in Mean Field Games Induced by Discount Factor Transformations
papers.abstract: This paper is devoted to the well-posedness of a class of infinite horizon discounted Mean Field Games (MFGs) problems, where both an exponential discount and a so-called cheap control factors are present simultaneously, and scale in a possibly different way. We introduce a new class of transformations of variables, at the level of both the MFG PDE and the corresponding FBSDE systems. We then show how these transformations reveal a new mechanism that generates semiconvexity estimates for the value function and ensures the existence of mean field equilibria, as long as the parameters land in a suitable regime, that we quantitatively describe. This new mechanism demonstrates furthermore how discount factors lead to a source of strong displacement monotonicity for the Lagrangian, without any initial monotonicity assumptions on the running costs. Consequently, in such regimes of parameters uniqueness of solutions manifests. Our approach uses a Lagrangian point of view, which lets us treat general non-separable Lagrangians and both deterministic and idiosyncratic noise driven models in a transparent, unified way. For a specific class of quadratic Lagrangians, using turnpike-type methods, we further obtain an exponential contractivity estimate for the mean field equilibria.

papers.title: An additively idempotent semiring of least order generating a limit variety
papers.abstract: We construct an additively idempotent semiring of order five that generates a limit variety and is not strongly nonfinitely based. The generated variety has exactly two maximal proper subvarieties, both hereditarily finitely based. We also prove that no ai-semiring of order at most four generates a limit variety. Consequently, five is the least possible order of a finite ai-semiring generating a limit variety.

papers.title: Gelfand-Kirillov dimension of constants of algebraic $q$-skew derivations
papers.abstract: Let $δ$ be an algebraic $q$-skew $σ$-derivation of an algebra $R$ over a field of arbitrary characteristic, where $σ$ is an algebraic automorphism of $R$, and let $R^δ$ be the algebra of constants of $δ$. We show that $GKdim(R) = GKdim(R^δ)$ whenever $R$ is semiprime and $R^δ$ is a PI algebra containing no infinite direct sum of nonzero ideals. The polynomial identity cannot be dropped. For every $r \geq 1$ we construct a primitive algebra $R$ with an inner derivation $d$ such that $d^{3} = 0$, $GKdim(R) \geq 2r$ and $GKdim(R^{d}) = 0$, while $R^{d}$ contains no direct sum of two nonzero ideals.

papers.title: Automorphisms of the Reduced Finitary Power Monoid of $\N^d$
papers.abstract: Given an additive semigroup $S$, the collection of its nonempty finite subsets can be equipped with the setwise addition \[ X + Y = \{x + y : x \in X, \; y \in Y\}, \] forming a semigroup denoted by $\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{fin}}(S)$, which is called the finitary power semigroup of $S$. If $S$ is a monoid with identity $0$, the finite nonempty subsets containing $0$ form a submonoid $\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{fin},0}(S)$, known as the reduced finitary power monoid, whose identity element is the singleton $\{0\}$. Let $d$ be a positive integer, $\mathbb{N}$ the set of nonnegative integers, and $\mathbb{N}^d = \{(a_1, a_2, \dots, a_d) \mid a_i \in \mathbb{N}\}$. For the one-dimensional case \(d=1\), Tringali and Yan (\textit{J. Comb. Theory, Ser. A}, \textbf{209} (2025)) established that the only nontrivial automorphism of $\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{fin},0}(\mathbb{N})$ is the involution $X \mapsto \max X - X$. In this paper, we focus on the higher-dimensional case $d \ge 2$.
