Numerical experiments confirm the fourth-order accuracy for a range of reaction-diffusion problems with Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions, and demonstrate that it outperforms existing standard ETD methods in serial and parallel implementations, yielding CPU time reductions of up to a factor of 20.

papers.title: The distribution of small gaps between zeros of the Riemann zeta function
papers.abstract: Let $0<γ_1\leq γ_2\leq \cdots$ be the ordinates of the non-trivial zeros $ρ_n$ of the Riemann zeta function in the upper half-plane, counted with multiplicity. Selberg proved unconditionally that there exists $λ_0<1$ such that a positive proportion of the zeros $ρ_n$ satisfy $γ_{n+1}-γ_n\leq 2πλ_0/\log γ_n$. Simonič, Trudgian and Turnage-Butterbaugh were the first to obtain an explicit value in Selberg's theorem, showing that $λ_0=1- 10^{-3\cdot 10^{13}}$ is admissible. This was considerably improved by Zhao who showed that $λ_0= 1-2.36\cdot 10^{-6}$ is admissible. In this paper, we use a different approach, based on an unconditional variant of Montgomery's pair correlation method, to obtain a substantial improvement of these results, showing unconditionally that $λ_0=0.7892<4/5$ is admissible.

papers.title: Automatic Continuity for projective clone homomorphisms
papers.abstract: We show that every projective clone homomorphism from a closed function clone containing the automorphism group of a countable homogeneous Ramsey structure $Δ$ in a finite relational language is uniformly continuous. This answers, for such structures, open questions previously raised by Barto, Bodirsky, Marimon, Pongrácz, and the second author in several papers (Bodirsky, Pinsker, Pongrácz, J. Symb. Log. 2021; Barto, Pinsker, SIAM J. Comput. 2020; Marimon, Pinsker, arXiv:2512.01086). Consequently, the polymorphism clone of a first-order reduct $Γ$ of $Δ$ admits a projective clone homomorphism if and only if $Γ$ primitively positively interprets all finite structures; in other words, this ability of $Γ$ is characterised by the absence of non-trivial identities in its polymorphism clone, a purely algebraic condition.sence of non-trivial identities in its polymorphism clone, i.e., a purely algebraic condition.

papers.title: Dynamic linear equations in the presence of small perturbations of an interface
papers.abstract: We consider solutions to the initial boundary value problems for both heat and wave equations in two dimensions. In this paper, we aim to advance the development of high-order terms in the asymptotic expansions of current boundary perturbations caused by small perturbations of the shape of a $C^2$-boundary inhomogeneity. Our derivations are rigorously derived by the field expansion (FE) method (formal derivation) and proved by layer potential techniques. It extends those already derived for small-volume inhomogeneities to develop efficient algorithms for determining certain properties of the shape of an inhomogeneity based on boundary measurements.

papers.title: Excess charge in the Engel-Dreizler model of atoms and molecules
papers.abstract: We prove an explicit excess-charge bound for the exchange-free Engel--Dreizler functional of atoms and molecules. If $αλ\le1/1233$ and $α^3Z_k^2\le1/137$ for each nucleus, every finite-mass electronic minimizer whose total energy, including nuclear repulsion, is nonpositive satisfies $N-\sum_kZ_k<(5913/1000)λ^{3/2}K$. For the gradient coefficient $λ=1/9$, this gives $N-\sum_kZ_k<0.219K$. The energy hypothesis holds automatically for atoms and for local minima of the Born--Oppenheimer energy at which the electronic infimum is attained. The proof uses no symmetry of the density, restriction on the total nuclear charge, or minimum nuclear separation. We combine molecular Sommerfeld estimates with a convex nonlinear comparison in the variable $F(p)$. The failure of the latter comparison at very high density is represented by a nonnegative Newton potential. A quartic coercivity estimate, obtained from nuclear repulsion and a signed localized Hardy inequality, controls the total mass of this source. The chemical potential is retained throughout. Exact covariance yields the invariant parameter domain, and all finite numerical inequalities are reduced to rational arithmetic.

papers.title: The expected number of holes of the planar Wiener sausage
papers.abstract: ```text Let $β_1^T(r)$ be the number of holes, that is, the first Betti number, of the Wiener sausage of radius $r$ of a planar Brownian motion run up to time $T$. We prove that $\mathbb{E}[β_1^T(r)]$ is of order $T/(r^2(\log T)^2)$ as $T\to\infty$, for each fixed $r>0$, which completes the lower bound obtained in a companion paper from a law for the inradii of the cavities of the path. We also identify which parts of the complement of the path contribute at leading order. At unit time and radius $\varepsilon$, the holes lying in the unbounded component of the complement have expected number $O(\varepsilon^{-2+θ_0})$ for an absolute $θ_0>0$, whereas the additional holes created when a cavity fragments under erosion have expected number of exact order $\varepsilon^{-2}(\log(1/\varepsilon))^{-2}$. In particular the one-pocket constant of the lower bound is strictly improved. The upper bound is obtained by pricing the contact configurations that pin near-critical pockets along the two independent arms of the path from a deterministic time, each arm contributing one factor $1/\log(1/\varepsilon)$. The outer estimate combines a stratified form of this first-moment bound with a packing argument near the frontier of the path, and the splitting lower bound forces a dumbbell-shaped cavity by a local construction followed by two logarithmic avoidance probabilities. The upper bound and the two structural estimates use no limit theorem for the shapes of cavities; the shape law enters only through the lower bound of the companion paper. ```

papers.title: Zeros of Katz's p-adic Eisenstein series E2
papers.abstract: For every prime $p\geq5$, the zeros of Katz's $p$-adic Eisenstein series $E_2$ on elliptic curves with good ordinary reduction have exactly $\lfloor p/12\rfloor+1$ distinct $j$-invariants. We prove that all these invariants lie in finite unramified extensions of $\mathbf{Q}_p$. Their reductions are given by a classical formula involving the supersingular polynomial, and each nonelliptic residue class contains a unique simple zero. For the Legendre family, hypergeometric congruences determine the polynomial of the lifted invariants modulo every power of $p$. We also study isogenies between the zeros. Each $p$-power isogeny class contains at most one zero $j$-invariant, and any two distinct isogenous zero invariants are algebraic over $\mathbf{Q}$. At a fixed cyclic degree, the nonelliptic isogenies give points in a finite divisor over $\mathbf{Q}$ on the corresponding modular curve. Its degree bounds their number and their fields of definition, and excludes several small degrees. The only zeros with complex multiplication have $j=0$ or $1728$. Whether a non-CM zero can have an algebraic $j$-invariant remains open.

papers.title: $G_2'$-Slodowy Slices II: Anosov Representations
papers.abstract: We find \emph{exotic} connected components of Anosov representations of surface groups in the higher rank group $G=G_2'$ that are neither $ι$-Fuchsian deformations nor higher rank Teichmüller spaces. These representations are found through the non-abelian Hodge correspondence via $G_2'$-Higgs bundles that we call \emph{$α$-bundles} and \emph{$β$-bundles}, which are particular cyclic Higgs bundles in the Slodowy slices of the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-triples associated to the simple roots $α$ and $β$ of $\mathfrak{g}_2^{\mathbb{C}}$. We first prove that (most) $β$-bundles that are also Hodge bundles are $P_β$-Anosov and $α$-bundles are $P_α$-Anosov. The strategy employed is new, geometric, and general. For $σ\in \{α, β\}$, we then show the locally homogeneous $(G_2', G_2'/P_σ)$-manifold ${\mathscr{M}}_σ(ρ)$ recently described in arXiv:2510.12757, for the representation $ρ:π_1S\rightarrow G_2'$ associated to a $σ$-bundle, coincides up to finite cover with the corresponding geometric structure for $ρ$ defined via domains of discontinuity by Guichard-Wienhard and Kapovich-Leeb-Porti. Consequently, we find that $π_1({\mathscr{M}}_σ(ρ))$ is an invariant for the connected component of $ρ$ in the space of $P_σ$-Anosov representations. After verifying the folklore result that the $G_2'$-character variety has exactly three connected components, we conclude lower bounds for the number of connected components of $P_σ$-Anosov representations in the two non-Hitchin components, most of which are exotic.
papers.comments: 53 pages, 7 figures, 1 table. No AI proof assistance

papers.title: Annular Counterexamples and Skew-Shape Block Identities
papers.abstract: We establish four connected results on weighted order ideals, cluster coefficients, and block-statistic enumerators. First, we give a counterexample to Theorem 14 of Kang, Lee and Lim (European Journal of Combinatorics, 2026): in the rank-two annular cluster model, a single bridging-lamination coefficient row produces $1+q^2$, contradicting the asserted unimodality. We identify the unsupported initial case in their published induction. Second, we refute their log-concavity Conjecture 1: the same gap example violates log-concavity, and a further single-curve computation gives the full-support polynomial $1+2q+7q^2+10q^3+9q^4+4q^5+q^6$, which also fails log-concavity. Third, we establish the skew-shape block-statistic identity proposed in Kahane's Conjecture 4.4 (arXiv:2607.11225v1) for arbitrary finite skew Young diagrams, under an explicitly specified root-exclusion convention. Its proof combines commuting tableau-transfer matrices, a connected-block inverse kernel, and finite polynomial differential equations; the corresponding mathematical statements have Lean 4/Mathlib formalizations. Fourth, we derive a bivariate block refinement whose coefficients are nonnegative after shifting the order parameter by one and, when necessary, multiplying by a monomial in the weight parameter. We specify the correction to the printed root convention, confirmed by Kahane in correspondence, and the geometric sign and specialization conventions clarified by the relevant authors for the annular examples.
papers.comments: Complete Lean 4 formalization available at this GitHub repository: https://github.com/adamtilepe/Annular_Counterexamples_and_Skew-Shape_Block_Identities

papers.title: Local Rigidity of Bergman Logarithmic Flatness on Compact Hermitian Symmetric Spaces
papers.abstract: We prove the local rigidity of Bergman logarithmic flatness near the standard metrics associated with fixed invariant positive polarizations on compact Hermitian symmetric spaces. Every sufficiently small smooth deformation preserving Bergman logarithmic flatness is induced by a holomorphic automorphism and a constant rescaling. This establishes a Bergman analogue of the local rigidity results for Szegő logarithmic flatness obtained by Lu--Tian (Duke Math. J., 2004) and, more recently, Loi--Palmieri--Zuddas (2026).

papers.title: Gradient Estimates for Singular-Degenerate Elliptic Equations with Solution-Dependent Coefficients
papers.abstract: We study a conormal boundary value problem for a class of singular-degenerate quasilinear elliptic equations in divergence form in bounded domains. The leading terms are measurable in the spatial variable and depend nonlinearly on both the solution and its gradient. The singularity or degeneracy is governed by a power of the distance to the domain boundary, with exponent greater than negative one. In particular, the corresponding weights need not belong to the Muckenhoupt $A_2$ class. Assuming that the weighted mean oscillations of the leading terms in the spatial variable are sufficiently small on small balls and that the domains have Lipschitz boundaries with sufficiently small Lipschitz constants, we establish global weighted $W^{1,p}$-estimates for weak solutions with bounded weighted mean oscillation. Our results extend recent estimates for equations whose leading terms are independent of the solution itself.

papers.title: The closure of the nonreal roots of bounded-height polynomials is connected exactly at pronic heights
papers.abstract: Let C_h be the closure of the nonreal roots of integer polynomials with coefficients of modulus at most h. With the nonzero real roots included, the closure is connected at every height; without them, connectedness becomes arithmetic. We prove that C_h is connected exactly when h=q(q-1) is a pronic number 2, 6, 12, 20, ..., and has at least five components otherwise. At height two this confirms a twenty-year-old numerical observation of Shmerkin and Solomyak on double zeros of power series: apart from 1/2 they form the interval $[1/ρ,1)=C_2\cap(0,1)$, with $ρ$ the tribonacci constant. Disconnection is almost always infinite. For (p-1)^2<h<=p^2-3, $h\neq p(p-1)$, infinitely many components with nonempty interior accumulate at $\pm p$ and $\pm 1/p$, and when h<p(p-1) these four points are themselves components. Next to each square q^2>=16, at least two of the three heights q^2-2, q^2-1, q^2 have infinitely many components accumulating at a common point of (1/(q+1),1/q). Explicit series give infinitely many components at every nonpronic height below 167 other than 1, 3, 4, 9, 25, 63 and 81, and in general at most sqrt(X)+1 nonpronic heights h<=X can have finitely many components, although C_h is a Peano compactum at every height. The proofs compare values and derivatives of all admissible power series near a real double zero; the comparison sets are open and closed in the whole core, so components separated near the axis cannot reconnect elsewhere. On the real axis, the double zeros at heights 1, 3, 4, 7 form sets with infinitely many components; at height one this proves a conjecture of Shmerkin and Solomyak and one of Solomyak on the connectedness locus for pairs of affine maps.
papers.comments: 45 pages, 8 figures, with a 35-page supplement (80 pages in all). Computational companion: Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.24117729

papers.title: Diffusion limits of cyclic finite-velocity random motions along vector fields
papers.abstract: We investigate diffusion approximations for a class of multivariate inhomogeneous finite-velocity random motions motivated by models of active particles. A particle alternates cyclically among prescribed velocity fields $V_1,\dots,V_p$ with random run times and evolves according to either a \emph{flight} dynamics, consisting of piecewise-linear motion, or a \emph{gliding} dynamics, in which the particle follows the corresponding velocity flow. Under a Kac-type scaling that couples vanishing run times with diverging particle speed, we prove weak convergence of both processes to multidimensional diffusions. It turns out that the order of successive cyclic motions affects the diffusion limit. In addition to the second-order term generated by fluctuations of the random run times, the limiting drift contains directional derivatives $DV_i[V_j]$ of the underlying vector fields. In Stratonovich form, part of this drift is expressed through their Lie brackets $[V_i,V_j]$. Thus, the generic non-commutativity of the microscopic motions survives the diffusive scaling and generates a macroscopic drift which depends on the cyclic order. The limiting drift also distinguishes the flight and gliding dynamics, despite their being driven by the same vector fields and run times. Several examples, including run-and-reverse motion and cyclic dynamics generated by multiple vector fields, illustrate how the cyclic switching protocol and the geometry of the underlying velocity fields shape the limiting diffusions.

papers.title: Compact Quasi-Metric Spaces Are Expand-Contract Plastic
papers.abstract: On a totally bounded metric space, every non-contractive self-map is an isometry. For quasi-metric spaces this fails. Here quasi-metrics are $T_1$: $d(x,y)=0$ implies $x=y$. Zavarzina gave a hereditarily precompact counterexample and asked whether rigidity holds at least for bijections. The author's toll spiral (arXiv:2610.13973) shows that it does not. We prove that compactness restores it: every compact quasi-metric space is expand-contract plastic, that is, each of its bijective non-contractive self-maps is an isometry. Countable compactness suffices, as does compactness of the conjugate topology. Bijectivity is needed, even on a compact, hereditarily precompact space. For arbitrary non-contractive self-maps, we prove rigidity when the space is hereditarily precompact and its conjugate topology is sequentially compact, in particular when it is also Yoneda complete; neither hypothesis can be dropped. Such maps are then surjective. In both theorems the $T_1$ axiom can be weakened to $R_0$, $d(x,y)=0$ implies $d(y,x)=0$, if hereditary precompactness is taken to mean that every sequence has a left K-Cauchy subsequence; surjectivity then holds up to points at distance 0 both ways. The weaker $T_0$ axiom is not enough: there is a $T_0$ space, compact in both topologies and satisfying all the other hypotheses of both theorems, with a bijective non-contractive non-isometry. Finally, for an asymmetric norm in finite dimension, the classical theorem makes the symmetric unit ball and sphere rigid for all non-contractive self-maps, and the forward ones if the norm is $T_1$. In infinite dimension, the symmetric ball and sphere need not be plastic, and for the forward ones we pose the quasi-metric form of the unit-ball question of Cascales, Kadets, Orihuela and Wingler. The two theorems and the counterexamples of Section 6 are machine-checked in Lean, except the steps listed at the end.
papers.comments: 23 pages. Lean 4 verification files included as ancillary files and archived with the paper at Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23265517. Answers two questions of the toll-spiral paper, arXiv:2610.13973. v2: Section 7 on asymmetric unit balls added. v3: numbering unchanged; notes that the maps of the second theorem are surjective, and derives Proposition 7.1 from the classical theorem

papers.title: Hamiltonian dynamics with nonconservative forces on extended phase space: An analytical mechanics derivation
papers.abstract: This note derives the full Hamiltonian equations of motion on extended phase space for nonconservative and/or nonautonomous dynamical systems, with particular attention given to the momentum coordinate and generalized force associated with time. Time reparameterization is also considered, clarifying when it does or does not preserve Hamiltonian structure. The analytical mechanics framework is used throughout, with all developments formulated in terms of arbitrary symplectic coordinates; the main developments are not predicated on a Lagrangian description.

papers.title: Lorentzian entropy, subgaussian matrix concentration, and sharp functional inequalities for all matroids
papers.abstract: We prove complete entropy contraction for homogeneous Lorentzian laws and derive subgaussian matrix concentration and sharp functional inequalities for every matroid. Uniform retention of $\ell$ out of $r$ particles contracts matrix entropy by the optimal universal factor $\ell/r$, in every finite matrix dimension and positive field, including repeated labels. The matrix Laplace comparison retains matrix variance and arbitrary Hermitian offsets. It gives subgaussian bounds for arbitrary Hermitian observables with bounded exchange differences, and Chernoff and Bernstein bounds for basis sums. Every unit-edge matroid basis graph satisfies the cube's small-set and Gross inequalities, with equality classified and optimal universal complete entropy-decay rate four. Its spectrum lies in $\{0,2\}\cup[3,\infty)$, with binary direct-factor contrasts spanning the eigenspace at two. We classify extremal down-up eigenfunctions, resolving Alaniz Pintos's degree-one conjecture and the equality problem for the Feder--Mihail walk. For degree at least two, every matrix entropy extremizer extends uniquely from its two-particle marginal. Equality depends only on the normalized pair law, with noncommutativity confined to mutually exclusive labels. We classify power-entropy extremizers for $1<p<2$ and give a fourth-order criterion for affine equality. Retained-level Gibbs reconstruction has sharp dimension-independent stability. For multiaffine laws whose generating polynomial and complement are Lorentzian, we determine the exact simultaneous all-field quantum marginal and matrix Hölder regions and classify the sharp half-marginal fields. Connected sharp laws are determinantal through rank three; stable nondeterminantal examples exist in every higher rank.

papers.title: Multivariate diagonal harmonics: character polynomials and proofs of two conjectures of Bergeron
papers.abstract: We prove Bergeron's Hook-Components and Coefficient-Length conjectures for the Vandermonde polarization module and full diagonal harmonics in every rank and number of alphabets. Hook-label characters are elementary skewings of the alternating character, and the maximal Schur length in label $μ$ is $n-μ_1$. We compute character and dimension polynomials of diagonal coinvariants in every bosonic--fermionic superspace for $D\ge3$, $n\ge\max\{D,2D-6\}$, answering Church--Ellenberg--Farb's character and dimension questions. For augmented commutative algebras in characteristic zero, we construct natural two-Schur presentations and filtered free resolutions with one Schur generator in each homological degree. For polynomial algebras, specialization to orthogonal idempotents identifies the first unstable correction for every nonempty tail $τ$ and degree $D>|τ|$. The stable threshold $n\ge D+τ_1$ is sharp when the row dimension is at least $\ell(τ)$. First parabolic algebras recover finite jets, their multiplication and their maps. Selected-label lifts give uniform Vandermonde generation through degree $D$ for $D\ge3$, $n\ge2D-3$, and disjoint-label products generate every first occurrence for positive integral row weights. Constructive degree reflection determines all two-column moment homology and generates its first syzygies from degree $n+1$; two-column Vandermonde generation reduces to degree $n-1$. Invariants and harmonics separate through the character range and through degree $n$ in two alphabets. The hook identities also give the fully graded sign component of the $t=0$, $(1,2)$-superspace Theta conjecture.

papers.title: Property Gamma and McDuff Factors from Shift-Similar and Houghton-like Groups
papers.abstract: We initiate the study of von Neumann algebras of shift-similar and Houghton-like groups, introduced by Mallery and Zaremsky as analogs of self-similar and Röver-Nekrashevych groups, respectively. Given a shift-similar group $G$ of permutations of $\mathbb{N}$, one can form the Houghton-like group $H_n(G)$, a ``mashup" of the classical Houghton group $H_n$ with $G$, which acts on $X_n$, the disjoint union of $n$ copies of $\mathbb{N}$. One main result is that when $G$ and the canonical shift map $σ$ admit a joint Følner sequence for their action on $\mathbb{N}$, then both group von Neumann algebras $L(G)$ and $L(H_n(G))$ are II$_1$ factors with property Gamma and hence $G$ and $H_n(G)$ are inner amenable. More generally, let $Γ$ be an ICC group of permutations preserving the ends of $X_n$. We prove that if the natural near action on $\mathbb{N}$ of the germs of almost permutations arising from $Γ$ along some ray is amenable, then $L(Γ)$ has property Gamma; if this group of germs is itself amenable, then $L(Γ)$ is McDuff. Then we construct a shift-similar group $G$, using property (T) groups with certain actions, such that neither $G$ nor $H_n(G)$ is inner amenable. Finally, we produce extremely broad and diverse sources of shift-similar groups satisfying the joint amenability condition. These examples come from residually finite groups and from wobbling groups of a variety of metric spaces. In particular, we completely characterize all metrics $d$ on $\mathbb{N}$ for which the wobbling group $W(\mathbb{N},d)$ is shift-similar in terms of a coarse geometric property---namely, that $σ^{-1}$ is bornologous with respect to $d$. As a consequence, this gives us necessary and sufficient conditions for when the wobbling group of any countable metric space admits a shift-similar embedding.

papers.title: An elliptic deformation of continued fractions
papers.abstract: We construct an elliptic deformation $\mathcal{Q}_{a,b;q,p}(x)$ of positive rational numbers $x$ by attaching Schlosser's small elliptic weights $w_{a,b;q,p}(s,t)$ to prefixes of Stern--Brocot words. On positive integers $n$ it gives Schlosser's elliptic numbers $[n]_{a,b;q,p}$. Parameter shifts realize $x \mapsto x+1$ and $x \mapsto x/(x+1)$, while a reciprocal parameter transformation gives an inversion formula. The Gaussian degeneration recovers the $q$-deformed rationals of Morier-Genoud and Ovsienko. The regular and negative elliptic continued fractions agree, since they evaluate the same word with the same ordered weights. The numerator and denominator satisfy weighted Farey recursions and, for rationals greater than $1$, are the closure polynomials, or quiver $F$-polynomials, of the associated oriented type-$A$ quivers. Finally, we express the vertex weights as normalized elliptic Euler expressions of balanced virtual torus representations.

papers.title: Efficient Conversion of Algorithms to Linear Programs
papers.abstract: The expressiveness of Linear Programming (LP) has motivated research on an LP compiler that generates polynomial-size LPs for polynomial-time solvable problems, including those having exponential extension complexity. By automating modeling from high-level algorithmic descriptions, the compiler offers a promising alternative to algebraic modelling languages. However, the resulting LPs are extremely large, posing challenges for existing solvers. Recently, we have introduced two LP compiler optimizations, namely Hierarachical Synchronization Barriers (HSB) and Constraint Sharing (CS), that address this challenge by exploiting structural and similarity-based patterns derived from the source code and the design of compiler-generated LPs, beyond what conventional compiler and presolve techniques can achieve in isolation. In this paper, we provide a comprehensive evaluation of these optimization methods on fundamental combinatorial algorithms and introduce the Execution Domain Aware (EDA) optimization framework to address a limitation revealed by this analysis. The framework reinterprets structural synchronizations as a time abstraction layer within which other optimizations can target localized reductions while remaining agnostic to time-step transitions. Across a broad suite of benchmarks, HSB and CS consistently generate smaller LPs, achieving LP file-size reductions of up to 96% and 53%, respectively, while also improving numerical conditioning, solver performance, and solution quality. HSB provides the strongest and most robust overall gains. The EDA framework further broadens the range of benchmarks that can benefit from HSB when its underlying structural assumptions are less effective. We view this work as a step toward systematic generation of Compact Integer Programming formulations for problems with exponential-size Integer Programs having polynomial-time separation oracles.
papers.comments: Full version with experimental data in appendices

papers.title: Oscillations in two-stage contagion on networks: contagion structure, turnover and connectivity
papers.abstract: Two-stage contagion describes processes, such as the adoption of an opinion or of a technological novelty, in which an individual must be exposed to an adopter twice before adopting. With demographic turnover these processes can generate waves of adoption and abandonment. We study these oscillations in a two-stage contagion model with turnover through a reservoir of inactive individuals and a small rate of spontaneous activation, and report four main findings. (i) In the mean-field description the oscillations are born at a supercritical Hopf bifurcation and require a predominantly two-stage contagion (first-contact adoption probability $Q\lesssim0.17$) and a slow turnover; spontaneous activation acts as a perturbation that destroys them. (ii) In finite populations demographic noise sustains quasi-cycles also outside this region, with a spectrum and variance predicted by a linear noise approximation away from the Hopf bifurcation. (iii) Reducing the connectivity of the network damps the oscillation, because naive nodes see fewer active neighbours than in a well-mixed population, and correlations measured in simulations confirm this damping mechanism; a pair approximation predicts that the sustained cycle disappears below a critical mean degree $\kc$, which decreases as $Q$ and the turnover rate decrease, and a finite-size test with up to $3.2\times10^5$ nodes confirms this threshold in simulations. (iv) At low connectivity the amplitude no longer depends on $Q$, so that sparsity erases the signature of the two-stage mechanism, whereas a faster turnover reduces the relative amplitude at every connectivity. The irregular dynamics observed in simulations are noise-driven quasi-cycles, not chaos.

papers.title: A novel derivative-corrected within-host viral model based on Caputo-Fabrizio fractional dynamics
papers.abstract: We study an implicit within-host viral dynamics model for uninfected target cells $H(t)$, infected cells $I(t)$, viral load $V(t)$, and damaged or removed cells $D(t)$. The model contains a parameter $\mathfrak{a}\in[0,1]$ that blends the classical instantaneous within-host dynamics with derivative-dependent correction terms. We rewrite the system as an explicit ordinary differential equation whenever a computable determinant $Δ(H,V)$ is nonzero, derive sufficient conditions for local and global well-posedness, prove positivity and conservation of $H+I+D$, compute the basic reproduction number by the next-generation approach, and analyze long-time behavior. Under natural nondegeneracy assumptions, $I(t)\to0$, $V(t)\to0$, $H(t)\to H_\infty>0$, and $D(t)\to D_\infty$. We also derive peak conditions, a final-size identity, and discuss the biological interpretation of $\mathfrak{a}$ as a dynamical responsiveness or short-memory parameter.

papers.title: Monitoring One Channel Is Not Communication Control: Causal Evidence for Adaptive Reallocation of Joint Message--Route Codes
papers.abstract: Monitoring a visible channel can change how learned agents communicate without removing why communication is useful. We test this distinction in an end-to-end game where a sender and receiver learn a discrete protocol and route policy without communication supervision. In two independent 20-seed batches, 20/20 and 19/20 protocols form. Online partial coverage increases shadow-route share over no monitoring by .701 [.574,.826] and .575 [.412,.737], while task accuracy remains .905/.913 and signed frozen message contribution remains .592/.563. Complete coverage removes most selective migration without removing communication. Frozen interventions, including a fresh pre-outcome confirmation, show that route is semantic: joint message--route shuffling changes .668 of receiver predictions and route alone retains .388 accuracy versus .25 chance. A corrected explicit-silence cost makes 18/20 policies fully silent and lowers mean sending to .050, but its strict complete-suppression gate fails because two seeds retain communication. Failed semantic-evasion and operational gates further bound the result. The evidence supports adaptive reallocation of a joint message--route code under partial monitoring, not open-world route discovery, emergent encryption, or a universal defense.
papers.comments: 23 pages total: 8-page main paper plus 15-page supplementary material; 1 main-paper figure and 3 main-paper tables. Equal contribution. Code available at: https://github.com/SummerRainET2008/DRCB

papers.title: Neural Networks with Local Converging Inputs for Solving the 3D Stokes Equations on Unstructured Meshes: Novel Techniques and Advances
papers.abstract: Neural-network surrogates for fluid-flow PDEs usually learn the solution globally, which requires large networks and many high-fidelity training simulations. Neural networks with local converging inputs (NNLCI) instead work locally. They predict the high-fidelity solution at a point from two converging coarse-grid solutions sampled near that point, which keeps the network small, needs little training data, and generalizes across geometries. Here, the two low-fidelity meshes, LF1 and LF2, have on average about 300 and 730 tetrahedra, compared with about 155,000 in the high-fidelity mesh (HF). In this work, we develop an NNLCI framework for three-dimensional Stokes equations on unstructured tetrahedral meshes and introduce two techniques for building local inputs near complex curved boundaries. First, input patches may extend beyond the boundary, with the outside values obtained from a local least-squares fit, so that every high-fidelity point can be predicted, including those next to the wall. Second, the local mesh spacing is estimated from neighboring centroids, which sets the stencil size consistently on unstructured meshes. For pipe flows with one to three bumps, including a circumferentially rotated bump, NNLCI reduces the relative $L^2$ error of the finer low-fidelity solution by $90\%$ to $94\%$, evaluated at all high-fidelity points. Both techniques carry over to other NNLCI problems with smooth solutions on point-cloud discretizations.

papers.title: A Beltrami Mode in Extreme Fractional Hydrodynamics under Stochastic Forcing
papers.abstract: We construct an exact stochastic solution of the extreme order endpoint of adaptive fractional Navier Stokes (AFNS) hydrodynamics on the three-dimensional periodic torus. A helical Beltrami eigenfield reduces the nonlinear vector equation to a scalar Ornstein Uhlenbeck process when the white-in-time forcing is aligned with that eigenfield. The resulting invariant Gaussian law yields explicit formulas for the stationary energy, its fluctuations, temporal correlations, circulation, and helicity. Under the same forcing, the corresponding classical Navier Stokes mode has a stationary energy that diverges as the Reynolds number tends to infinity, while the Euler limit exhibits linear growth of the mean energy and has no invariant probability law. The construction isolates, without a cascade hypothesis, the statistical effect of the finite fractional dissipation retained at the extreme endpoint of AFNS.

papers.title: A constrained mixed variational formulation with Legendre-dual defects for incremental irreversible thermodynamics
papers.abstract: We present a constrained mixed variational formulation for incremental irreversible thermodynamics. A single augmented action combines a linearized contact-increment penalty, equilibrium and dissipative Fenchel--Young defects, a storage--transport functional, and multipliers enforcing the constitutive increments. Under frozen-coefficient and boundary assumptions, stationarity yields the linearized contact condition, the Tisza relation, the Onsager flux--force law, and the implicit balance equation. An exact-elimination theorem shows that the contact and multiplier fields can be reconstructed algebraically from a solution of the reduced weak balance problem. We also prove off-shell invariance of the equilibrium--storage--multiplier sector under an equilibrium-sector partial Legendre transformation; invariance of the full augmented action is not claimed. For Fourier heat conduction, we derive a weighted drift identity and a per-step energy-drift bound for the energy-representation three-term incremental functional. In one spatial dimension, a small-time-step estimate yields a uniform $H^1$ bound and a discrete $L^2(0,T_f;H^2)$ bound, leading to cumulative $O(δt)$ drift over fixed time intervals. A conservative mixed discontinuous Galerkin (DG0)--Raviart--Thomas (RT0) discretization with fully implicit conductivity $κ(T)=1+T^2$ preserves discrete energy to roundoff. A separate lumped-mass piecewise-linear benchmark reproduces the predicted finite-step drift.
papers.comments: 19 pages, 2 figures, 2 tables. Companion paper (Part II) to be submitted

papers.title: Quadratic Bendixson criterion for delay systems: a numerical implementation
papers.abstract: We present a software implementation (as a Python package) of approximation schemes for verifying frequency inequalities arising from the quadratic Bendixson criterion for systems of delay equations (with a single delay in the linear part). In applications to dissipative nonlinear autonomous systems, such inequalities ensure global stability. The theoretical foundations of this approach were developed in our related work. In particular, it was shown that the transfer operators involved into the frequency inequalities can be represented as integral operators with bounded kernels of the Hardy--Volterra type. Here, we use this representation to construct approximation schemes based on finite-dimensional truncations of the transfer operators. Examples of using the package are provided.

papers.title: A Markovian SuASR epidemic framework with stochastic external factors
papers.abstract: Epidemic waves are often shaped by uncertain external drivers, such as environmental variability or behavioral and policy changes, that can randomly amplify or dampen transmission. Capturing this randomness requires models whose dynamics evolve under time-varying, stochastic influences. In this paper, we introduce a stochastic Susceptible-Asymptomatic-Symptomatic-Removed (SuASR) framework that embeds random external factors directly into the epidemic mechanism through an extended continuous-time Markov chain (CTMC). The proposed framework is flexible enough to represent epidemic dynamics both with reinfection and with infection-induced immunity, depending on the epidemiological setting under study. Unlike standard Markovian epidemic models, our formulation explicitly tracks two concurrent infectious sources (asymptomatic and symptomatic), yielding coupled infection pathways and substantially richer transient behavior. A key contribution is analytical tractability, where we derive computable expressions for the joint distribution of asymptomatic and symptomatic infection-event counts and develop tools tailored to extreme-outbreak risk, including the distribution of the maximum infectious burden. These results enable probabilistic quantification of epidemic severity beyond mean trajectories, providing direct estimates of the likelihood of rare but consequential surges. We validate the model through extensive sensitivity analysis and an application to the H1N1 influenza epidemic, illustrating how stochastic external influences reshape outbreak profiles, total infections from both sources, and the probability of extreme epidemic scenarios

papers.title: Second-level termination of the PPT entanglement-cost hierarchy for two qutrits
papers.abstract: We prove that for arbitrary two-qutrit quantum states, the semidefinite programming lower-bound hierarchy for the PPT entanglement cost terminates at the second level. Therefore, under operations preserving positive partial transpose, its zero-error asymptotic entanglement cost can be obtained by a semidefinite program involving only three Hermitian matrix variables. The key to the proof is to shorten the feasible dual chain by one level; to this end, we combine finite certificates verified by exact rational arithmetic with analytic estimates near the boundary of the parameter domain. This result shows that a unified terminating level exists for two-qutrit systems, whereas no unified terminating level exists for all dimensions.

papers.title: Combinatorial optimization with bounded subdeterminants
papers.abstract: We take a first step toward a broader study of classical combinatorial optimization problems through the maximum subdeterminants of their standard integer programming formulations, yielding new positive results for several famous (NP-hard) problems. An integer matrix is totally $Δ$-modular if every square submatrix has determinant of absolute value at most $Δ$. For every fixed $Δ$, it has been known that maximum clique, maximum stable set, and minimum vertex cover can be solved in polynomial time on instances for which the coefficient matrix of the natural formulation is totally $Δ$-modular. We extend this list by showing that the same holds for many other problems, including the weighted versions of maximum cut, the traveling salesman problem, feedback vertex set, odd cycle transversal, dominating set, max 2-sat, induced matching, and cluster vertex deletion, as well as for $k$-colorability and graph isomorphism. Our proofs reveal several new ways in which bounded subdeterminants impose combinatorial structure: they bound the size or maximum degree of the input graph, bound packings of cycles and other obstructions, or yield decompositions into tractable graph classes such as forests, chordal graphs, graphs of bounded treewidth, and graphs of bounded linear mim-width.

papers.title: Causal Learning with Invalid Instruments for High-dimensional Imaging Responses
papers.abstract: Large-scale neuroimaging studies provide high-dimensional imaging phenotypes for understanding brain-related diseases and their causal relations with biological risk factors. While instrumental variable (IV) methods can address unmeasured confounding in such observational data, existing IV methods face significant limitations when applied to high-dimensional imaging data, particularly in handling large-scale data and leveraging the intrinsic spatial structure of images. To address these challenges, we propose High-dimensional Functional-imaging Instrumental Variable Estimation (Hi-FIVE), a novel framework for estimating spatially varying causal effects when a majority of the candidate instruments may be locally invalid. We first establish identifiability conditions under which the spatial continuity of the causal effect surface propagates identification from regions where valid instruments form a plurality into regions where they do not, provided that invalid-IV effects switch on non-smoothly. Motivated by this result, Hi-FIVE combines penalized multivariate splines over triangulations for the causal surface and region-wise penalties for spatially localized invalid-IV effects, under an anchor constraint that keeps at least one relevant instrument valid on every simplex. A distributed algorithm parallelizes the computation over simplices for two- and three-dimensional images. We study the asymptotic properties of Hi-FIVE, establish consistency and pointwise asymptotic normality, and construct bootstrap-calibrated simultaneous confidence regions whose finite-sample coverage is evaluated through simulations. Hi-FIVE is illustrated with an analysis of the effect of phosphorylated tau on FDG-PET imaging in the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative, interpreted under the stated IV assumptions.

papers.title: Robust State-Parameter Estimation in Second-Order Thévenin Batteries
papers.abstract: We propose a scheme for estimating the full states and parameters of a second-order Thévenin battery model, using distinct features of the measured current. An identification step, run during suitable rest intervals, identifies the resistances and capacitances of the two RC branches from the voltage relaxation by linear least squares, without knowledge of the open-circuit voltage (OCV) map. An online estimator then runs continuously: the polarization voltages are estimated by open-loop observers; the series resistance is updated at current jumps using least squares; the state of charge (SOC) is propagated by Coulomb counting using the current capacity estimate, and both estimates are updated periodically by a sliding-window regression. We show that the identification is exact under a mild rank condition, that the series resistance is recovered at the first current jump, and that the online state and capacity estimates converge exponentially under verifiable excitation conditions. We also establish robustness of the online estimator under bounded process disturbances and measurement noise.
papers.comments: Under review for European Control Conference (ECC)

papers.title: An Improved $(1+2e)$-Approximation Algorithm for Metric Data Placement
papers.abstract: We study the metric data placement problem with site-capacity constraints and fixed installation costs, aiming to minimize the total cost of placing data (resources) and accessing their nearest copies. We develop a deterministic polynomial-time approximation algorithm based on a natural linear programming relaxation of the problem. Starting from an optimal fractional solution, we construct multiscale metric-ball partitions independently for each resource and connect overlapping balls at consecutive levels to form a flow network. The resource layers are then coupled through shared site-capacity arcs, allowing us to obtain an integral placement by minimizing a surrogate cost over a single min-cost circulation. By optimizing the choice of ball radii, we establish an approximation factor of $1+2e\approx 6.44$. To our knowledge, this is the best approximation guarantee for the metric data placement problem since its introduction by Baev and Rajaraman in 2001.

papers.title: Continuous Horizon Forecasting
papers.abstract: Multi-horizon forecasting has been dominated by discrete forecast strategies that treat model outputs as fixed-vectors or recurrently create them. In this paper, we introduce the Continuous Horizon (CH) strategy that generalizes upon recursive, direct, and multi-step strategies by redefining forecasts as a continuous operator and the forecast horizon as a query variable rather than an index. We present the theoretical foundations for the CH strategy, a Universal Operator Approximation Theorem, and a continuous-horizon bias-variance decomposition that formally proves the estimation variance improvements of CH over the discrete strategies. We validate the CH strategy empirically through a simulation study, and on 16 large-scale datasets from the M-series benchmark, showing how CH achieves competitive RMSE accuracy, while uniquely enabling parallel inference, targeted horizon querying, and interpolation and extrapolation across unseen horizons.
papers.comments: International Journal of Forecasting (Work in progress paper)

papers.title: Expiscating the black hole singularity in holography
papers.abstract: We argue that the leading exponential rate in the high frequency asymptotics of holographic thermal two-point functions is independent of the conformal dimension and spin (held fixed) of the operator. We analyze the leading universal WKB spectral curve governing the asymptotics at non-vanishing momentum scaling with frequency. We show that its classical action governs time domain signatures of the bouncing geodesic singularity, highly damped quasinormal modes, and the asymptotics of multi-stress tensor OPE coefficients. Beyond the leading order, we examine linear and dimension-dependent sublinear scalings of momentum with frequency. In both regimes, we derive the connection matrix between the boundary and the horizon using exact-WKB techniques. The results show a factorization of the spectral function into a perturbative part controlled by the OPE and a non-perturbative part governed by WKB transport. For linear scaling at fixed $k/ω$ in the timelike regime, the turning points controlling physical transport remain separated from the curvature singularity. Nevertheless, a singularity-anchored representative of the same transport homology class determines the leading WKB action. In the sublinear regime, the relevant turning points approach the singularity. We match an exact solution of the near-singularity scaled equation to the exterior WKB solution to determine the connection matrix and spectral function. Our results clarify how the black hole curvature singularity is encoded in dual field theory observables at leading order in the planar expansion.

papers.title: Challenging the hoop conjecture with spinning pancakes and baguettes
papers.abstract: Understanding when gravitational collapse produces a black hole remains a central challenge in general relativity. Black-hole uniqueness results characterize the stationary endpoint under suitable assumptions, while singularity theorems establish geodesic incompleteness in the presence of trapped surfaces and appropriate energy and global conditions. Neither, however, provides a general criterion for horizon formation. The hoop conjecture offers such a criterion by relating the enclosed mass to the compactness of a matter distribution in every direction. We construct axisymmetric families of initial data describing rotating dust and test a formulation of the conjecture adapted to this setting. We explore highly prolate and oblate configurations with both constant and differential rescaled angular-velocity profiles, including configurations near the threshold for apparent-horizon formation. We find that the conjecture holds for rotating configurations, with a coefficient within 14% of unity as in the nonrotating case, provided the quasilocal mass includes the rotational energy. If the irreducible mass of the apparent horizon is used instead, the deviations grow with spin, as they do for Kerr black holes. For horizonless configurations, the conjecture likewise holds when the mass is restricted to the energy enclosed by the matter surface, whereas using the ADM mass, which also includes rotational field energy outside the matter, leads to apparent violations of up to $\approx$25%. We also discuss the possible evolution of compact configurations without apparent horizons, their relation to weak cosmic censorship, and their implications for horizonless compact objects.

papers.title: Pulsatile Endocrine Regulation with a Releasable Hormone Pool: Impulsive Feedback Model
papers.abstract: An impulsive model of endocrine regulation equipped with frequency- and amplitude-modulated pulsatile feedback is extended to study the dynamical effects pertaining to limitations due to the releasable hormone pool. The model describes a three-hormone regulatory loop and is applicable to endocrine systems such as the reproductive, stress, and growth hormone axes. Conditions guaranteeing the existence and uniqueness of a periodic solution with a single feedback-triggered impulse per period (a 1-cycle) are derived, together with monotonicity properties of its characteristics. An explicit Jacobian formula is obtained to assess local orbital stability. Model analysis demonstrates that a reduced hormone-pool replenishment rate produces a lower-amplitude, higher-frequency 1-cycle. This behavior is consistent with experimentally observed alterations in testosterone regulation in aging human males.

papers.title: Constant query LCCs over the reals
papers.abstract: This note describes a new construction, found by ChatGPT Astra, of constant query Locally Correctable Codes (LCCs) over the real numbers. Prior constructions of constant query LCCs were exclusive to fields of positive characteristic and were conjectured not to exist over the reals. The construction uses low degree polynomial evaluations over an integer grid, together with a novel sampling procedure which outputs, for a given grid point $P$, a random quadratic curve through $P$ which intersects the grid in many other points (the decoding queries). The sampler is `smooth' in the sense that no grid point is queried with high probability. These codes have the additional property that the queried locations (the curve/grid intersections) are all nearby grid points.

papers.title: Implicit DeepReach Without Implicit Differentiation
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of approximating backward reachable and reach-avoid tubes for high-dimensional nonlinear systems whose Hamiltonians require numerical optimization over constrained controls and disturbances. Existing neural Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) reachability methods alleviate the dimensionality bottleneck of grid-based solvers, but evaluating Hamiltonians without closed-form expressions introduces an additional computational challenge. We show that, under suitable assumptions, the gradients required for value-function training can be computed without differentiating through the inner optimization problem. Specifically, we establish an envelope-type gradient identity for the saddle point Hamiltonian, under which the optimal control and disturbance enter backpropagation as constants without gradient tracking. This enables end-to-end neural HJ reachability with numerically evaluated Hamiltonians while avoiding both solver unrolling and implicit differentiation. We demonstrate the accuracy and computational efficiency of the proposed approach on nonlinear reachability and reach-avoid problems of different scales.

papers.title: Time Series Change Point Detection with Gaussian Processes
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a novel general Gaussian process framework for change point detection in time series. A change is defined as an alteration of the hyperparameters of the Gaussian process prior. We formulate the problem in the context of statistical hypothesis testing and demonstrate its performance over both offline and online multiple change points detection. The approach provides theoretical guaranties of its performance. An important advantage of the developed framework is that it does not need a detailed specification of the time series function before and after a change. The hyperparameter values are learned from the data. Comprehensive evaluation of the proposed framework is provided both on synthetic and real data and its efficiency is demonstrated.

papers.title: The wave equation and two-electron atomic wavefunctions
papers.abstract: Axisymmetric solutions of the classical wave equation in three spatial dimensions are shown to be in one-to-one correspondence to functions which annihilate the two-electron kinetic energy operator expressed in coordinates relative to a fixed nucleus.

papers.title: FP64 Performance and the Limits of Ozaki Emulation on HPC Systems
papers.abstract: A growing industry narrative holds that native double precision can be deprioritized in HPC accelerators, on the hypothesis that low-precision tensor cores can emulate FP64 on demand, and that most HPC workloads are bandwidth-bound. This paper evaluates some of those claims and explores the importance of FP64 in scientific computing. We show roofline profiling data of representative HPC workloads, across a variety of common computational motifs, to evaluate the arithmetic-intensity and accuracy requirements of these workloads. We also consider FP64 emulation via the Ozaki method to ascertain some of the possibilities and limitations of these approaches. These results indicate that Ozaki emulation should not be evaluated as a general replacement for FP64, but as an optimization for the subset of workloads whose dominant computation is sufficiently large, dense, and GEMM-shaped. Our analysis indicates this is less than 10\% of the HPC ecosystem. Furthermore, even in this favorable regime, standalone GEMM speedup is not enough to accelerate (or avoid performance regression) for the application: numerical behavior, workspace requirements, matrix shape, and integration overhead determine whether the benefit survives at application scale. This paper characterizes those boundaries empirically. Furthermore, we show that dense GEMM accounts for only a small fraction of FP64 computation across HPC workloads, leaving most application-level FP64 work beyond the reach of GEMM-based emulation.

papers.title: VC-Dimension and Generalization in Geometric Machine Learning with Applications to Active Learning
papers.abstract: We compute the VC-dimension of metric ball classifiers in the model spaces of Riemannian geometry (Euclidean, spherical, hyperbolic) and present upper and lower bounds on the VC-dimension of metric balls in several other situations, including general normed vector spaces (potentially infinite VC-dimension), vector spaces with $\ell^p$-norms (VC-dimension grows at least linearly in the dimension, faster than Euclidean for $p=1$), flat tori, and general Riemannian manifolds (arbitrarily large VC-dimension after a conformal change). In several situations where the VC-dimension is large or even infinite, we prove generalization bounds under additional assumptions on the data distribution using covering arguments. Both in the VC-dimension and covering setting, we consider data on low-dimensional subsets of high-dimensional Euclidean spaces. As an application, we consider coverage-based algorithms in active learning.

papers.title: Computational Power of Clifford and Ising Quantum Computers
papers.abstract: We extend the efficient classical simulation of Ising quantum computers from braidings to measurements. We investigate several different definitions of efficient Clifford quantum computation by varying the power of the circuit generator. In case the circuit generator can see the entire input, we give a detailed proof that efficient simulation of classical computation would imply the separation of complexity classes $\mathbf{P}$ and $\mathbf{PSPACE}$. If the circuit generator sees only the input length, we prove that Clifford quantum computers decide what we call affine languages.

papers.title: Quantifying the impact of 3D diffusion and local versus global removal by surface deposition on indoor airborne transmission
papers.abstract: The Viral Infection Risk Indoor Simulator (VIRIS) [Xue et al. 2024] combines architectural layout, people movement, and airborne transmission modelling to predict infection risk in indoor spaces. The modelling assumptions in VIRIS include: (i) uniform aerosol concentration over the building height, allowing airborne transmission to be modelled in a two-dimensional (2D) domain, and (ii) first-order global removal of aerosols to account for surface deposition. Both assumptions lead to underestimating the infectious aerosol concentration in the breathing zone. Here, we extend VIRIS to model airborne transmission more realistically and compare the impact on infection risk predictions. We develop VIRIS-3D-L by extending the airborne transmission model in VIRIS (a reaction-diffusion equation) to three dimensions (3D) and replacing global removal with a Robin boundary condition representing localised removal due to surface deposition. We compare VIRIS and VIRIS-3D-L across three single-storey buildings with increasing architectural and people-movement complexity: a courtroom, a care home, and a supermarket. We find that VIRIS underestimates the disease transmission rate and infection risks for individuals by up to 50% relative to VIRIS-3D-L in all three buildings. However, VIRIS-3D-L requires, on average, four times the computation time of VIRIS, mainly because it extends the computational domain from a 2D surface to a 3D volume. Overall, VIRIS-3D-L provides a more realistic modelling of airborne transmission than VIRIS and is particularly suited to settings with variations in people and furniture heights and frequent 3D movement. For simpler single-storey buildings, VIRIS is suitable because of its lower computational cost.

papers.title: Discrete Model-Based Diffusion for Combinatorial Optimization in Multi-Robot Task Allocation
papers.abstract: Decision making in multi-agent and multi-robot systems often involves discrete decision variables, leading to NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems that must be solved within seconds for near real-time implementation. Denoising diffusion has emerged as a powerful tool for such problems, but existing approaches face a trade-off: Model-Based Diffusion (MBD) incorporates diffusion in sampling-based optimization (SBO) without training but only over continuous spaces, while existing diffusion-based combinatorial solvers operate over discrete spaces but require offline training. To this end, we propose Discrete Model-Based Diffusion (Discrete MBD), a training-free SBO method that directly optimizes discrete variables by approximating categorical reverse transition distributions through Monte Carlo sampling. We establish a finite-step lower bound on the probability of finding a global minimizer and show that this bound converges to one as the number of denoising steps increases. Extensive experiments on generic integer programs and heterogeneous multi-robot coalition formation and scheduling demonstrate that Discrete MBD outperforms SBO baselines in nearly all settings while achieving solution quality competitive with that of mixed-integer programming and reinforcement learning methods at a fraction of their computational cost.

papers.title: Settling the Burn-in Gap: Sharp Risk Bounds for Tail-Averaged SGD in Linear Regression
papers.abstract: We study the excess risk of constant-stepsize online stochastic gradient descent (SGD) with tail-averaging for high-dimensional linear regression. Building on the instance-dependent spectral framework of Zou et al. (2021), we establish matching initialization-explicit upper and lower bounds on the total excess risk of tail-averaged SGD in terms of the population covariance spectrum $\mathbf{H}$ and initialization $\mathbf{w}_0-\mathbf{w}^*$ whenever a trajectory spectral feedback condition holds. Existing analyses exhibit a fundamental gap in the effective variance: the upper bound of Zou et al. (2021) retains an undamped contribution from the initial error in the head eigenspace $\mathbf{I}_{0:k^\dagger}$, whereas their lower bound omits the variance induced by the head initialization altogether. We show that both the existing upper and lower bounds are loose: the single-hop fast-mode variance contribution from the head initialization is exponentially damped during the burn-in phase, whereas fourth-moment energy scattered from the head initialization into slow spectral modes during the early burn-in steps survives undamped into the averaging window. We prove that our spectral feedback condition is satisfied in two concrete constant-stepsize regimes: (i) for arbitrary covariance spectra $\mathbf{H}$ and any finite horizon, under an explicit horizon-dependent stepsize chosen prior to execution; and (ii) for polynomially decaying spectra $λ_i\asymp i^{-a}$ ($a>1$), under a single horizon-independent positive stepsize. Finally, we complement these positive results with explicit one- and two-dimensional separation constructions proving an exponential-versus-polynomial gap in the lower bound of Zou et al. (2021) and showing why fourth-moment assumptions alone cannot determine the asymptotic exponential decay rate without additional structural conditions.

papers.title: Sample complexity of learning fermionic and bosonic Gaussian states with single-copy and entangled measurements
papers.abstract: With single-copy measurements, every mixed fermionic Gaussian state on $m$ modes, pure modes included, is learned to trace distance $ε$ from $Θ(m^3/ε^2)$ copies, with no logarithmic factor, against the known $Θ(m^2/ε^2)$ for collective measurements. We prove the upper bound, resolving Conjecture 10.1 of arXiv:2609.23189 (lower bound for $ε\le1/3600$), and fill most open entries of the sample-complexity table of fermionic and bosonic Gaussian states, for single-copy, $k$-copy and collective measurements. The single-copy measurement's noise is matched to the metric at every occupation scale. With blocks of $k$ copies, the covariant highest-weight measurement of arXiv:2611.07271, read out through the Weyl-shift estimator, is exactly unbiased for every state; it gives $Θ(\max\{m^3/k,m^2\}/ε^2)$ in Frobenius norm on all states and in trace distance on every class at a fixed distance from the pure boundary. The gain $1/k$ ($k\le m$) away from the pure boundary, against $1/\sqrt k$ on cold number-conserving states, is therefore attained. For bosonic Gaussian states with bounded covariance, any displacement and squeezing, and occupations $n_1\le\dots\le n_m$, $O((m^2+r^3+\sum_{i,j>r}1/(n_i+n_j))/ε^2)$ single-copy measurements suffice, $r$ the largest index with $r\,n_r\le2$; this is the minimax rate on dyadic-interval classes, with no spectral gap or cold-mode count assumed, and holds with no covariance bound for displaced passive states. With no bound on energy or squeezing, non-Gaussian measurements learn centred one-mode states, mixed included, from $O(ε^{-2})$ and centred pure $m$-mode states from $O(m^2/ε^2)$ single copies, free of the $\log\log E$ term of Gaussian measurements, and $m$-mode states from $O(m^3/ε^2)$ copies, entangled only in a first round on blocks of $4m+6$.

papers.title: Regression Modeling for the Bloc Basu Bivariate Exponential Distribution: Marginal and Conditional Means
papers.abstract: The bivariate absolutely continuous exponential distribution introduced by \citet{block1974continuous} provides a model for dependent lifetimes in reliability and survival analysis. Its marginal means depend jointly and nonlinearly on the rate parameters, which complicates regression modeling and the interpretation of covariate effects on these means. In this paper, we develop two regression approaches based on a region-wise multivariate exponential-family representation. In the full-distribution approach, link functions relate the cumulant derivatives in a fixed reference region to linear predictors. These derivatives do not directly equal the marginal means, which are instead probability-weighted combinations of the regional derivatives. This relationship allows covariate effects on the marginal means to be examined. Likelihood derivatives are obtained through the chain rule, and the regression coefficients are estimated by maximum likelihood. The rate parameter estimates are then recovered through the inverse link functions and an explicit inverse mapping, with the admissible solution selected to ensure positive rates. As an alternative, we propose regression models based on the normalized conditional distribution within each region. In this setting, the cumulant derivatives coincide with the conditional means, allowing covariates to be linked directly to these means. Both approaches are evaluated through a simulation study.

papers.title: Sufficient Dimension Reduction with Multimodal Predictor Objects
papers.abstract: We study the regression of a scalar response $Y$ on a Euclidean predictor $\mathbf{X} \in \mathbb{R}^p$ and a random predictor object $\mathcal{Z}$ in a general metric space under arbitrary structural dependence. We introduce a joint sufficient dimension reduction $(\mathbf{B}^\top\mathbf{X}, \mathcal{G}_Z)$ constructed via a sequential conditional independence framework, which differs fundamentally from the ordinary central subspace of $Y \mid \mathbf{X}$. Methodologically, $\mathcal{Z}$ is embedded into a reproducing kernel Hilbert space, and a regularized kernel-response envelope model extracts a finite-dimensional reduction of the feature map. Partial adaptive estimation then recovers the Euclidean reduction conditional on the first-stage coordinates. We establish root-$n$ consistency rates for the first-stage envelope subspace under a shrinking regularizer, alongside large-sample consistency for the second-stage Euclidean subspace estimator. Simulations and two real-data applications illustrate the utility and flexibility of the proposed method.

papers.title: Impact of Reduced-Order Modelling on Sum-of-Squares Region-of-Attraction Certification for Grid-Forming and Grid-Following Converters
papers.abstract: With the increasing penetration of power-electronic equipment, the transient stability of grid-forming (GFM) and grid-following (GFL) converters is increasingly characterized through the region of attraction (ROA) of the post-fault equilibrium. Sum-of-squares (SOS) programming yields certified inner approximations of the ROA, yet its computational cost grows rapidly with system order. Reduced-order models are therefore widely used to reduce computational cost and, more importantly, to enable analytical investigation. However, ROA analyses based on these models often assume that reproducing the converter's transient response, or retaining more dynamics in the correct time-frame, is sufficient to preserve the ROA of the full-order system. Using time-domain ODE simulations as a reference, the SOS-based ROA of each reduced-order GFM and GFL model is assessed against both its own simulated ROA and that of the corresponding full-order model, thereby separating SOS-induced conservativeness from model-order-induced ROA distortion. The results indicate that increasing reduced-order model complexity does not necessarily improve SOS-based ROA fidelity. In the cases examined, more complex reduced-order models yield lower SOS coverage of the full-order reference ROA, despite closer ODE-boundary agreement in some regions. Model selection should therefore consider both full-order ROA fidelity and certified coverage of the practical operating range, rather than model complexity alone.

papers.title: Parallel Broyden Methods for Efficiently Evaluating Nonlinear State Space Models
papers.abstract: Nonlinear state space models are typically evaluated sequentially, limiting their ability to exploit modern parallel hardware. Recent work has shown that state space models can be evaluated in parallel by reformulating evaluation as a root-finding problem, which can be solved with a parallel form of Newton's method. However, exact Newton methods require expensive multiplication of dense Jacobian matrices, and quasi-Newton methods based on diagonal approximations, while more scalable, are often slow to converge because they neglect interactions across state dimensions. We introduce a novel quasi-Newton approach based on Broyden's method, which captures coupling terms with diagonal-plus-low-rank approximations to blocks of the Jacobian. We construct the approximations from trajectory secants, avoiding automatic differentiation while retaining the favorable scaling of diagonal approximations and remaining compatible with parallel scan through rank compression. We prove finite-step recovery of the exact trajectory under the compressed scan, and show that convergence is tracked by the compression error and by the block approximation error along the current trajectory error, rather than in spectral norm. Empirically, we show that our method is advantageous when interactions are approximately low rank or when Jacobian evaluation is expensive: on low-rank RNNs, parallel MCMC algorithms, and denoising diffusion models, it converges in fewer iterations than other quasi-Newton methods and is the fastest parallel method when Jacobian evaluation is expensive or state dimensions are large.

papers.title: Metamorphic testing of learned AC optimal power flow surrogates reveals representation dependence
papers.abstract: Evaluating a learned AC optimal power flow (AC-OPF) surrogate on one grid serialization cannot show whether its accuracy depends on that encoding. We test this dependence with thirteen metamorphic relations, each specifying when a transformation is valid and how to compare its outputs. Our audit covers 17 model and pipeline configurations: two released trained checkpoints and 15 random-weight architecture or mechanism controls. Every configuration violates at least six relations, even at reporting tolerances ten times tighter or looser. For GridSFM-Open v1.1, source inspection and intermediate-tensor interventions point to an indexing bug and three noncanonical or numerically unstable preprocessing choices; a repaired checkpoint remains untested. In a separate case500 training experiment, augmentation lowers transformed-view error in three of four models and median discrepancy and constraint-violation P95 in all four. These benefits depend on the training protocol: some relations worsen, and every evaluated prediction remains AC infeasible. A GPU/CPU eigensolver mismatch accounts for most of the large raw-Laplacian-baseline gain. We recommend reporting representation consistency alongside accuracy, feasibility, and cost. These results establish neither deployment readiness nor universal invariance.
papers.comments: Accepted to the NeurIPS 2026 Workshops on (i) Trustworthy AI Evaluation, (ii) AI Foundations for Power Grids, (iii) Tackling Climate Change with Machine Learning, (iv) Sim2Science, and (v) Representations for the Physical Sciences

papers.title: Approximating graphic TSP by b-matchings
papers.abstract: We give a polynomial-time algorithm for graphic TSP that returns a tour of length at most $\frac{89}{64}=\frac{7}{5}-\frac{3}{320}$ times the value of the subtour relaxation. This improves the long-standing ratio $\frac75$ of Sebő and Vygen and shows that the integrality gap of the subtour LP on graphic instances is at most $\frac{89}{64}\approx 1.3906$. We optimize a non-linear objective function over an odd-join polytope, which uses (i) a new removable system of edges, and (ii) reconnection of subtours if the graph is disconnected. This approach gives a $\frac{13}{10}$-approximation algorithm for $4$-regular $4$-vertex-connected graphs, improving the $\frac43$ of Newman, and a $\frac43$-approximation for $k$-vertex-connected graphs of maximum degree at most $k+1$, for every $k\ge 3$. For the general graphic TSP, we construct a feasible point in the odd-join polytope, using an optimal vertex from the Subtour linear programming relaxation of TSP, which helps us bound the approximation factor by 89/64.

papers.title: Multifidelity Operator Inference for Non-intrusive Model Reduction under Data Scarcity
papers.abstract: Many-query analyses, in which a computational model is repeatedly evaluated, play an important role in uncertainty quantification and optimization for engineering design. However, many-query analyses can be prohibitively expensive when considering high-fidelity numerical models, especially those governed by partial differential equations (PDEs). Surrogate modeling replaces costly simulations with cheap approximations, enabling practical uncertainty quantification and design workflows. Machine learning (ML) approaches to surrogate modeling have gained significant traction in the development of surrogate models due to their non-intrusive nature; they do not require access to the underlying simulation code. The Operator Inference (OpInf) approach, in particular, fits reduced operators to state and corresponding time derivative data. However, high-fidelity training data is scarce due to limited computational budgets, and OpInf models trained on such scarce data often exhibit high variance, a critical liability in high-risk engineering design. We propose Multifidelity Operator Inference (MF-OpInf), which reduces this variance by supplementing scarce high-fidelity snapshots with abundant low-fidelity data drawn from coarser discretizations of the same problem. MF-OpInf handles data across varying fidelity levels by utilizing a multifidelity linear regression framework to estimate the reduced operators. Numerical experiments on model PDE problems demonstrate that MF-OpInf predicts PDE solution fields with higher accuracy compared to the high-fidelity-only OpInf with the same computational budget.

papers.title: Quantum Langlands correspondence for Painlevé II
papers.abstract: We construct an irregular KZ-BPZ correspondence for quantum Painlevé II from a rank-three Wakimoto-Whittaker module. The irregular KZ equation and the quantum isomonodromy equation form a joint affine system whose Drinfeld-Sokolov reduction yields scalar BPZ equations. We obtain matrix-integral solutions of this system for one fundamental insertion. An exact quantum Langlands duality exchanges the fundamental insertion with the zero of the dual Whittaker differential and allows affine solutions to be reconstructed from the BPZ equations. This duality interchanges the classical and Nekrasov-Shatashvili limits, which yield the Painlevé II Lax connection and an irregular Gaudin oper, respectively.

papers.title: Geometry of Gauge-invariant Quantum Fields
papers.abstract: Gauge-invariant representatives of massless gauge fields generally involve inverse differential operators. We trace this non-locality to the homotopy contracting the free gauge complex and replace it, at field level, by a local map using an independent scalar and a differential constraint. We discuss the BRST completion needed to preserve the physical content and the relation to the Stückelberg theory. We finally comment on the extension of this approach to non-Abelian gauge groups via the extension to interactions through $L_\infty$ homotopy transfer.
papers.comments: 11 pages, submitted to the proceedings of the 36th International Colloquium on Group Theoretical Methods in Physics Valladolid (Spain), 13-17 July 2026

papers.title: Decision-Focused Learning via Neural Optimization Layers for Battery-Assisted Grid-Import Smoothing in AI Data Centers
papers.abstract: Rapid AI data-center power fluctuations challenge grid integration. Sustained grid-import smoothing requires allocating limited battery power and energy under uncertain demand. We formulate risk-aware BESS scheduling that coordinates advance reserve commitments and demand-responsive dispatch, accounting for operating costs, grid-ramp penalties, and their conditional value-at-risk. We develop battery scheduling decision-focused learning (BS-DFL) with a constraint-aware neural optimization layer trained directly from this objective without optimal-solution labels. The trained layer is then frozen to guide demand-predictor learning through scheduling costs and ramping risk, enabling solver-free rolling-horizon scheduling. In a 10,000-minute simulation using loads derived from measured AI workloads, BS-DFL reduces mean absolute minute-to-minute grid-import changes by 71.70% and total scheduling cost by 18.01% relative to an MSE-trained predictor coupled with a mixed-integer linear programming solver, with an average decision time of 18.77 ms.

papers.title: Recursive memory for prediction and generation
papers.abstract: Recurrent and state-space language models compress the past into a state of fixed size. The state must answer questions about the future now, and it must remain useful as new tokens arrive, including tokens the model samples itself. We show that the second requirement can cost far more memory than the first. For a known hidden Markov source with positive transition probabilities, a state of $O(\log(1/\varepsilon))$ bits answers every question about the future to accuracy $\varepsilon$, however far ahead it looks, because the Bayesian filter forgets its rounding errors. Generating the future is different. When a model feeds each sampled token back into its state, the small errors in its next-token distributions add up, and $T$ tokens can require a state of order $\log(T/\varepsilon)$ bits. The lower bound comes from the KL chain rule: at every step, a model with $K$ states pays for approximating the true next-token distribution by one of only $K$ distributions. The argument applies to any source, including a language model continuing a prompt, and a small-ball estimate makes it tight for two-state sources.
