papers.comments: Clarified some parts of the manuscript and added references. This version has been accepted in Communications in Partial Differential Equations

papers.title: The Ordering Principle and Higher Dependent Choice
papers.abstract: We provide, for any regular uncountable cardinal $κ$, a new argument for Pincus' result on the consistency of $\mathrm{ZF}$ with the higher dependent choice principle $\mathrm{DC}_{<κ}$ and the ordering principle in the presence of a failure of the axiom of choice. We also generalise his methods and obtain these consistency results in a larger class of models.

papers.title: DualHash: Stochastic Primal-Dual Algorithms for W-Type Regularized Deep Hashing
papers.abstract: Deep hashing encodes high-dimensional image features into compact binary codes, enabling efficient similarity search in large-scale content-based image retrieval, a problem akin to semantic-preserving lossy compression under extreme bit-rate constraints. A fundamental challenge in deep hashing stems from the discrete nature of quantization in generating the codes. W-type regularizations, such as $z\mapsto\||z|-1\|_1$, are widely adopted and empirically effective at pushing network outputs toward binary values. However, existing methods often directly optimize these regularizations without convergence guarantees. While proximal gradient methods offer a promising solution, the coupling between W-type regularizers and neural network outputs results in composite forms that generally lack closed-form proximal solutions. In this paper, using Fenchel duality, we reformulate the nonconvex W-type regularization term through its convex conjugate, yielding a min-max problem with tractable proximal updates. We show that this min-max problem captures the stationarity of the original deep hashing objective up to the quantization error. Building on this problem, we present a stochastic primal-dual hashing algorithm, referred to as DualHash, with oracle complexity guarantees. We derive two algorithm instances: a momentum-based version with $O(\varepsilon^{-4})$ oracle complexity and an improved $O(\varepsilon^{-3})$ version using variance reduction, both for $\varepsilon$-KKT points of the min-max problem, which yield near-stationarity guarantees for the original objective. Experiments on three standard datasets demonstrate competitive retrieval accuracy and reduced quantization error, validating the practical value of DualHash for image retrieval problems. Our implementation of DualHash is available at https://github.com/RailLee/DualHash.

papers.title: Zeroth-Order Gradient Estimators under Decision-Dependent Noise
papers.abstract: We study zeroth-order optimization of a generally nonconvex optimization problem that is accessible only through a noisy black-box oracle, where the observation noise has zero mean and its distribution depends on the queried decision vector. Since the gradient of the objective function is inaccessible, various zeroth-order methods have been developed to solve the problem. However, it remains unclear how the choice of search directions affects the sample complexity of zeroth-order methods and how their algorithmic parameters should be selected. In this paper, we conduct a unified sample complexity analysis of zeroth-order methods across gradient estimators with different search directions. As a result, we show that gradient estimators that average over multiple directions, either uniformly from the unit sphere or from a Gaussian distribution, achieve the lowest sample complexity. The resulting sample-complexity bounds improve upon those of existing zeroth-order methods for nonconvex objective functions that are not bounded above. Moreover, through simulation experiments on multiple products pricing and strategic classification applications, we demonstrate the practical performance of zeroth-order methods with various gradient estimators.
papers.comments: Accepted for publication in Computational Optimization and Applications (COAP). Author's website: https://yuya-hikima.github.io/

papers.title: A functional Breuer--Major theorem with Poisson noise and a sharp regularity condition
papers.abstract: We extend the functional Breuer--Major theorem to stationary sequences generated from a Poisson point process under a regularity condition on the nonlinearity. We use the $L^p$ spectral gap inequality of the Poisson point process to prove the tightness. Our use of the spectral gap inequality naturally requires a regularity condition. In contrast to the Gaussian case, this condition cannot in general be replaced by integrability alone. We construct an example at the critical regularity showing that the regularity condition is necessary and the regularity threshold is sharp.

papers.title: Linear relations among radicals
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a field, fix an algebraic closure $\overline{K}$, and let $G$ be a subgroup of $\overline{K}^\times$. We are able to give a closed formula for the ratio between the degree $[K(G):K]$ and the index $|GK^\times:K^\times|$, provided that the latter is finite. Our formula explains all the $K$-linear relations among radicals, which (beyond the ones stemming from the multiplicative group $GK^\times/K^\times$) are generated by relations among roots of unity and single radicals. Our work builds on results by Rybowicz, which in turn are based on work by Kneser and Schinzel.
papers.comments: v2: Theorem 3 and its applications in the paper have been corrected

papers.title: On a Question of Mirzakhani and Vondrák concerning Sperner Labelings of the Simplex-Lattice Hypergraph
papers.abstract: Mirzakhani and Vondrák asked whether the simplex-lattice hypergraph admits a Sperner-admissible labeling in which every hyperedge receives at most two colors. We answer this question affirmatively by introducing the \emph{dominant labeling}, in which every lattice point is labeled by its unique \emph{dominant index}. In their hybrid model of fair division, this yields preference functions under which at most two players are nearly satisfied. We determine the number of vertices of each color and the number of hyperedges using a given pair of colors; these counts are expressed through the entries of Catalan's triangle. We also characterize the color sets of hyperedges of the other hypergraphs that arise from the edgewise triangulation of the dilations of the standard unit simplex.
papers.comments: We introduce the dominant labeling, which answers the question of Mirzakhani and Vondrák affirmatively. We enumerate the vertices of each color and the hyperedges receiving each pair of colors, expressing both counts through Catalan's triangle. We also characterize the color sets of hyperedges in the other hypergraphs arising from the edgewise triangulation

papers.title: An Algebraic Abstraction of the Localic Sheafification via the Tripos-to-Topos Construction
papers.abstract: Localic and realizability toposes are two central classes of toposes in categorical logic, both arising from the Hyland, Johnstone and Pitts tripos-to-topos construction. We investigate the common geometric structure underlying these classes by developing an algebraic abstraction of localic presheaves, localic sheafification, and the role of supercompactification in the Comparison Lemma. The resulting framework applies to a broad class of toposes arising from the tripos-to-topos construction, including all $\set$-based triposes. These results establish a common geometric framework encompassing both localic and realizability toposes.

papers.title: Sufficient average degree conditions for the existence of large highly connected subgraphs
papers.abstract: Mader proved that every sufficiently large graph with average degree at least $(2+\sqrt{2})k-1$ has a $(k+1)$-connected subgraph. He also conjectured that already an average degree of at least $3k-1$ is sufficient. The best known sufficient factor was improved by multiple authors but never reached $3$. In the present paper, it is further improved to $3.109$. In addition, the obtained $(k+1)$-connected subgraph is guaranteed to have more than $1.2k$ vertices. Moreover, similar conditions on the average degree are proven to be sufficient for the existence of even greater $(k+1)$-connected subgraphs. In particular, for $σ\geq \sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}$, every graph with average degree at least $\big(2+σ+\frac{1}{3σ}\big)k-1$ has a $(k+1)$-connected subgraph on more than $(1+σ)k$ vertices, where the factor $2+σ+\frac{1}{3σ}$ is asymptotically sharp for $σ\geq 1$.
papers.comments: New version: Theorem 1(1) has been extended, a generalization of high connectivity and order has been studied, and the structure of all proofs has been revised

papers.title: Proper maps of annuli
papers.abstract: We study proper holomorphic maps of annuli in complex Euclidean spaces, that is, domains with $U(n)$ as the automorphism group. By the Hartogs phenomenon and a result of Forstnerič, such maps are always rational and extend to proper maps of balls. We first prove that a proper map of annuli from $n$ dimensions to $N$ dimensions where $N < \binom{n+1}{2}$ is always an affine embedding. This inequality is sharp as the homogeneous map of degree 2 satisfies $N=\binom{n+1}{2}$. Next we find a necessary and sufficient condition for a map to be homogeneous: A proper map of annuli is homogeneous if and only if its general hyperplane rank, the affine dimension of the image of a general hyperplane, is exactly $N-1$. As a corollary, we obtain a classification of homogeneous proper maps of balls. A homogeneous proper ball map takes all spheres centered at the origin to spheres centered at the origin. We show that if a proper ball map has general hyperplane rank $N-1$ and takes one sphere centered at the origin to a sphere centered at the origin, then it is homogeneous. Another corollary of this result is a complete classification of proper maps of annuli from dimension 2 to dimension 3. Finally, we give a complete normal form of rational proper maps of annuli of degree 2.
papers.comments: 28 pages, clean up proofs, add some details, fix typos. Accepted to Nagoya Mathematical Journal

papers.title: The doubling property of the elliptic measure, for elliptic operators with drifts satisfying an average diverging condition
papers.abstract: We show doubling of the elliptic measure corresponding to the operator with an elliptic principal term and a drift that diverges, on average on Whitney cubes, like the inverse distance to the boundary, with a small constant. Essentially a small Carleson constant assumption on the drift, this generalizes earlier results with the hypothesis of pointwise smallness of such a drift. This relates to recent perturbative results of rough Dirichlet solvability in domains with drifts or potentials that satisfy a Carleson measure condition, which have also been considered earlier by Hofmann-Lewis and Kenig-Pipher. While we work in 1-sided chord arc domains, these results are new even for the half-space. In the process, we also prove Hardy inequalities in such domains with Alhfors-David regular boundary, using a stopping time argument.
papers.comments: Corrected a minor error with addition of Lemma 6

papers.title: Partial sequencings and other combinatorial aspects of large groups
papers.abstract: A \emph{partial sequencing} of length $k$ in a finite group $G$ is a sequence $g_0,g_1,\dots,g_{k-1}$ of distinct elements of $G$ with $g_0=1_G$ such that the partial products $g_0,\, g_0g_1,\,\dots,\, g_0g_1\cdots g_{k-1}$ are also distinct. Partial R-sequencings and partial harmonious sequences are defined similarly. Using the recent work of Müyesser and Pokrovskiy, we determine when such partial sequences extend to full ones in sufficiently large groups. In particular, if $G$ is sufficiently large and $k\le\sqrt{|G|}$, then a partial sequencing of length $k$ extends to a sequencing of $G$ if and only if some element of $G$ that is not one of its partial products has the same image in the abelianization as the product of all elements of $G$. This holds automatically when the commutator subgroup has more than $k$ elements, and we show that it can fail otherwise. Using the fact that every group of odd order has a symmetric harmonious sequence, we also prove that $\mathbb{Z}_{2^k}\times H$ is doubly R-sequenceable for every group $H$ of odd order, unless it is $\mathbb{Z}_2$ (in particular, every abelian group other than $\mathbb{Z}_2$ is), that $K\times H$ is symmetric sequenceable whenever $K$ is, that all sufficiently large groups are doubly sequenceable, doubly R-sequenceable, doubly harmonious and doubly $\#$-harmonious, and we verify these four properties for all groups of order $4$ to $12$ and for several small dihedral and dicyclic groups.

papers.title: Low-rank cross approximation of function-valued tensors for reduced-order modeling of parametric PDEs
papers.abstract: The paper considers function-valued tensors, viewed as multidimensional arrays with entries in an abstract Hilbert space. Despite the absence of the algebraic structure of a field, the geometric inner-product structure suffices to introduce the Tucker rank, higher-order SVD, and Tucker-cross decomposition for function-valued tensors. An adaptive cross-approximation algorithm is developed to compute low-rank approximations of such tensors. The framework is motivated by, and applied to, model order reduction of the parameter-to-solution map for a parametric PDE. The resulting reduced-order model can be interpreted as an encoder-decoder scheme with a nonlinear encoder and a multilinear decoder. The performance of the proposed non-intrusive approximation method is demonstrated in numerical examples for two nonlinear parametric PDE systems.

papers.title: Herman's converse KAM mechanism revisited
papers.abstract: In his counterexample to the KAM theorem, Herman used a hyperbolic perturbation together with a bump and asked whether the latter was necessary \cite[p.~78, Remark~4.7.3]{H1}. Motivated by this question, we compare destruction and persistence for a sine perturbation, with and without a Gevrey bump. The combined perturbation destroys all invariant circles with sufficiently small nonzero rotation numbers, whereas the sine perturbation alone preserves a sequence of analytic invariant circles in the same frequency range.

papers.title: Marked stable Lévy processes in Brownian local time
papers.abstract: We construct a random partition of the (local) time-space half-plane $\mathbb R_+\times \mathbb R$, measurable with respect to a single Brownian motion. The construction is driven by two objects canonically associated with this Brownian path: a white noise driving a pair of coupled squared Bessel flows whose parameters differ by $δ\in (0,2)$, and a continuous space-filling exploration of the half-plane. Exceptional bifurcation points of the coupled flows generate a random partition of the half-plane, up to a zero-measure gasket, whose widths are squared Bessel excursions with negative parameter $(-δ)$. A suitable time-change of the Brownian exploration arranges these excursions, in exploration order, as marks attached to the jumps of a spectrally positive stable Lévy process of index $(1+δ/2)$. As applications, we recover the interval partition evolutions of [Forman et. al. 2020] as horizontal slices of our construction, and use this representation to prove the independence between their total mass evolution and normalized partition evolution, as conjectured in [Forman et. al. 2021]. We also prove that the gasket of our partition is homeomorphic to the half-plane analogue of the stable shredded sphere introduced in [Björnberg, Curien and Stefánsson 2022].
papers.comments: 58 pages, 11 figures. Revised title and exposition. Added a theorem confirming the conjecture of [Forman et. al. 2021] concerning the independence between the de-Poissonized interval partition evolution and the total mass process (Section 5.3)

papers.title: R-harmonious groups
papers.abstract: A finite group $G$ of order $n$ is \emph{R-harmonious} if the non-identity elements of $G$ can be listed as $g_1,g_2,\dots,g_{n-1}$ so that the consecutive products $g_1g_2,g_2g_3,\dots,g_{n-1}g_1$ again list every non-identity element exactly once. Beals, Gallian, Headley and Jungreis proved that an abelian group is R-harmonious if and only if it does not have a unique element of order~$2$ and is not $\mathbb{Z}_3$. We prove a lifting lemma which shows that, under suitable conditions on $G/H$, a group $G$ with a normal subgroup $H$ of odd order is R-harmonious. As applications we show that every group of odd order whose abelianization is not an elementary abelian $3$-group is R-harmonious; in particular, every nontrivial group of odd order not divisible by~$3$ is R-harmonious. We also show that every split extension of a group of odd order by a ``harmoniously matched'' group is harmoniously matched, and hence R-harmonious. Together with a computer search, this gives many non-abelian even-order R-harmonious groups, among them the dihedral groups $D_{2n}$ with $n\equiv 8\pmod{16}$ or $n\equiv 16\pmod{32}$. Finally, we observe that the quaternion group $Q_8$ satisfies the Hall--Paige condition but is not R-harmonious.

papers.title: Cocycle perturbations and ergodicity for actions on type III factors
papers.abstract: We study cocycle perturbations of state preserving actions on type $\mathrm{III}_1$ factors. Extending the theorem of Marrakchi and Vaes for type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors, we show that a state preserving outer $\mathbb Z$-action on a type $\mathrm{III}_1$ factor with trivial bicentralizer admits a unitary cocycle whose perturbation becomes an ergodic action. This partially answers a question of Marrakchi and Vaes. A major difference from the type $\mathrm{II}$ case is that the modular automorphism group naturally appears as part of the action, making the construction of the required cocycle more delicate.
papers.comments: 19 pages. Corrected errors in the final section

papers.title: Topological flatness of orthogonal spin local models
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime and $F$ be a complete discretely valued field with residue field of characteristic $p$. For any parahoric level structure of the split even orthogonal similitude group $\operatorname{GO}_{2n}$ over $F$, we prove a preliminary form of the Pappas-Rapoport flatness conjecture: the associated spin local model is topologically flat.

papers.title: Pair Space Analysis of Some Four-Body Central Configurations
papers.abstract: I study central configurations in the four-body problem, i.e., configurations in which the forces on all the bodies point to a fixed, single point in space. The newly formulated pair-space formalism yields a set of vectorial equations that fully characterize such configurations. I investigate a sub-class of solutions in which at least two pairs of inter-body distances are equal. The only such non-collinear configurations are the tetrahedron (the unique non-planar configuration), kites and the isosceles trapezium. The specific shapes (internal angles) are determined by the ratio of the masses of the bodies. Mathematical expressions are given for all these relations.

papers.title: Multiset Deletion Codes: Cyclic Syndrome Constructions, Bounds, and Exact Results
papers.abstract: We determine sharp class-size estimates for multiset codes over $q$ symbols that correct up to $t$ deletions. For fixed $q,t\ge2$, we prove that the syndrome classes defined by Nathanson's geometric-sum labels modulo $M=1+t+\cdots+t^{q-1}$ differ from their average size by $O(n^{q/p-1})$, where $n$ is the blocklength and $p$ is the least prime divisor of $q$. This exponent is sharp, and every prescribed class has size asymptotic to the average. For prime $q$, all classes have equal size when $n\equiv-1,\ldots,-(q-1)\pmod M$. We also present our radix construction, whose labels are zero and the first $q-1$ powers of $t+1$, starting at $1$, modulo $t(t+1)^{q-2}+1$. We determine its sharp class-size deviation exponent. For even $q\ge4$, its syndrome classes have a smaller deviation exponent, although their average size is smaller. Over four symbols and every $t\ge2$, we show that the radix labels still correct up to $t$ deletions modulo a reduced modulus, which gives bounded deviations and eventually larger classes than either unmodified construction. For a fixed number $k\ge2$ of surviving symbols, we prove that some maximum code contains all constant words, reducing the remaining optimization to multisets with multiplicities below $k$. Finally, for one deletion at length four over $q\ge4$ symbols, we show that the best bound from fractional weights on deletion outputs, rounded down, equals the maximum code size exactly when $q\equiv2,4\pmod6$.

papers.title: Random tree Besov priors: Data-driven regularisation parameter selection
papers.abstract: We develop a data-driven algorithm for automatically selecting the wavelet density parameters in Bayesian inversion under random tree Besov priors. One of the key challenges in Bayesian inversion is the construction of priors that are both expressive and computationally feasible. Random tree Besov priors, introduced in \cite{Kekkonen2023}, provide a flexible framework for capturing local regularity properties and sparsity patterns in a wavelet basis. In this paper, we extend this approach by introducing a hierarchical model that enables data-driven selection of the wavelet density parameter, allowing the regularisation strength to adapt across scales while retaining computational efficiency. We focus on nonparametric regression and also present preliminary plug-and-play results for a deconvolution problem.

papers.title: Robust Joint Power Allocation and Antenna Placement for Pinching-Antenna Systems under Gaussian Location Uncertainty
papers.abstract: Pinching antenna systems (PASS) have attracted much attention recently owing to their capability to maintain reliable line-of-sight communication in high-frequency bands. By guiding signals through a waveguide and emitting them via a movable pinching antenna, PASS enable dynamic control of signal propagation and spatial adaptability. However, their performance heavily depends on effective resource allocation, including power allocation and antenna positioning, which becomes challenging under user localization uncertainty. Existing studies largely assume perfect user locations, while our prior work considered uniformly distributed localization errors. In this paper, we develop a robust resource allocation framework for multi-user downlink PASS under Gaussian-distributed localization uncertainty. An energy-efficiency (EE) maximization problem is formulated subject to probabilistic outage constraints, and the minimum transmit power is analytically characterized for any given antenna position. For the unbounded Gaussian model, we prove that the resulting one-dimensional antenna-placement objective is convex and derive a globally optimal derivative-bisection algorithm. We further consider a circularly truncated Gaussian model for bounded localization-error regions and develop a deterministic branch-and-bound method that returns an $ε_{\rm B}$-globally optimal antenna position. Finally, we discuss how position-dependent waveguide attenuation modifies the placement objective and may destroy its convexity. Simulation results verify that the proposed branch-and-bound solution closely matches the bounded grid-search benchmark, demonstrate substantial EE gains from optimized pinching-antenna placement over the bounded fixed-antenna architecture, and reveal an increasing distinction between the bounded and unbounded Gaussian models as the location uncertainty grows.
papers.comments: accepted by IEEE TVT; pinching antenna; user location uncertainty; imperfect CSI

papers.title: Gromov-Hausdorff and intrinsic flat convergence of RCD(K,N) and Kato spaces
papers.abstract: We consider metric measure spaces $(X,\mathsf{d},\mathscr{H}^N)$ satisfying the curvature-free properties (ETR), (LDB), and whose regular set is almost everywhere quasi-convex. In particular, these assumptions are satisfied by non-collapsed RCD$(K,N)$ spaces without boundary, as well as by non-collapsed strong Kato limit spaces without boundary. In this framework, we establish a local rigidity result for top-dimensional integral currents and deduce uniqueness, up to a sign, of orientations in the sense of metric currents. We then prove stability of orientation under pointed Gromov--Hausdorff convergence and show that, for both the RCD and strong Kato classes, the pointed Gromov--Hausdorff limit coincides with the local intrinsic flat limit. The proof of the convergence is based on the local degree of (ETR) charts and on the $L^1$-stability of the degree under flat convergence. A central ingredient is a full-measure biLipschitz decomposition of splitting charts around almost-Euclidean regular points of non-collapsed RCD$(K,N)$ spaces.

papers.title: Timelike curves: homotopies and domain of determinacy
papers.abstract: This paper studies domains of determination of linear strictly hyperbolic second order operators $P$. For an open set $\mathcal O$, a set $Z$ is a domain of determination when the values of solutions of the differential equation $Pu=0$ are determined on $Z$ by their values in $\mathcal O$. Fritz John's global Hölmgren theorem implies that points that can be reached by deformations of noncharacteristic hypersufaces with initial surface and boundaries in $\mathcal O$ belong to a domain of determination provided that local uniqueness holds at noncharacteristic surfaces. Using spacelike hypersurfaces yields sharp finite speed results whose domains of determination are described in terms of influence curves that never exceed the local speed of propagation. This paper studies deformations of noncharacteristic nonspacelike hypersurfaces. We prove that points reachable by (repeated) deformations by noncharacteristic nonspacelike hypersurfaces coincide exactly with the set of points reachable by (repeated) homotopies of timelike arcs whose initial curves and endpoints belong to $\mathcal O$. When the set $\mathcal O$ is a small neighborhood of a forward timelike arc connecting $a$ to $b$, a natural candidate for $Z$ is the intesection of the future of $a$ with the past of $b$. This candidate is exact for D'Alembert's equation. We prove that it is also exact when $a,b$ are points close together on a fixed timelike arc. The timelike homotopy criterion fuels the construction of surprising examples for which the domain of determination is strictly larger (resp. strictly smaller) than the future-intersect-past candidate.

papers.title: Complexity of Projected Gradient Methods for Strongly Convex Optimization with Hölder Continuous Gradient Terms
papers.abstract: This paper studies the complexity of projected gradient descent methods for a class of strongly convex constrained optimization problems where the objective function is expressed as a summation of $m$ component functions, each possessing a gradient that is Hölder continuous with an exponent $α_i \in (0, 1]$. Under this formulation, the gradient of the objective function may fail to be globally Hölder continuous, thereby rendering existing complexity results inapplicable to this class of problems. Our theoretical analysis reveals that, in this setting, the complexity of projected gradient methods is determined by $\hatα = \min_{i \in \{1, \dotsc, m\}} α_i$. We first prove that, with an appropriately fixed stepsize, the complexity bound for finding an approximate minimizer with a distance to the true minimizer less than $\varepsilon$ is $O (\log (\varepsilon^{-1}) \varepsilon^{2 (\hatα - 1) / (1 + \hatα)})$, which extends the well-known complexity result for $\hatα = 1$. Next we show that the complexity bound can be improved to $O (\log (\varepsilon^{-1}) \varepsilon^{2 (\hatα - 1) / (1 + 3 \hatα)})$ if the stepsize is updated by the universal scheme. We illustrate our complexity results by numerical examples arising from elliptic equations with a non-Lipschitz term.
papers.comments: This manuscript is, in fact, an updated version of arXiv:2505.03506. We would therefore like to withdraw the current manuscript and resubmit it as a updated version of arXiv:2505.03506

papers.title: A Dynamical Fekete-Szegő Theorem
papers.abstract: Let $E\subset\mathbb{C}$ be a compact set, symmetric with respect to the real axis and regular for the Dirichlet problem. A classical theorem of Fekete and Szegő asserts that if $cap(E)\ge 1$ then every neighbourhood of $E$ contains infinitely many complete sets of conjugate algebraic integers. We prove a dynamical strengthening: $cap(E)\ge1$ if and only if every neighbourhood of the polynomially convex hull $Pc(E)$ contains filled Julia sets of monic integral polynomials of arbitrarily large degree. When $cap(E)=1$, we show that the minimal polynomials $P_n$ of distinct algebraic integers whose entire Galois orbits approach $E$ have filled Julia sets $K_{P_n}$ converging to $Pc(E)$ in the Klimek metric, and Brolin measures converging to the equilibrium measure $μ_E$. The key step is that algebraic numbers of small Rumely height $h_E$ have minimal polynomials that are asymptotically minimal on $E$. As an arithmetic application, we show that the Call--Silverman canonical heights $\hat{h}_{P_n}$ converge to $h_E$ uniformly on $\bar{\mathbb{Q}}$.
papers.comments: v2: corrected proofs of Lemma 1 and Theorem 1; clarified the conjugate-localisation hypothesis; strengthened canonical-height convergence to uniform convergence; added Hausdorff convergence for real sets and corrected references. 12 pages

papers.title: Warped area-minimizing hypersurface and warped product metric
papers.abstract: Let $(M^n,g)$ be a smooth, compact, connected and oriented Riemannian manifold with $3\le n\le 7$ and $H_{n-1}(M;\mathbb{Z})\neq 0$, and let $u>0$ be smooth on $M$. Suppose that \[ -γu^{-1}Δ_g u+\Ricmin_g\ \geq\ (n-1)(n-3)\,u^{-2}|\nabla u|^2, \qquad γ=n-1, \] where $\Ricmin_g$ is the pointwise least Ricci curvature. Since both this hypothesis and the class of warped (weighted) area-minimizers are invariant under $u\mapstoλu$, we normalize $u\equiv1$ on the minimizer. We prove that some non-trivial class in $H_{n-1}(M;\mathbb{Z})$ contains a warped area-minimizing hypersurface $Σ$ on which $u$ is constant, and that $M$ locally splits as a warped product $(-ε,ε)\times_fΣ$, $g=dt^2+f^2(t)g_Σ$, with $f=u^{-1}$ and $\operatorname{Ric}_{g_Σ}\geq (n-2)[(f')^2-ff'']\,g_Σ$. By extending the foliation via Federer--Fleming compactness of the constant-warped-area leaves, this local splitting upgrades to a \emph{global} one: $M$ is covered by $\mathbb{R}\times_fΣ$, its universal cover is $\mathbb{R}\times_f\tildeΣ$ where $\tildeΣ$ is the universal cover of $Σ$, and $f=u^{-1}$ is periodic and bounded above and below, so $M$ fibres over $\mathbb{S}^1$ with fibre a quotient of $Σ$. This spectral bound is saturated with equality by warped product metrics, which is what makes it the natural threshold for warped rather than direct product rigidity. When $u\equiv1$ it reduces to $\Ricmin_g\geq0$ and our conclusion to the classical product splitting.

papers.title: Biquantization of the necklace Lie bialgebra
papers.abstract: For the double of a quiver, the works of Ginzburg, Bocklandt-Le Bruyn and Schedler show that its closed paths, called the necklaces, have a natural Lie bialgebra structure. Schedler also constructed,in [Int. Math. Res. Notices, 2005 (12), 725-760], a Hopf algebra that quantizes this Lie bialgebra. In this paper, we pursue one more step in this direction by constructing its biquantization, in the sense of Turaev [Ann. Sci. École Norm. Sup. (4) 24 (1991), no. 6, 635-704].

papers.title: Linear Asymptotic Stability of the Smooth 1-Solitons for the Degasperis-Procesi Equation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the asymptotic stability of smooth 1-solitons in the Degasperis-Procesi (DP) equation. Such solutions necessarily exist on a non-zero background, and their spectral and orbital stability has previously been verified by Li, Liu & Wu and by Lafortune & Pelinovsky. Using the complete integrability of the DP equation to establish the strong spectral stability of smooth solitary waves, namely that the origin is the only eigenvalue of the associated linearized operator acting on $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ and that, moreover, in appropriate exponentially weighted spaces the non-zero spectrum for the linearized operator admits a spectral gap away from the imaginary axis. This spectral gap result {is then} upgraded to an exponential decay estimate on the semigroup associated with the linearized operator, establishing a linear asymptotic stability result in exponentially weighted spaces. Finally, we outline analytical challenges with extending our result to the nonlinear level.
papers.comments: 44 pages, 2 figures. Correcting typos, adding additional exposition

papers.title: Persistence of the Wiener sausage: sampling stability and limit theorems for Betti-curve functionals of drifted planar Brownian motion
papers.abstract: We study the persistent homology of the offset filtration generated by the range of a planar Brownian motion with constant nonzero drift (Wiener sausages of increasing radius). We prove what are, to our knowledge, the first law of large numbers and central limit theorem for its smoothed Betti-curve functionals. For every bounded Borel weight $ψ$ supported in a compact radius window $[r_0,r_1]\subset(0,\infty)$, the functional $Φ_ψ(T)=\int_{r_0}^{r_1}β_1(T,r)ψ(r)\,dr$, where $β_1(T,r)$ counts the holes of the radius-$r$ sausage at time $T$, satisfies $Φ_ψ(T)/T\toρ_ψ$ almost surely and in every $L^p$, for a deterministic constant $ρ_ψ$. This yields a finite positive Betti-curve intensity measure on the radius axis, which we identify as absolutely continuous through a fixed-radius law of large numbers along regeneration times, valid at almost every radius. We also prove Gaussian fluctuations at scale $\sqrt{T}$, for one weight and jointly for finitely many, with a Green-Kubo variance over the regeneration cycles. The proof combines a renewal structure along the drift direction, obtained by the method of Sznitman and Zerner without invoking the strong Markov property at the cut times, with a Mayer-Vietoris control of the non-additivity of topology under concatenation and a deterministic bound on the integrated hole count of a planar offset proved in a companion paper. A sampling theorem bounds the bottleneck distance between the diagram of the continuous filtration and that of a time-sampled point cloud by the pathwise modulus of continuity, placing these objects in a data-analytic framework.
papers.comments: The only difference between this new version (version 3) and the previous version 2 is a correction in the paper's title

papers.title: Solution of Erdős Problem 633
papers.abstract: We classify triangles that can be tiled only into a square number of congruent triangles, settling Erdős Problem 633.

papers.title: Computing Families of Periodic Solutions of the 4- and 6-Body Problems Using an Adaptive Gradient-Free Stochastic Method
papers.abstract: In this paper, we numerically compute planar periodic motions of the 4- and 6-body problems. We consider a 4-body configuration formed by two opposite pairs of bodies and a 6-body configuration formed by two equilateral triangles. More generally, for two regular $k$-gons with masses $1$ and $m_2$ in the respective groups, we derive a system of four second-order differential equations for two radial and two angular variables; for $k=2$, the groups are opposite pairs. With $r_1(0)=1$, the periodicity conditions lead to an overdetermined nonlinear system consisting of eight return equations in five unknowns. We show that, for collision-free solutions, four symmetry conditions at $H=T/2$ imply these eight equations. For prescribed mass ratio and angular advance, we solve the resulting four equations in four unknowns using Newton's method. An adaptive stochastic black-box procedure, which uses only function evaluations, provides initial approximations. The method searches for solutions by sampling in an anisotropic box whose dimensions adapt using information from previous successful iterations. Exact satisfaction of the return conditions gives a motion that repeats up to rotation and relabeling; an angular advance that is a rational multiple of $2π$ then gives a periodic motion. We report numerical examples and check the return residuals of the printed initial conditions using both the reduced equations and independent integrations of the full Cartesian equations.
papers.comments: 20 pages, 6 figures. This version reduces the eight return equations to four midpoint conditions for the collision-free symmetric motions considered and derives the reduced ODEs for two regular k-gons (opposite pairs for k=2), giving 2k-body configurations for every integer k>1

papers.title: Discounted MPC and infinite-horizon optimal control under plant-model mismatch: Stability and suboptimality
papers.abstract: We study the robustness to plant-model mismatch of nonlinear systems in closed loop with (discounted) optimal controllers designed for a nominal model, with quadratic stage costs across finite and infinite horizons. By combining Lyapunov analysis with a unifying relaxed dynamic programming framework, we establish conditions that guarantee robust stability alongside improved suboptimality bounds compared to existing literature. A key step in our analysis is proving that stability counteracts time-accumulated error growth due to plant-model mismatch, yielding robustness bounds that hold uniformly across all prediction horizons.

papers.title: Nonlinear Stochastic Optimal Control and Optimal Stopping using the Fokker-Planck Transformation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a theoretical framework for nonlinear stochastic optimal control problems with optimal stopping by establishing a density-based deterministic representation of the underlying diffusion. For state-independent diffusion, we rewrite the controlled Fokker-Planck equation as a continuity equation driven by a score-corrected velocity field, yielding a deterministic characteristic dynamics that reproduces the marginal law of the stochastic system. Leveraging Stein-type identities, we show that the associated distributional dynamic programming equation admits the same second-order differential operator as the distributional stochastic Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman formulation. Building on this representation, we formulate an optimal control problem with state-dependent terminal-time assignment and terminal distributional constraints and derive the first-order necessary conditions using variational analysis. We present the conditions both for a common terminal time and for the general case of state-dependent stopping.
papers.comments: 40 pages, revised version of a journal submission. We acknowledge the insightful feedback from Tryphon T. Georgiou on an early version of this manuscript

papers.title: Allard Regularity for Abelian Yang--Mills--Higgs Equation
papers.abstract: We prove an Allard regularity theorem for critical points of the Abelian Yang-Mills-Higgs energy at critical coupling in every ambient dimension. A new cylindrical monotonicity formula for the full excess, based on an improved Modica inequality, converts the tilt-excess decay of De Philippis-Halavati-Pigati into rigidity of nontrivial entire critical points with almost unit density. This resolves their Gibbons conjecture without a local minimising assumption. Adapting the local vortex expansion and projected linear theory of Badran-del Pino, we obtain quantitative vortex approximation and uniform interior $C^{2,α}$ estimates for the nodal sets. To pass to nonzero complex levels, we use a Hodge decomposition of the difference between the actual and approximate connections: curvature comparison controls the co-closed part, while the Coulomb condition gives estimates for the exact part and hence for the phase. In the Coulomb gauge with vanishing normal component on the outer boundary, this yields graphical $C^{2,α}$ bounds for all levels $\{u_\varepsilon=t\}$, uniformly for $|t|\leq1-b$, in an interior tubular neighbourhood of the nodal set.
papers.comments: This is a substantial update to the previous paper - we remove the dimension restriction and extend the regularity from the nodal set to all level sets

papers.title: Optimizing Bit-Labeling of Voronoi Constellations
papers.abstract: We optimize the bit-to-symbol map of the $D_4$ and $E_8$ root lattices in reference to bit error rate, by implementing two searches on a performance metric, Hamming Density. The first search is a traditional gradient descent and the second is an efficient search using twisted theta functions. We hold other sources of lattice gain constant by fixing the lattice constellation, and consider basis changes that permute the integer labelings of the lattice points. After searching the possible basis matrices for $D_4$ and $E_8$, we found up to 0.09 dB of gain in $D_4$ bit error rate curves, and up to 0.36 dB of gain in $E_8$ compared to the standard bases commonly used in literature at a BER of $10^{-4}$, which is on the scale of gain from Gray coding uncoded QAMs.
papers.comments: 6 Pages, 5 Figures, and submitted to IEEE ICC 2027

papers.title: Variable decoupling and the Kolmogorov Superposition Theorem for rational functions
papers.abstract: The goal of this paper is to show that for rational multivariate functions, the Kolmogorov Superposition Theorem (KST) involves several univariate functions, which can be written down by inspection. In other words, no computation is required for decoupling the variables of multivariate rational functions. The key tool for this development is the Loewner Framework for multivariate functions. Applications of this result involve the approximation of multivariate non-rational functions by low-complexity multivariate rational and polynomial functions.

papers.title: Superintegrability in the interaction of two particles with spin: First-order pseudo-scalar integrals of motion
papers.abstract: In a recent work, we initiated a research program aimed at the systematic investigation of quantum superintegrable systems describing the interaction of two non-relativistic spin-$1/2$ particles in three-dimensional Euclidean space. In that study, we classified all such superintegrable systems admitting additional first-order scalar integrals of motion. In the present paper, we continue this program by focusing on systems that admit additional pseudo-scalar integrals of motion. Starting from the most general rotationally invariant Hamiltonian for two interacting spin-$1/2$ particles, we construct the most general pseudo-scalar operator of differential order at most one in the form of a matrix polynomial in the momenta. Imposing the commutativity of this operator with the Hamiltonian leads to a system of determining equations. By solving these equations, we obtain a complete classification of Hamiltonians in the considered class admitting additional pseudo-scalar integrals of differential order at most one, and determine these integrals explicitly. The resulting classification provides new families of spin-dependent Hamiltonians with additional pseudo-scalar symmetries. These systems enrich the class of integrable models relevant to nucleon--nucleon interactions and contribute to the broader program of classifying superintegrable quantum systems with spin. For selected cases, we further construct the associated polynomial symmetry algebras generated by the integrals of motion, providing additional insight into the algebraic structure of the systems.

papers.title: Minimax Optimal Estimation of Transport-Growth Pairs in Unbalanced Optimal Transport
papers.abstract: Unbalanced optimal transport extends classical optimal transport to measures with different total masses, but statistical guarantees for estimation of the transport map and the growth map remain limited. We study unbalanced optimal transport with quadratic cost and Kullback-Leibler marginal penalties and argue that the natural target of estimation is a transport-growth pair. Consequently, we develop two estimators for the transport-growth pair under two setups: a nearest-neighbor estimator for transporting between general densities, and a kernel-based estimator for transporting between smooth densities. We prove that the kernel-based estimator achieves the minimax optimal rate up to a logarithmic factor by deriving a matching lower bound on the minimax risk. Our main technical contribution is a reduction of estimation to a stability bound on the unbalanced optimal transport value. This bound controls the transport map and growth map risks through the duality gap of the true dual potentials for the estimated measures. These results provide a statistical foundation for estimation of the transport-growth pair in unbalanced optimal transport.

papers.title: Subperiodic groups and bounded automorphisms of periodic graphs
papers.abstract: A subperiodic group is a group of motions of $d$-dimensional Euclidean space $\mathbb R^d$ which contains a translation lattice $\mathbb Z^r$ of rank $r < d$ as a subgroup of finite index. Cayley graphs of subperiodic groups are used to illustrate the concept of bounded automorphisms (particularly of finite order), i.e. those when the distance between a graph vertex and its image has an upper bound. The description of subperiodic groups in dimension 3 in terms of subgroup structure and abstract group isomorphism types [75 crystallographic rod groups ($r=1$) and 80 layer groups ($r=2$) belong to 32 and 34 types, respectively] allows for a convenient characterization of bounded automorphisms of their Cayley graphs. An easy-to-compute set of invariants is developed for recognizing the isomorphism types of crystallographic groups in $\mathbb R^3$ from finite presentations which makes use of only the number of nonconjugate subgroups up to a given finite index $n$ ($n \leq 12$ for rod groups, $n \leq 8$ for layer groups, and $n \leq 24$ for space groups), and how many of them are normal. A criterion is proven that if a finite (inverse-closed) generating set of a group $G$ is stabilized by conjugation by a nontrivial element of finite order in $G$, then the respective Cayley graph possesses nontrivial bounded automorphisms of finite order. This criterion is applied to three-periodic sphere-packing graphs. Subperiodic groups in $\mathbb R^4$ with a three-dimensional translation lattice are used to systematically derive embeddings of three-periodic ladder graphs in $\mathbb R^3$.
papers.comments: 24 pages, 10 figures, 7 tables; Section 3.3 (a bit) extended, Section 4.1 revised and extended, Appendix A corrected, Fig. 5 improved, references added

papers.title: Computing Lower Bounds on the Nonnegative Rank via Non-Convex Optimization Solvers
papers.abstract: The nonnegative rank of a nonnegative matrix $X$ is the smallest number of nonnegative rank-one factors that sum to $X$. Since computing the nonnegative rank is NP-hard, it is common to circumvent this issue by computing lower and upper bounds. In this paper, we propose non-convex formulations and practical implementations for four important lower bounds for the nonnegative rank, namely the fooling set bound (FSB), the rectangle covering bound (RCB), the hyperplane separation bound (HSB), and the self-scaled bound (SSB). In particular, to the best of our knowledge, our algorithm for computing the SSB is the first available in the literature. We compute the SSB for several matrices for which its value had not previously been reported. In some cases, the SSB provides the best known upper bound, while the other three bounds do not. Moreover, on canonical benchmarks, we show that our non-convex approaches are often competitive with existing methods. The paper also provides a consolidated reference for the current state of several classical lower bounds on a large number of benchmark matrices.
papers.comments: Added a proof that the hyperplane separation bound equals 2 for the linear Euclidean distance matrices studied here. Improved the lower bound on the nonnegative rank of the slack matrix of the icosidodecahedron from 10 to 11. Clarified how the self-scaled bound recovers the known nonnegative rank of 7 for both M11 and M12

papers.title: Higher Rank-Support Weights and q-Polymatroids
papers.abstract: The aim of this paper is to develop a $(q,m)$-polymatroidal approach to higher supports and higher rank-weight enumerators of rank-metric codes. In this framework, we establish analogs of several fundamental results known for matroids and linear codes, including the description of minimal supports in terms of cocircuits of truncations and a Greene-type identity relating higher rank-weight enumerators to rank generating functions. We also show that the associated $(q,m)$-polymatroid and the higher support distributions determine each other. As a further application, we derive MacWilliams-type identities for higher rank-weight enumerators.

papers.title: Maximum Probability of Independence in Transitive Matroids
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a matroid on a finite ground set $E$, and suppose that the automorphism group of $M$ acts transitively on $E$. We show the following: if $X_1,\ldots,X_K$ are sampled independently from a distribution $p$ on $E$, then the probability that the samples are distinct and that $\{X_1,\ldots,X_K\}$ is an independent set in $M$ is quasi-concave in $p$ and maximized when $p$ is uniform. For $2\le K\le\rank(M)$, we characterize all maximizers by uniform total mass on the parallel classes and, in particular, show that the maximizer is unique and has global quadratic stability when $M$ is simple. As a corollary, for a random $K\times N$ matrix over a finite field with i.i.d.\ rows, uniform sampling from the nonzero vectors maximizes the probability of full row rank. Finally, we show that uniform sampling maximizes $\Prob\big(\rank_M(X_1,\ldots,X_L)\ge r\big)$, and hence also $\E\rank_M(X_1,\ldots,X_L)$, for every $L, r$.

papers.title: Stacky geometry and logarithmic topology of transversely affine foliations
papers.abstract: We study the linear monodromy of codimension-one transversely affine foliations through multiplicative quotient stacks and logarithmic boundary topology. When the transverse affine structure admits a global presentation on $U$, a choice of multiplicative developing coordinate induces a morphism to $[\mathbb{C}^*/Γ]$, where $Γ\subset\mathbb{C}^*$ is the image of the linear monodromy. We prove that for infinite $Γ$ every strict semi-equivariant holomorphic self-map of $\mathbb{C}^*$ is a monomial, and classify the nonconstant strict semi-equivariant rational self-maps of $\mathbb{P}^1$ for arbitrary $Γ$. For a logarithmic connection along a simple normal crossings divisor, we describe the meridional characters and angular foliations on the boundary fibres of the Kato--Nakayama space, including the topology and closures of their leaves. We also describe the extension of the linear monodromy local system to this space and the effect of local Kummer base change on finite meridional monodromy.

papers.title: Spectral inequalities for weighted $p$-Laplacians via Talenti symmetrization
papers.abstract: We consider the weighted $p$-Laplacian associated with a measure $μ$ having a continuous positive density with respect to the Lebesgue measure on an open convex subset $X\subset\mathbb{R}^N$. We prove that Talenti's weighted Pólya--Szegő inequality---originally established for Lipschitz functions on $X$---extends to the weighted Sobolev space of functions vanishing on the relative boundary of an open set $Ω\subset X$, defined as the closure of Lipschitz functions supported away from it. This yields Faber--Krahn-type inequalities for the first $(p,q)$-eigenvalue of the weighted Dirichlet $p$-Laplacian. We present several examples fitting this abstract framework, in which the isoperimetric sets are balls, half-spaces, or complements of balls.

papers.title: Inequivalence of the various notions of completeness for Cartan geometries
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that the three standard notions of completeness for Cartan geometries are not actually equivalent, modernizing and extending results due to Yeaton Clifton. In an effort to rectify the folklore on the topic, we also provide detailed explanations of how specious proofs in the literature that would claim that these types of completeness are equivalent break down. In the affine case, we construct geodesically complete homogeneous examples with an inextensible exponential curve for each connected Lie group of dimension at least 2, as well as an infinite-dimensional family of examples whose exponential curves are defined for all time but whose overlying frame bundle is not complete as a metric space with respect to a natural metric for the Cartan connection.

papers.title: Ferrofluids: Modeling and Approximation
papers.abstract: Starting from Maxwell's and linear momentum balance equations, we derive a ferrofluid model using the generalized Onsager's principle. Guided by a discrete perturbation estimate, we design and analyze families of Galerkin schemes that converge to sufficiently regular solutions and derive error estimates. Finally, we numerically explore the model with our proposed method.
papers.comments: 27 pages, 3 figures. v2: We incorporated the anonymous referee's suggestions and corrected previously unidentified typos and minor mistakes

papers.title: A Noetherian Hopf algebra is affine iff its Hopf coradical is affine
papers.abstract: Let $\K$ be an arbitrary field. Extending the structural frameworks established in \cite{JZ2025-2}, this paper introduces novel techniques utilizing mirror reduction orders, prime words, and the generalized lifting methodology. We establish a definitive necessary and sufficient criterion for the affineness of Noetherian Hopf algebras, thereby providing a significant advancement toward resolving the long-standing Wu--Zhang question \cite{WZ2003}. Specifically, we prove that a left or right Noetherian Hopf algebra over $\K$ is affine if and only if its Hopf coradical is affine. This characterization fundamentally reduces the verification to the first filtration step, yielding a criterion that is structurally transparent and highly operational. To establish necessity, we provide an essential intrinsic result demonstrating that the Hopf coradical of an affine Hopf algebra inherits the property of being affine. Furthermore, as direct applications of this equivalence, we prove that a left or right Noetherian Hopf algebra $H$ is affine provided that its coradical $H_{(0)}$ forms a subalgebra (the dual Chevalley property), its coradical $H_{(0)}$ is cocommutative, or its Hopf coradical $H_{[0]}$ is commutative.
papers.comments: 33 pages. v3: Theorem 6.3 strengthened (redundant assumption removed); the proof of Theorem 6.5 streamlined; minor editorial revisions

papers.title: Asymptotic Theory for Sample Canonical Direction Alignment in High-Dimensional Spiked CCA
papers.abstract: This paper studies the asymptotic behavior of sample canonical directions in a finite-rank spiked high-dimensional canonical correlation analysis model under a Gaussian population assumption. Under the asymptotic regime in which the dimensions of the two data blocks grow proportionally with the sample size, sample canonical directions are generally not consistent estimators of their population counterparts, even when the corresponding sample canonical correlations separate from the bulk spectrum. To quantify directional recovery, we investigate the squared alignment between a sample canonical direction and its associated population direction. For a supercritical simple population spike, we establish an explicit nonzero deterministic limit for the squared alignment. In contrast, for population non-spikes, we show that the alignment with the corresponding population signal directions vanishes asymptotically. Thus, the same phase transition that governs eigenvalue separation also marks a transition in directional recovery. For a supercritical simple spike, we further prove a central limit theorem for its fluctuations around the deterministic limit, with an explicit asymptotic variance expressed through deterministic limits of resolvent trace functionals. To make the theoretical quantities computable from data, we further construct plug-in estimators for both the deterministic alignment limit and the asymptotic variance by inverting the deterministic outlier eigenvalue map, and prove their consistency. Numerical simulations and a real-data illustration support the theoretical results and demonstrate how the proposed estimators assess the recovery quality of sample canonical directions.
papers.comments: Added the subcritical alignment result, refined the central limit theorem and its asymptotic variance, and improved the proofs and presentation

papers.title: The inradius law for the cavities of planar Brownian motion, with applications to the Wiener sausage
papers.abstract: ```text Let $K_1=B[0,1]$ be the trace of a planar Brownian motion, and let $N_{\mathrm{in}}(η)$ be the number of its cavities, the bounded components of $\mathbb{R}^2\setminus K_1$, whose inradius exceeds $η$. We prove that, almost surely and in $L^p$ for every $p\in[1,2]$, $η^2(\log(1/η))^2 N_{\mathrm{in}}(η)\to c_{\mathrm{in}}=\fracπ{2}\int G^2 d\mathcal{L}\in(0,\frac12]$, where $G$ is the ratio of the inradius of a shape to the square root of its area and $\mathcal{L}$ is Werner's limiting shape law. The inradius, and not the area by which the cavities have been counted classically, decides survival under thickening: a cavity contains a hole of the Wiener sausage of radius $r$ if and only if its inradius exceeds $r$. Through Brownian scaling, the number $β_1^T(r)$ of holes of the sausage of radius $r$ of $B[0,T]$, the Betti curve of its degree-one persistent homology, is bounded below at the scale $T/(r^2(\log T)^2)$, with the identified constant $4c_{\mathrm{in}}$ in expectation and with any smaller constant with probability tending to one. A matching upper bound cannot follow from any general bound in terms of perimeter, area, diameter or length; we prove that it is equivalent to a first-moment estimate for near-critical pockets, the holes at level $η$ on which the distance to the trace is at most $2η$. That estimate is proved in a companion paper, so that the expected number of holes is of exact order $T/(r^2(\log T)^2)$. ```
papers.comments: v3: revised; the upper bound is now reduced to a first-moment estimate proved in a companion paper

papers.title: Resolution of Vinzant's Conjecture on Phase Retrieval Injectivity
papers.abstract: Let $A\in\mathbb C^{N\times M}$ with $N=4M-5$ has independent standard complex Gaussian entries. We prove that the probability that the phase retrieval map generated by $A$ is injective is strictly smaller than $1$, and is $O(M^{-1})$ as $M\to \infty$. This proves a conjecture of Cynthia Vinzant, which was later restated by Afonso S. Bandeira in \cite{bandeira2026randomstrasse101}. The main result of this paper was obtained using generative AI, in particular GPT6-Astra, GPT 5.6-sol, and the Rethlas system.

papers.title: List coloring uncrowded hypergraphs at the shattering threshold
papers.abstract: A foundational theorem of Ajtai, Komlós, Pintz, Spencer, and Szemerédi asserts that every $n$-vertex $k$-uniform uncrowded hypergraph (i.e., with girth at least $5$) of maximum degree at most $Δ$ contains an independent set of size $cn(\logΔ/Δ)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}$ for some absolute constant $c>0$. Improving an earlier bound of Frieze and Mubayi, Iliopoulos showed that every such hypergraph has list chromatic number at most $(1+o(1))(k-1)(Δ/\logΔ)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}$. Determining the optimal leading constant in this bound remains a major open problem. A natural target, suggested by the coupon-collector heuristic, is $(k-1)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}$, which also corresponds to the shattering threshold for coloring sparse random hypergraphs. Our main result shows that this target is attained: for every integer $k\ge2$, every $k$-uniform uncrowded hypergraph of maximum degree at most $Δ$ satisfies: $$χ_\ell(\mathcal{H})\le(1+o(1))\Big((k-1)\fracΔ{\logΔ}\Big)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}.$$ In particular, this confirms a 2019 conjecture of Molloy for uncrowded hypergraphs. Building on this result, we prove that every $k$-uniform linear hypergraph of maximum degree at most $Δ$ has chromatic number at most $(c_k+o(1))(Δ/\logΔ)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}$, where $c_k\to1$ as $k\to\infty$, thereby proving a conjecture of Verstraëte and Wilson on the independence number of linear hypergraphs in the stronger form of colorings. Our techniques also yield a palette sparsification theorem for uncrowded hypergraphs, partially answering a question of Casselgren and Eriksson.

papers.title: Well-posedness of the weakly singular Burton-Miller equation for Helmholtz transmission problems
papers.abstract: Although various boundary integral formulations are available for the Helmholtz transmission problem, the weakly singular Burton--Miller equation is promising because it possesses favorable properties for numerical computation. This paper rigorously shows that the weakly singular Burton--Miller equation is well-posed. We establish bounded invertibility on $C(Γ)\times C(Γ)$ for $C^2$ boundaries by proving injectivity and applying the Fredholm alternative. For the prescribed analytic incident field, the integral equation further yields $u\in C^{1,β}(Γ)$ and $q\in C^{0,β}(Γ)$, for $0<β<1$. We also provide a proof that its fictitious eigenvalues are associated with an exterior Dirichlet problem and an interior impedance problem.

papers.title: The $M/M_D/c$ queue with dependent servers: A canonical Markovian extension of $M/M/c$
papers.abstract: The classical $M/M/c$ queue is the canonical Markovian model for a single-node queue with Poisson arrivals and homogeneous independent servers. We identify its natural counterpart when the servers are dependent. For homogeneous Markovian labelled service-completion mechanisms (retaining the identities of the completing servers), consistency under restriction to subsets of busy servers is equivalent to an independent Poisson shock representation, yielding homogeneous Marshall--Olkin multivariate exponential residual-service laws. This characterization identifies the $M/M_D/c$ queue as the canonical Markovian extension of $M/M/c$ to dependent homogeneous servers, with a Markovian queue-length process. For heterogeneous servers, augmenting boundary states with busy-server identities yields a Markovian queue-state process, as in the classical independent-server setting. For arbitrary $c$ and fixed idle-set assignment, we derive an explicit matrix-analytic stationary solution and departure and customer-delay laws. Waiting time conditional on delay is exponential, and the stationary sojourn distribution has a phase-type representation with at most $c+1$ phases. A three-server comparison with identical bivariate residual-service laws demonstrates how higher-order dependence can change waiting-time behavior.

papers.title: The parental parsimony problem on binary, tree-child phylogenetic networks
papers.abstract: Phylogenetic reconstruction is one of the major challenges in computational biology. Among existing reconstruction methods for phylogenetic networks, an important subtask emerges in extending a leaf-labelling on a phylogenetic network to determine a most parsimonious tree inside the network. There exist different variants of this subtask depending on the biological model assumptions for which distinct evolutionary phenomena are captured by the network. In this article we assume that next to hybridization or recombination events, also allopolyploidy or incomplete lineage sorting are present. Then, finding the most parsimonious tree inside the network is called the parental parsimony score problem (PPS), a NP-hard combinatorial optimization problem. We provide the first constant-factor approximation for the PPS on arbitrary but fixed leaf labels and a class of networks on which the PPS remains NP-hard, namely binary, semi-simplex, tree-child phylogenetic networks. Furthermore, we introduce a novel exact solution algorithm for the PPS on binary, tree-child phylogenetic networks and analyze its performance on simulated data.

papers.title: Plancherel Identities for unbounded subsets of $\mathbb R^d$
papers.abstract: We investigate spectral pairs associated with unbounded subsets of $\mathbb R^d$ that are periodic with respect to full-rank lattices. We establish a characterization of such spectral pairs in terms of the spectrality of an associated bounded fundamental component. More precisely, we prove that the Fourier transform defines an isometric isomorphism onto an $L^2$ space with an explicitly determined absolutely continuous pair measure, supported on a union of translates of a dual-lattice fundamental domain, if and only if the bounded component admits an orthogonal basis of exponential functions with frequencies in the dual lattice. In particular, the Plancherel identity alone is sufficient to characterize these spectral pairs. As an application, when the bounded component tiles $\br^d$ by a lattice, we obtain an equivalence between certain translational tiling properties of unbounded periodic sets and the existence of the corresponding Plancherel identities. We also examine periodicity properties of sets that tile by finite translation sets, highlighting distinctions between the one-dimensional and higher-dimensional settings.

papers.title: A Trichotomy for Modified Scattering Across the Yukawa-Coulomb Transition
papers.abstract: We study the long-time asymptotics of the three-dimensional Hartree equation with Yukawa potential \[ V_μ(x)=\frac{e^{-μ|x|}}{|x|}, \qquad 0\leqμ\leq1. \] The Coulomb case corresponds to $μ=0$, while $μ>0$ introduces the screening length $μ^{-1}$. In the limit $μ\to0$ and $t\to\infty$, the asymptotic behavior depends on the comparison between the observation scale $t$ and the screening length $μ^{-1}$, equivalently on the parameter $μt$. This leads to three distinct asymptotic regimes, according as $μt\to0$, $μt\to L\in(0,\infty)$, or $μt\to\infty$, with different modified scattering phases in each case.
papers.comments: Corrected minor errors, simplified the notation and organization

papers.title: Existence of the Lyapunov exponent for $S$-unimodal maps
papers.abstract: In this paper, we show that for any $S$-unimodal map $T$ on $[0,1]$ with a non-flat critical point the Lyapunov exponent exists for Lebesgue almost every point and is equal to a constant $λ_T$. Moreover, $λ_T=0$ if and only if $T$ admits neither an absolutely continuous $T$-invariant probability measure with positive entropy nor a strictly stable periodic orbit. Consequently, if an $S$-unimodal map with a non-flat critical point is infinitely renormalizable or non-statistical then for Lebesgue almost every $x\in [0,1]$ the Lyapunov exponent along the orbit of $x$ exists and is equal to $0$. A key ingredient is the following result of independent interest. If an $S$-unimodal map with a non-flat critical point has no periodic attractor then for Lebesgue almost every $x\in [0,1]$ the lower Lyapunov exponent along the orbit of $x$ is non-negative. This shows that, in the absence of periodic attractors, exponential contraction cannot occur along the orbit of Lebesgue almost every point.

papers.title: Trefftz DG Approximation of the T-Matrix for Scattering by Periodic Layered Structures
papers.abstract: We study the scattering of time-harmonic electromagnetic waves by periodic layered gratings, modelled by the 2D Helmholtz equation. The periodic obstacle may include penetrable and impenetrable regions, and consists of a finite number of stacked layers. The boundary value problem is formulated on a single periodic cell using quasi-periodic boundary conditions. The radiation condition in the vertical directions is imposed through Dirichlet-to-Neumann (DtN) operators. To efficiently treat multilayer configurations, we adopt a formulation based on the T-matrix method. The global scattering problem is decomposed into boundary value problems posed on individual layers. On the layer boundaries, the field is expressed in terms of quasi-periodic modal expansions, and the layer T-matrix describes the map between incoming and outgoing wave modes. Each local T-matrix is approximated numerically using a plane-wave based Trefftz Discontinuous Galerkin (TDG) method, which provides an efficient discretization of the layer scattering response. The T-matrix technique leads to linear computational complexity in the number of layers in the grating.

papers.title: Spectral Characterisation of Covariance Existence in Markov-Switching Affine Recurrences
papers.abstract: This paper provides a finite-dimensional spectral characterisation of covariance existence for finite-state Markov-switching affine recurrences of the form \[ Z_{n+1}=A_{Θ_{n+1}}Z_n+ζ_{n+1}. \] While strict stationarity is typically governed by negativity of the top Lyapunov exponent of the random matrix products, this does not ensure finite variances, covariances, or Pearson correlations. We show that these second-order properties are governed instead by a Markov-switching Kronecker operator. Writing \(T_{ji}:=p_{ij}(A_j\otimes A_j)\) and denoting its spectral radius by \(ρ(T)\), we prove that, under a natural Perron-excitation condition on the innovation covariance, \(ρ(T)<1\) is necessary and sufficient for the stationary solution to be square-integrable. When this condition holds, the regime-weighted second moments solve a finite-dimensional linear system, yielding the covariance matrix explicitly. Thus, the mean-square spectral condition becomes an exact covariance-existence criterion for the stationary law. Examples illustrate the separation: the top Lyapunov exponent may be negative while the second-order spectral radius exceeds one, so strict stationarity can persist even when finite second moments, and hence population covariances and Pearson correlations, do not exist.

papers.title: The quantum double of the restricted quantum group $\mathbf{\overline{u}}_q(\mathfrak{sl_2})$
papers.abstract: In this paper, we construct the quantum double $D(\mathbf{\overline{u}}_q(\mathfrak{sl_2}))$ of the restricted quantum group $\mathbf{\overline{u}}_q(\mathfrak{sl_2})$. We describe the algebraic structure of $D(\mathbf{\overline{u}}_q(\mathfrak{sl_2}))$ by generators and relations. Moreover, we give the comultiplication $Δ$, the counit $\varepsilon$ and the antipode $S$, respectively. Finally, we classify all irreducible representations of $D(\mathbf{\overline{u}}_q(\mathfrak{sl_2}))$ when $p=2$.
papers.comments: This work will be incorporated into anther manscript, so this preprint is withdrawn

papers.title: Compact Coefficient Formulae for Logarithmic Tangent and Hyperbolic Integrals
papers.abstract: We develop compact coefficient-extraction formulae for several families of hyperbolic, logarithmic tangent, and Malmsten-type integrals whose values are finite linear combinations of odd zeta values and even Dirichlet beta values. The principal advantage of these formulae is that coefficients previously encoded by recursive arrays or nested finite sums are replaced by a single coefficient of an explicit elementary expression. This makes the coefficients easier to compute, keeps the dependence on the parameters visible, and reveals structural features---such as vanishing ranges, extremal coefficients, and sign patterns---without hidden cancellations. For shifted hyperbolic integrals with numerator $\sinh((2k+1)x)$, the coefficients are expressed through Chebyshev--arcsine extractions. The same mechanism yields Laurent coefficient formulae for logarithmic tangent integrals and leads to direct proofs of simple initial and terminal coefficients, including a parity-free terminal identity. For $m,n\geq1$, $m\geq n$, and $m+n$ even, we prove \[ \int_0^\infty\frac{\tanh^{m+1}x}{x^{n+1}}\,dx = (-1)^{(m-n)/2} \sum_{p=\lceil n/2\rceil}^{(m+n)/2} \binom{2p}{n} (2^{2p+1}-1) \frac{ζ(2p+1)}{π^{2p}} [u^{m+n-2p}](u\cot u)^{m+1}. \] \[\int_0^\infty \frac{\tanh^m x}{x^n\cosh x}\,dx = (-1)^{(m-n)/2} \sum_{p=\lceil n/2\rceil}^{(m+n)/2} 2^{2p}\binom{2p-1}{n-1} \frac{β(2p)}{π^{2p-1}} [u^{m+n-2p}] \frac{u}{\sin u}(u\cot u)^m \] In the diagonal zeta case, the formula gives the family $\int_0^\infty(\tanh x/x)^N\,dx$ in a direct, non-recursive form and makes the disappearance of the initial zeta values immediate.

papers.title: Standard modules and Dold--Kan correspondences for generalized Reedy categories
papers.abstract: We develop a representation-theoretic approach to generalized Reedy categories through a systematic study of standard modules. For a broad class of these categories, we provide a uniform, computable framework that reduces abstract Hom-spaces between standard modules to elementary linear algebra and graph theory via incidence matrices and morphism fibers. As a primary application, we establish a uniform extension of the Dold--Kan correspondence for certain categories arising from rooted trees, and obtain an orthogonal decomposition for finite spiders, including the category of finite sets and partial injections. Crucially, this machinery unifies and provides a single conceptual framework for several classical, seemingly disparate results across algebraic topology and representation theory, including Kuhn's decomposition theorem for vector spaces and the Thévenaz--Webb semisimplicity theorem for Mackey functors.
papers.comments: Techinical issues and small errors fixed

papers.title: Skeletal Homology
papers.abstract: By ``skeletal homology'' $K_{n}^{\varepsilon}(X)$ we mean the homology of the chain complex $S_{n}^{\varepsilon}(X)$ generated by skeletal $(n,\varepsilon )$-simplices, i.e.\ maps from the $0$-skeleton of the standard simplex into a metric space $X$ whose image has diameter less than $\varepsilon$. Goldfarb showed for finite metric spaces that this homology is isomorphic to the simplicial homology $H_{n}^Δ(VR_{\varepsilon}(X))$ of the Vietoris--Rips complex. We give a new proof of this isomorphism for arbitrary metric spaces. We then develop a metric analogue of methods from singular homology by replacing the topological notion of ``homotopic'' with the metric notion of ``close''. The key tool is a discrete prism construction, which shows that uniformly close functions with a common modulus of continuity induce the same homomorphism on skeletal homology. This leads to stability results for $K_{n}^{\varepsilon}(X)\cong H_{n}^Δ(VR_{\varepsilon}(X))$, including broad extensions of the theorems of Hausmann and Latschev beyond the setting of Riemannian manifolds. Finally, repeated barycentric subdivision and restriction induce a natural homomorphism $ρ_{\varepsilon}:H_{n}% (X)\longrightarrow K_{n}^{\varepsilon}(X). $ We call its image the \emph{real homology} $H_{n}^{\varepsilon}(X)$ at scale and define the corresponding \emph{phantom homology} $P_{n}^{\varepsilon}(X) = K_{n}^{\varepsilon}% (X)/H_{n}^{\varepsilon}(X). $ We show that phantom homology can detect impending topological collapse, as illustrated by collapsing Riemannian manifolds such as Berger spheres.

papers.title: Data informativity for feedback rectification of switched linear systems
papers.abstract: For switched linear systems, we leverage the concept of data informativity for data-driven feedback rectification to design a stabilizing controller. The established rectified eigenstructure means that all closed-loop subsystems share a common set of eigenvectors and enables us to compute a common quadratic Lyapunov function to ensure global uniform exponential stability of the closed-loop system. The proposed methodology is illustrated for two examples including a model of an unmanned aerial vehicle.

papers.title: Sonic-supersonic jet flows from a straight two-dimensional nozzle with van der Waals equation of state
papers.abstract: This article concerns sonic-supersonic jet flows issuing from a two-dimensional straight nozzle described by the steady compressible Euler system under the van der Waals equation of state. The flow state is prescribed at the nozzle exit, while the surrounding medium is assumed to be either a vacuum or a static atmosphere with lower pressure. When the flow reaches the sonic state at the nozzle exit, the governing equations become degenerate hyperbolic and the resulting jet flow problem can be formulated as a degenerate free boundary problem. The analysis is further complicated by singular behavior near the endpoints of the nozzle exit. By employing characteristic decompositions and suitable a priori estimates, we establish the global existence of locally Lipschitz continuous sonic-supersonic jet flows expanding into a vacuum. Moreover, in the presence of a static atmosphere with pressure lower than that at the nozzle exit, we prove the local existence of sonic-supersonic jet flows near the nozzle exit.

papers.title: Tiling a triangle into a prime number of congruent triangles
papers.abstract: We prove that if a triangle is cut into $N$ congruent triangles and $N$ is prime, then $N=2$, $N=3$, or $N\equiv 1 \pmod 4$, and every such $N$ occurs. In particular, if $N > 3$ then $N$ is not a prime congruent to $3$ modulo $4$. All the proofs in this paper have been formalized in Lean. The argument divides into cases according to possible shapes of the tiled triangle. Let $α,β,γ$ be the angles of the tile. Prior to this posting, there remained several open shapes. The two most difficult shapes were $(2α,β,α+β)$, the {\em triquadratic} shape, and $(β,β,3α)$, the {\em isosceles-$β$} shape, in which $3α+2β= π$ and $α$ is not a rational multiple of $π$. A previous version of this paper relied on incorrect proofs of those cases, which have been retracted, and are replaced here by correct proofs. For each of those two shapes the number of tiles has the form $N = j^2 N_0$, where $N_0 > 1$ is determined by the shape of the tile and $j$ is a positive integer; so $N$ is prime, or even squarefree, only if $j = 1$. We prove by geometric reasoning that neither shape admits a tiling with $j = 1$, which shows that for both shapes $N$ is never prime, and indeed never squarefree. The shape $(β,β,3α+β)$ (where $3α+ 3β= π$) has been settled by Bonfioli. In this paper, we settle the remaining cases, by number-theoretic arguments based on the area equation. Those proofs rule out $N$ prime, but not $N$ squarefree, and we give examples to show that tilings with squarefree $N$ do sometimes exist.
papers.comments: 40 pages, ten figures. This version is essentially the same as the previous version, except that all proofs have been verified in Lean, and a pointer is given to the Lean repository with an index to the theorem names

papers.title: Fixed-time stabilization of systems with nilpotent matrices in the presence of large unknown delays
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study state-feedback fixed-time stabilization of continuous-time perturbed linear systems with nilpotent matrices in the presence of unknown large constant input/measurement delays with known bounds.
